children.translated_text: Ḍhuṇḍhukanātha: Rasendracintāmaṇi

children.text:
RCint, 1
he bhasmāṅgaviraktirūpaguṇadaṃ taṃ preraṇādaṃ śivaṃ gaṅgābhūṣitaśekharaṃ smaraharaṃ śaktisvarūpaṃ prabho /
tvāmīśaṃ karuṇārṇavaṃ śaraṇadaṃ vidyānidhiṃ nirguṇaṃ bhūteśaṃ girijāpatiṃ śaśidharaṃ māṅgalyadevaṃ namaḥ /
namāmi devaṃ suravṛndapūjitaṃ gaṇādhipaṃ vighnavināśakārakam /
smaranti ye nityam udāracetasaḥ kaṣṭāni te nānubhavanti satyam /
children.translated_text: those noble-minded ones who remember him constantly do not truly experience sufferings.
<s>Siddhinandanamiśra</s> [composed] this pure and essence-laden
commentary on the <s>Rasendracintāmaṇi</s>, which I compose by the command of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: idānīṃ kālanāthaśiṣyaḥ śrīḍhuṇḍhukanāthāhvayo rasendracintāmaṇigrantham ārabhamāṇas tanmūladevate śrīmadambikāmaheśvarau sakalajagadutpattisthitipralayanidānaṃ viśeṣasiddhāntagarbhavācā varīvasyati // RCint_1.1 //
children.translated_text: Now, the disciple of <s>Kālanātha</s>, called <s>Śrī Ḍhuṇḍhukanātha</s>, commencing the treatise <s>Rasendracintāmaṇi</s>, praises the root deities, the glorious <s>Ambikā</s> and <s>Maheśvara</s>, who are the cause of the creation, sustenance, and dissolution of the entire universe, with words pregnant with special doctrinal meaning. // RCint_1.1 //

RCint, 1
O Lord, whose body is adorned with ashes, who bestows detachment, form, and virtue, who is the giver of inspiration, the auspicious <s>Śiva</s>, whose crest is adorned with <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the destroyer of <s>Smara</s> (Kāmadeva), whose nature is <s>Śakti</s> itself,
to You, <s>Īśa</s>, the ocean of compassion, the giver of refuge, the treasure of knowledge, the attributeless one, the Lord of beings, the husband of <s>Girijā</s>, the bearer of the moon, the auspicious deity — salutations!
I bow to the deity worshipped by the host of gods, the lord of the <s>Gaṇas</s>, the destroyer of obstacles,
The form of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, which is a lotus-pool of illuminating commentary rich in meaning,
resplendent with <s>saccidānanda</s> (existence-consciousness-bliss) — I take refuge in that form. // RCint_1.2 //
Like a <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem), this <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> [text] bestows complete knowledge of mercury despite its small size. // RCint_1.3 //

children.text: aśrauṣaṃ bahuviduṣāṃ mukhād apaśyaṃ śāstreṣu sthitam akṛtaṃ na tallikhāmi /
children.translated_text: What I heard from the mouths of many learned ones, what I saw established in the treatises — what was not done, I do not write about;

children.text: yatkarma vyaracayamagrato gurūṇāṃ prauḍhānāṃ tadiha vadāmi vītaśaṅkaḥ // RCint_1.4 //
children.translated_text: the work that I performed before my teachers, the accomplished ones — that I declare here without hesitation. // RCint_1.4 //

children.text: adhyāpayanti yad darśayituṃ kṣamante sūtendrakarma guravo guravasta eva /
children.translated_text: Those teachers are true teachers who teach and are able to demonstrate the work of <s>Sūtendra</s> (mercury);

children.text: śiṣyāsta eva racayanti guroḥpuro ye śeṣāḥ punastadubhayābhinayaṃ bhajante // RCint_1.5 //
children.translated_text: those are true students who perform it before the teacher; the rest merely imitate both activities. // RCint_1.5 //
The processes that are hidden in other texts, indicated by successful practitioners,

children.text: tāneva prakaṭīkartum udyamaṃ kila kurmahe // RCint_1.6 //
children.translated_text: we indeed undertake to make them manifest. // RCint_1.6 //

children.text: granthād asmādāharanti prayogān svīyaṃ vāsminnāma ye nikṣipanti /
children.translated_text: Those who extract procedures from this treatise or place their own name upon it,
may the heat of our labor reduce their lineages to ashes for an entire age! // RCint_1.7 //

children.text: saṃskārāḥ śivajanuṣo bahuprakārās tulyā ye laghubahulaprayāsaṃsādhyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The processes for the birth of <s>Śiva</s> (transforming mercury) are of many kinds, some equal, some achievable with little or great effort;

children.text: yadyekaṃ sukaram udāharāmi teṣāṃ vyāhāraiḥ kimihaphalaṃ tataḥ pareṣām // RCint_1.8 //
children.translated_text: if I present one easy method among them, what is the use of verbose descriptions of the others? // RCint_1.8 //

children.text: iha khalu puruṣeṇa duḥkhasya nirupādhidveṣaviṣayatvāt tadabhāvaścikīrṣitavyo bhavati sukhamapi nirupādhipremāspadatayā gaveṣaṇīyam tadetatpuruṣārthadvayam /
children.translated_text: Here indeed, since suffering is the object of unconditional aversion for a person, its removal must be sought; likewise happiness, being the object of unconditional love, must be pursued — these two constitute the <s>puruṣārtha</s> (human aims),
because of the otherness of absence. // RCint_1.9 //

children.text: kiṃca srakcandanavanitādiviṣayāṇāṃ satyapi tatkāraṇatve nāntarīyakaduḥkhasambhedād anarthaparamparāparicitatvān mūrkhāṇāṃ kośāṇḍakavad ābhāsamānatvād anaikāntikatvād virodhināṃ yugapadadṛśyamānatvād atyantatāvirahitatvācca pariharaṇīyatvam // RCint_1.10 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, even though garlands, sandalwood, butter and such objects may cause pleasure, because they are not free from attendant suffering, because they lead to chains of misfortune, because like a silkworm's cocoon they are merely apparent to the foolish, because they are uncertain, because contradictory experiences occur simultaneously, and because they lack absolute permanence — they are to be rejected. // RCint_1.10 //

children.text: ekāntātyantataśca punaste hyupāyāḥ khalu hariharabrahmāṇa iva tulyā eva sambhavanti /
children.translated_text: And those means which are absolutely and permanently effective — they indeed arise as equal, like <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s>;
they are: <s>jñānayoga</s> (the yoga of knowledge), <s>pavanayoga</s> (the yoga of breath), and <s>rasayoga</s> (the yoga of mercury). // RCint_1.11 //

children.text:
nanu kathameṣāṃ tulyatetyapekṣāyāṃ brūmaḥ mokṣopāye bṛhadvāsiṣṭhādau bhuśuṇḍopākhyāne vasiṣṭhavākyam /
asādhyaḥ kasyacidyogaḥ kasyacijjñānaniścayaḥ /
dvau prakārau tato devo jagāda paramaḥ śivaḥ /
children.translated_text: therefore the supreme Lord <s>Śiva</s> taught two methods:
either by the restraint of the vital breaths, or by the driving away of latent impressions;
if you do not raise the consciousness of the exalted ones, then you are not a practitioner of yoga;

children.text: dvāveva hi samau rāma jñānayogāvimau smṛtau // RCint_1.12 //
children.translated_text: these two, <s>jñānayoga</s> and [prāṇa]yoga, are regarded as equal, O <s>Rāma</s>." // RCint_1.12 //

Now, when asked how these are equal, we say: regarding the means of liberation, in the <s>Bṛhadvāsiṣṭha</s> and elsewhere, in the <s>Bhuśuṇḍa</s> episode, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s words are:
"For some, yoga is impossible; for others, firm knowledge is unattainable;

children.text: tatrādyayoḥ kevalaṃ pakvakaṣāyāṇāmapi kathañcana sādhyatvāccarame tu punarbhogalolupānām apyadhikāritvāttābhyāṃ samīcīno'yamiti kasya na pratibhāti // RCint_1.13 //
children.translated_text: Of those, the first two are somehow attainable even by those whose afflictions are ripened, but the last (<s>rasayoga</s>) is accessible even to those addicted to sensual pleasures — who would not recognize that this is superior to those two? // RCint_1.13 //

children.text: kiṃca asya bhagavanniryāsatayā sevakānāṃ svasambhūtasakaladhātutvāpādakasya bhagavato rasarājasya guṇasindhoḥ kiyantaḥ pṛṣatāḥ prasaṅgāllikhyante // RCint_1.14 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, of this blessed Lord <s>Rasarāja</s> (King of Mercury), who is the divine exudation and who transforms all bodily constituents into his own nature — how many drops of his ocean of virtues can be written here in passing? // RCint_1.14 //
"In a short time, O <s>Devī</s>, a body free from old age and death is born,
and steadiness of mind is attained through <s>rasayoga</s> (mercury-yoga). // RCint_1.15 //

children.text: sattvaṃ ca labhate devi vijñānaṃ jñānapūrvakam /
children.translated_text: One obtains <s>sattva</s> (purity), O <s>Devī</s>, and knowledge preceded by wisdom;

children.text: satyaṃ mantrāśca sidhyanti yo'śnāti mṛtasūtakam // RCint_1.16 //
children.translated_text: truly, mantras become efficacious for one who consumes the killed mercury. // RCint_1.16 //
As long as there is no descent of <s>Śakti</s>, as long as the bonds are not severed,
how can the purification of killed mercury arise for such a person? // RCint_1.17 //
As long as one does not consume mercury, the seed of <s>Hara</s>,

children.text: tāvattasya kuto muktiḥ kutaḥ piṇḍasya dhāraṇam // RCint_1.18 //
children.translated_text: how can there be liberation for such a person, or preservation of the body? // RCint_1.18 //

children.text: svadehe khecaratvaṃ vai śivatvaṃ yena labhyate /
children.translated_text: That by which one attains the state of moving through the sky and the state of <s>Śiva</s> in one's own body,

children.text: tādṛśe tu rasajñāne nityābhyāsaṃ kuru priye // RCint_1.19 //
children.translated_text: in such knowledge of mercury, practice constantly, O beloved! // RCint_1.19 //

children.text: tvaṃ mātā sarvabhūtānāṃ pitā cāhaṃ sanātanaḥ /
children.translated_text: You are the mother of all beings, and I am the eternal father;

children.text: dvayośca yo raso devi mahāmaithunasambhavaḥ // RCint_1.20 //
children.translated_text: and the mercury born from the great union of both of us, O <s>Devī</s>, // RCint_1.20 //
by seeing it, by touching it, by consuming it, by its destruction, O beloved,
by worshipping it, and by giving mercury — a sixfold fruit is seen. // RCint_1.21 //
Whatever <s>liṅgas</s> there are on earth, such as <s>Kedāra</s> and others,

children.text: tāni dṛṣṭvā ca yatpuṇyaṃ tatpuṇyaṃ rasadarśanāt // RCint_1.22 //
children.translated_text: the merit obtained by seeing them — that same merit comes from seeing mercury. // RCint_1.22 //
Mercury mixed with sandalwood, aloe, camphor, and saffron,
when solidified, becomes a worship of <s>Śiva</s> for the attainment of <s>Śiva</s>'s proximity. // RCint_1.23 //
By consuming it, O Supreme Goddess, mercury destroys the three-fold suffering;

children.text: durlabhaṃ brahmaviṣṇvādyaiḥ prāpyate paramaṃ padam // RCint_1.24 //
children.translated_text: the supreme state, difficult to attain even by <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is obtained. // RCint_1.24 //
O Supreme Goddess, one who meditates on <s>Rasendra</s> (mercury) dwelling in the interior of the heart-lotus,
is immediately freed from sins accumulated in previous births. // RCint_1.25 //
The fruit obtained from the proper worship of a thousand <s>svayambhū-liṅgas</s>,
that fruit is multiplied ten million times by worshipping a mercury <s>liṅga</s>. // RCint_1.26 //
One who gives purified and properly prepared mercury to the sick
obtains the eternal fruit of <s>tulādāna</s> (balance-gift) and <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifices). // RCint_1.27 //

children.text: rasavidyā parā vidyā trailokye'pi ca durlabhā /
children.translated_text: The science of mercury is the supreme science, rare even in the three worlds;
since it bestows both enjoyment and liberation, it should be known as endowed with virtues. // RCint_1.28 //
One who, devoid of the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, is a sinner who denigrates mercury —

children.text: nāhaṃ trātā bhave tasya janmakoṭiśatairapi // RCint_1.29 //
children.translated_text: I am not the protector of such a one in this world, even in hundreds of millions of births. // RCint_1.29 //
One who engages in conversation or bodily contact with those who denigrate mercury,
for thousands of births, such a person will be afflicted by sin. // RCint_1.30 //
Mercury consumed with gold gives the state of <s>Rudra</s>; as ash it also grants <s>Rudra</s>-hood;

children.text: viṣṇutvaṃ tārajīrṇastu brahmatvaṃ bhāskareṇa tu // RCint_1.31 //
children.translated_text: consumed with silver it gives the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; with the sun-gem, the state of <s>Brahmā</s>. // RCint_1.31 //
Consumed with lead it gives the state of <s>Dhaneśa</s> (Kubera); with <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment), the state of <s>Sūrya</s>;

children.text: rājare tu śaśāṅkatvamamaratvaṃ ca rohaṇe // RCint_1.32 //
children.translated_text: with <s>rājata</s> (silver), the state of the Moon; with <s>rohaṇa</s> (a mineral), immortality. // RCint_1.32 //

children.text: sāmānyena tu tīkṣṇena naraḥ śakratvamāpnuyāt // RCint_1.33 //
children.translated_text: In general, with lead, a man may attain the state of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra). // RCint_1.33 //
Mercury free from defects is <s>Brahmā</s>; when solidified, it is <s>Janārdana</s> (Viṣṇu);

children.text: mārito rudrarūpī syād baddhaḥ sākṣāt sadāśivaḥ // RCint_1.34 //
children.translated_text: when killed, it takes the form of <s>Rudra</s>; when bound, it is <s>Sadāśiva</s> himself. // RCint_1.34 //

children.text: īdṛśasya guṇānāṃ paryavasānamambujasambhavo'pi mahākalpairapi vacobhirnāsādayitumalamityalaṃ bahunā // RCint_1.35 //
children.translated_text: Even <s>Brahmā</s>, born from the lotus, cannot exhaust the description of the qualities of such [mercury] even with words spanning a great cosmic age — enough of prolixity! // RCint_1.35 //

children.text: yadyanmayākriyata kārayituṃ ca śakyaṃ sūtendrakarma tadiha prathayāṃbabhūve /
children.translated_text: Whatever work on <s>Sūtendra</s> (mercury) was done by me and can be made to be done, that I have set forth here;

children.text: adhyāpayanti ya idaṃ natu kārayanti kurvanti nedamadhiyantyubhaye mṛṣārthāḥ // RCint_1.36 //
children.translated_text: those who teach this but do not have it performed, and those who perform it but do not study it — both are engaged in vain. // RCint_1.36 //
Now we expound the chapter on <s>mūrcchana</s> (solidification/swooning of mercury). // RCint_2.1 //
RCint, 2
<s>Mūrcchana</s> is the unfailing capacity to destroy disease. // RCint_2.2 //
<s>Mūrcchana</s>: (medical) definition

children.text: tattattantranigaditadevatāparicaraṇasmaraṇānantaraṃ tattacchodhanaprakriyābhir bahvībhiḥ pariśuddhānāṃ rasendrāṇāṃ tṛṇāraṇimaṇijanyavahṇinyāyena tāratamyam avalokamānaiḥ sūkṣmamatibhiḥ palārdhenāpi kartavyaḥ saṃskāraḥ sūtakasya ceti rasārṇavavacanād vyāvahārikatolakadvayaparimāṇenāpi pariśuddho raso mūrchayitavyaḥ // RCint_2.3 //
children.translated_text: After performing worship and meditation of the deities prescribed in the respective texts, mercury that has been thoroughly purified through numerous purification procedures — by those of subtle intellect who observe the gradations as in the analogy of fire produced from grass, friction-stick, and gem — should be processed even with half a <s>pala</s> measure; as stated in the <s>Rasārṇava</s>, 'the process of mercury should be done,' even mercury purified in the practical measure of two <s>tolakas</s> should be subjected to <s>mūrcchana</s>. // RCint_2.3 //
The methods of <s>mūrcchana</s> are of many kinds. // RCint_2.4 //

children.text: <jāraṇa:: central for medic. activation of mercury>
children.translated_text: <s>Jāraṇa</s>: central for the medicinal activation of mercury

children.text: rasaguṇabalijāraṇaṃ vināyaṃ na khalu rujāharaṇakṣamo rasendraḥ /
children.translated_text: Without <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion/assimilation) using substances that enhance the virtues and potency of mercury, <s>Rasendra</s> (mercury) is not capable of destroying diseases;

children.text: na jaladakaladhautapākahīnaḥ spṛśati rasāyanatāmiti prasiddhiḥ // RCint_2.5 //
children.translated_text: it is well known that without the process of washing with water, purifying, and cooking, it does not attain the status of a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenating elixir). // RCint_2.5 //
For that purpose, two types of <s>sikatāyantra</s> (sand-bath apparatus) are described. // RCint_2.6 //
<s>Vālukāyantra</s> (sand-bath apparatus)

children.text: yathā niravadhiniṣpīḍitamṛdambarādipariliptām atikaṭhinakācaghaṭīm agre vakṣyamāṇaprakārāṃ rasagarbhiṇīm adhastarjanyaṅgulipramāṇitacchidrāyām anurūpasthālikāyām āropya paritastāṃ dvitryaṅgulimitena lavaṇena nirantarālīkaraṇapuraḥsaraṃ sikatābhir ā galam āpūrya vardhamānakam āpūraṇīyaṃ kramataśca tricaturāṇi pañcaṣāṇi vā vāsarāṇi jvalanajvālayā pācanīyam ityekaṃ yantram // RCint_2.7 //
children.translated_text: As follows: a very hard glass vessel, smeared with well-pressed clay and cloth, containing mercury as described later, is placed upon a suitable pan with a hole the size of a forefinger at the bottom, then surrounded with salt to fill all gaps to two or three finger-widths, then filled to the neck with sand, and a dome-shaped cover is placed on top; then it should be heated with flames gradually for three or four, or five or six days — this is one apparatus. // RCint_2.7 //

children.text: hastaikamātrapramāṇavasudhāntarnikhātāṃ prāgvatkācaghaṭīṃ nāticipiṭamukhīṃ nātyuccamukhīṃ maṣībhājanaprāyāṃ kharparacakrikayā kācacakrikayā vā niruddhavadanavivarāṃ mṛṇmayīṃ vā ghaṭīṃ vidhāya karīṣairupari puṭo deya ityanyadyantram // RCint_2.8 //
children.translated_text: A glass vessel of one cubit measure, buried in the earth, not too flat-mouthed nor too tall-mouthed, resembling an ink-pot, with its opening sealed by a stone disc or glass disc, or alternatively an earthen vessel may be prepared; and a cake of cow-dung fuel is placed on top as a sealed heating — this is the other apparatus. // RCint_2.8 //
<s>Vālukāyantra</s> (sand-bath apparatus)

children.text: asamaśakaladvayātmakalohasampuṭakena sikatāyantramadhye bhūdhare veti trilocanaḥ // RCint_2.9 //
children.translated_text: <s>Trilocana</s> (Śiva) states: in the <s>sikatāyantra</s> (sand-bath), using a metal container made of two unequal stone pieces, [the process is done] on the earth. // RCint_2.9 //
<s>Jāraṇa</s>: further apparatus

children.text: kūrmayantre rase gandhaṃ ṣaḍguṇaṃ jārayedbudhaḥ ityanye // RCint_2.10 //
children.translated_text: Others say: the wise one should assimilate six parts of sulphur into mercury in a <s>kūrmayantra</s> (tortoise apparatus). // RCint_2.10 //
Mercury: <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation)

children.text: atra pakṣe rāgastathā na syāt tenādau pañcaguṇān jārayitvā śeṣaikaḥ kūpikādau jāraṇīyastadā rāgaḥ sādhuḥ syāt // RCint_2.11 //
children.translated_text: In this method, the color does not develop properly; therefore, first assimilating five parts, the remaining one part should be assimilated in a <s>kūpikā</s> (flask) and similar vessel — then the color will be excellent. // RCint_2.11 //
<s>Jāraṇa</s>: producing color

children.text: atra kajjalim antareṇa kevalagandhakamapi sātmyena jārayanti // RCint_2.12 //
children.translated_text: Here, some assimilate sulphur alone gradually even without <s>kajjalī</s> (black sulphide of mercury). // RCint_2.12 //
Mercury: <s>jāraṇa</s>: <s>sindūra</s> (vermilion) color

children.text: kūpīkoṭaramāgataṃ rasaguṇairgandhaistulāyāṃ vibhuṃ vijñāya jvalanakrameṇa sikatāyantre śanaiḥ pācayet /
children.translated_text: Mercury that has entered the cavity of the flask, balanced on a scale with its measure of sulphur, should be gently heated in a <s>sikatāyantra</s> (sand-bath) by the gradual method of fire;

children.text: vāraṃvāramanena vahṇividhinā gandhakṣayaṃ sādhayet sindūradyutito'nubhūya bhaṇitaḥ karmakramo'yaṃ mayā // RCint_2.13 //
children.translated_text: again and again by this fire-method one should accomplish the consumption of sulphur; when the brilliance of <s>sindūra</s> (vermilion) is perceived — this procedure of the process has been stated by me. // RCint_2.13 //

children.text: āroṭakam antareṇa hiṅgulagandhakābhyāṃ piṣṭābhyāmapi rasasindūraḥ saṃpādyaḥ // RCint_2.14 //
children.translated_text: Even without <s>āroṭaka</s> (sublimate), <s>rasasindūra</s> can be prepared from <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar) and sulphur ground together. // RCint_2.14 //
<s>Rasasindūra</s> (mercuric sulphide/vermilion): production
Taking three parts of mercury and one part each of gold, pearl, silver, and lotus,

children.text: rasaguṇabalibhir vidhāya piṣṭiṃ racaya nirantarambubhiḥ kumāryāḥ // RCint_2.15 //
children.translated_text: make a <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste) with substances that enhance the virtues and potency of mercury, continuously grinding with the juice of <s>kumārī</s> (aloe vera). // RCint_2.15 //
<s>Piṣṭī</s>/<s>kajjalī</s> (?)
Up to six times the base quantity, this should be applied through progressive assimilation with increasing proportions of sacrificial substances;

children.text: yoge piṣṭiḥ pācyā kajjalikārthaṃ jāraṇārthaṃ ca // RCint_2.16 //
children.translated_text: in combination, the <s>piṣṭī</s> should be cooked for the purpose of making <s>kajjalī</s> and for the purpose of <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation). // RCint_2.16 //

children.text: prakāro'yam adhoyantreṇaiva sidhyati na punarūrdhvayantreṇa // RCint_2.17 //
children.translated_text: This method succeeds only with the lower apparatus, not with the upper apparatus. // RCint_2.17 //

children.text:
<bottle:: appr. material>
kācamṛttikayoḥ kūpī hemno'yastārayoḥ kvacit /
children.translated_text:
Bottle: appropriate material
The flask may be of glass or clay; sometimes of gold, iron, or silver.
The coating is made of molasses and iron, with the addition of chalk and salt. // RCint_2.18 //
Bottle: appropriate coating
With these two types of apparatus, the skilled ones assimilate even abundant gold, mica, <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence), and the like;

children.text: yathecchamacchaiḥ sumanovicārair vicakṣaṇāḥ pallavayantu bhūyaḥ // RCint_2.19 //
children.translated_text: let the discerning ones further elaborate at will with pure and excellent deliberations. // RCint_2.19 //
Mercury: <s>rañjana</s> (coloring): <s>antardhūma</s> (internal fumigation)
Mercury colored by sulphur of hundredfold measure, cooked by the <s>antardhūma</s> (internal fumigation) method,

children.text: sa bhavetsahasravedhī tāre tāmre bhujaṅge ca // RCint_2.20 //
children.translated_text: becomes capable of transmuting a thousandfold in silver, copper, and lead. // RCint_2.20 //
Mercury: <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation)
Placing a measure equal to the mercury as an offering in a small clay vessel within a <s>sikatāyantra</s> (sand-bath apparatus),

children.text: tailāviśeṣe 'tra rasaṃ nidadhyānmagnārdhakāyaṃ pravilokya bhūyaḥ // RCint_2.21 //
children.translated_text: one should place the mercury in any oil, observing that it is half-submerged, and then again // RCint_2.21 //

children.text: ā ṣaḍguṇaṃ gandhakam alpam alpaṃ kṣipedasau jīrṇabalirbalī syāt /
children.translated_text: one should add sulphur little by little up to six times the quantity; the offering once assimilated makes it potent;

children.text: raseṣu sarveṣu niyojito'yamasaṃśayaṃ hanti gadaṃ javena // RCint_2.22 //
children.translated_text: when employed in all mercurial preparations, it undoubtedly destroys disease swiftly. // RCint_2.22 //

children.text: nāgādiśulvādibhir atra piṣṭiṃ vādeṣu yogeṣu ca nikṣipanti // RCint_2.23 //
children.translated_text: With lead, copper, and similar metals, they add this <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste) in alchemical transmutation and medicinal preparations. // RCint_2.23 //
Mercury: <s>nigaḍa</s> (binding/fettering)
Milk from <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia) and <s>arka</s> (Calotropis), seeds of <s>Brahma</s> (a plant), <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium resin),

children.text: saindhavaṃ dviguṇaṃ mardyaṃ nigaḍo'yaṃ mahottamaḥ // RCint_2.24 //
children.translated_text: <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt) in double quantity — these should be ground together; this is the supreme <s>nigaḍa</s> (fetter). // RCint_2.24 //
Mercury: <s>rasasindūra</s>? <s>nigaḍa</s>?
Mercury mixed with <s>mārakāmbu</s> (a liquid), white <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), placed in the belly of a flask in sand,

children.text: pācito yadi muhurmuhuritthaṃ bandhamṛcchati tadaiṣa rasendraḥ // RCint_2.25 //
children.translated_text: if cooked repeatedly in this manner, then this <s>Rasendra</s> (mercury) attains binding. // RCint_2.25 //
Filling a firmly constructed pan halfway with a quarter portion of salt,
with the powder of red bricks on top, and then a quarter portion of mercury, // RCint_2.26 //

children.text: sitasaindhavaṃ nidhāya sphaṭikārīṃ tatsamāṃ ca tasyordhve /
children.translated_text: placing white <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), and above it an equal amount of alum,
with alum, white rock salt, and pure mercury ground with the juice of <s>kanyakā</s> (aloe), // RCint_2.27 //
making a suitable thin layer and placing it on top, and again in the same manner
one should add alum and rock salt with mercury to prevent the mercury from slipping down. // RCint_2.28 //
For collecting it, placing pieces of earthen saucers on top, and covering with another firm pan,
sealing it, one should cook it methodically for three days. // RCint_2.29 //

children.text: atrānuktamapi bhallātakaṃ dadati vṛddhāḥ pāradatulyam // RCint_2.30 //
children.translated_text: Here, the elders also add <s>bhallātaka</s> (marking nut), though not mentioned, in an amount equal to the mercury. // RCint_2.30 //
RCint, 3
Now, we expound the chapter on <s>bandhana</s> (binding of mercury).
When natural fluidity exists, not being destroyed by fire constitutes being bound in solid form. // RCint_3.1 //
Even medicines prepared from forest herbs, such as ghee and oils, possess irresistible potency;
how much more so this [mercury], born from the body of the Lord, assimilated with dense gold, moon-metal, and sun-metal? // RCint_3.2 //
The nineteen <s>saṃskāras</s> (processes)
There are no less than nineteen procedures that accomplish this:

<s>mardana</s> (grinding), <s>mūrcchana</s> (solidification), <s>utthāpana</s> (sublimation), <s>svedana</s> (steaming), <s>pātana</s> (distillation), <s>bodhana</s> (awakening), <s>niyamana</s> (restraining), <s>saṃdīpana</s> (kindling), <s>anuvāsana</s> (oiling), <s>gaganādigrāsa</s> (feeding with mica etc.), <s>pramāṇa</s> (measuring), <s>cāraṇa</s> (making mobile), <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction), <s>bāhyadruti</s> (external liquefaction), <s>yoga</s> (combination), <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation), <s>rañjana</s> (coloring), <s>sāraṇa</s> (extraction), <s>krāmaṇa</s> (progressive pervasion), <s>vedhana</s> (transmutation), and <s>bhakṣaṇa</s> (ingestion). // RCint_3.3 //
Ritual rites before starting the <s>saṃskāras</s>

children.text: sampūjya śrīguruṃ kanyāṃ baṭukaṃ ca gaṇādhipam /
children.translated_text: Having worshipped the glorious <s>Guru</s>, the maiden, <s>Baṭuka</s>, and the Lord of the <s>Gaṇas</s>,
the <s>Yoginīs</s> and the <s>Kṣetrapālas</s> (field-guardians), preceded by offerings in four directions, // RCint_3.4 //
mercury should be placed in a secret chamber at an auspicious moment when the moon is strong,

children.text: khalve pāṣāṇaje lohe sudṛḍhe sārasambhave // RCint_3.5 //
children.translated_text: in a mortar made of stone or strong steel of excellent quality, // RCint_3.5 //
with a similarly clear, smooth pestle of four finger-breadths,
depositing it with an accomplished mantra, guarded by two or three attendants, // RCint_3.6 //
the physician should grind it with powders mixed in a sixteenth part
of the mercury, strained through cloth, with the fluids and other substances to be described. // RCint_3.7 //
One should grind and solidify the mercury, then sublimate it again, seven times.
Mercury: <s>doṣa</s> (defect): removal
With red brick powder, turmeric, smoke-residue, <s>sāra</s> (essence), wool, ash, and <s>tumbikā</s> (bottle gourd),
combined with lemon juice — for the removal of the <s>nāga</s> (lead) defect. // RCint_3.8 //
With the powder of <s>viśālā</s> and <s>aṅkola</s>, it releases the <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) defect;

children.text: rājavṛkṣasya mūlasya cūrṇena saha kanyayā // RCint_3.9 //
children.translated_text: with the powder of the root of <s>rājavṛkṣa</s> (castor plant), together with <s>kanyā</s> (aloe), // RCint_3.9 //
for the removal of the <s>mala</s> (impurity) defect, the auspicious grinding and sublimation [should be done];
with the juices of black <s>dhattūraka</s> (Datura), for the removal of <s>cāñcalya</s> (instability). // RCint_3.10 //
With the water of <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits) and <s>kanyakā</s> (aloe), for the pacification of the <s>viṣa</s> (poison) defect;
the <s>giri</s> (mineral) defect with <s>trikaṭu</s> (three pungents) in <s>kanyā</s> (aloe) water, with care. // RCint_3.11 //
With the powder of <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago) together with <s>kanyā</s> (aloe), for the destruction of the <s>agni</s> (fire) [defect];
and with hot <s>āranāla</s> (sour gruel), one should purify each defect.
Thus purified, the mercury becomes free from the seven defects

children.text: jāyate kāryakartā ca hy anyathā kāryanāśanaḥ // RCint_3.12 //
children.translated_text: and becomes capable of performing its function; otherwise it destroys its purpose. // RCint_3.12 //
Mercury: <s>utthāpana</s> (sublimation/raising)
The powder remaining from the <s>utthāpana</s> (sublimation) process, in a distillation apparatus,
the physician should collect the mercury adhering to the upper vessel. // RCint_3.13 //
<s>Svedana</s> (steaming)

children.text: rasaṃ caturguṇe vastre baddhvā dolākṛtaṃ pacet /
children.translated_text: One should tie the mercury in a cloth folded four times and cook it in a swing-like apparatus (<s>dolāyantra</s>),
for one day, in <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel) with pastes of <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents), <s>varā</s> (triphalā), <s>vahni</s> (Plumbago), and <s>kanyā</s> (aloe);
this is called <s>svedana</s> (steaming), for the removal of remaining defects. // RCint_3.14 //
<s>Kāñjika</s> (sour gruel): production
With various available grains, dehusked and mixed with water,
an earthen vessel should be filled and kept until it becomes sour. // RCint_3.15 //
In that [gruel], <s>ghanā</s> (Cyperus), <s>vāṅmuṇḍī</s>, <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>,

children.text: mīnākṣī caiva sarpākṣī sahadevī śatāvarī // RCint_3.16 //
children.translated_text: <s>mīnākṣī</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, <s>sahadevī</s>, <s>śatāvarī</s>, // RCint_3.16 //

children.text: triphalā girikarṇī ca haṃsapādī ca citrakaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>triphalā</s>, <s>girikarṇī</s>, <s>haṃsapādī</s>, and <s>citraka</s> —

children.text: samūlakāṇḍaṃ piṣṭvā tu yathālābhaṃ vinikṣipet // RCint_3.17 //
children.translated_text: grinding them with roots and stems, one should add them as available. // RCint_3.17 //
Added to the previously prepared sour vessel, this becomes <s>dhānyāmlaka</s> (grain-vinegar);
it should be employed in all processes of <s>Rasarāja</s> (mercury), beginning with <s>svedana</s> (steaming). // RCint_3.18 //
In its absence, very sour <s>āranāla</s> (sour gruel) may be used instead.
<s>Ūrdhvapātana</s> (upward distillation)
Three parts of mercury and one part of <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) powder, with lemon [juice],
should be ground together until it forms a mass. // RCint_3.19 //
That mass is placed in the lower vessel, and water is put in the upper vessel;

children.text: kṛtvālavālaṃ kenāpi dattvā vārdraṃ hi plotakam // RCint_3.20 //
children.translated_text: making a rim with some material and placing a wet cloth, // RCint_3.20 //
sealing the junction, fire should be maintained beneath for four <s>yāmas</s> (twelve hours);
then one should collect the mercury adhering to the upper vessel by proper method. // RCint_3.21 //
This is called <s>ūrdhvapātana</s> (upward distillation) by physicians for the purification of mercury.
<s>Saṃdhirodha</s> (junction-sealing): importance
The mouth of the vessel containing mercury swallows the other vessel;

children.text: tathā saṃdhir dvayoḥ kāryaḥ pātanātrayayantrake // RCint_3.22 //
children.translated_text: thus the junction of the two should be properly sealed in all three types of distillation apparatus. // RCint_3.22 //
Sizes, measures: taught by the <s>Guru</s>
The dimensions of the apparatus should be learned from the mouth of the <s>Guru</s> by the discerning;

children.text: rasasya mānāniyamāt kathituṃ naiva śakyate // RCint_3.23 //
children.translated_text: because the quantity of mercury is not fixed, it cannot be stated precisely. // RCint_3.23 //
<s>Adhaḥpātana</s> (downward distillation)
Mercury called 'butter-like' should be ground for a day with lemon juice
together with <s>vānarī</s>, <s>śigru</s> (drumstick), <s>śikhi</s> (peacock [feather plant]), combined with salt and <s>asurī</s> (mustard). // RCint_3.24 //
Knowing that the mercury has been reduced to a vanished paste, one should smear it on the upper vessel;

children.text: ūrdhvabhāṇḍodaraṃ liptvā tv adhogaṃ jalasaṃbhṛtam // RCint_3.25 //
children.translated_text: having smeared the interior of the upper vessel, the lower vessel should be filled with water. // RCint_3.25 //

children.text: saṃdhilepaṃ dvayoḥ kṛtvā tadyantraṃ bhuvi pūrayet /
children.translated_text: Having sealed the junction of both vessels, one should bury that apparatus in the earth;

children.text: upariṣṭātpuṭe datte jale patati pāradaḥ // RCint_3.26 //
children.translated_text: when heat is applied from above, the mercury falls into the water. // RCint_3.26 //
This is called <s>adhaḥpātana</s> (downward distillation) by the <s>Siddhas</s> and others in the processing of mercury.
<s>Tiryakpātana</s> (lateral distillation)

children.text: ghaṭe rasaṃ vinikṣipya sajalaṃ ghaṭam anyakam /
children.translated_text: Placing mercury in one pot and water in another pot,

children.text: tiryaṅmukhaṃ dvayoḥ kṛtvā tanmukhaṃ rodhayet sudhīḥ // RCint_3.27 //
children.translated_text: making the mouths of both face sideways, the wise one should seal that junction. // RCint_3.27 //
One should kindle fire beneath the mercury until it enters the water;
this is called <s>tiryakpātana</s> (lateral distillation) by the <s>Siddhas</s> such as <s>Nāgārjuna</s> and others. // RCint_3.28 //

children.text: <3 pātanas:: removal of vaṅga and nāga>
children.translated_text: The three <s>pātanas</s> (distillations): removal of <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) and <s>nāga</s> (lead)
If <s>nāga</s> (lead) and <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) have been mixed into the mercury for commercial fraud,

children.text: tābhyāṃ syātkṛtrimo doṣas tanmuktiḥ pātanatrayāt // RCint_3.29 //
children.translated_text: these cause an artificial defect; liberation from that comes through the three distillations. // RCint_3.29 //
<s>Bodhana</s> (awakening): removal of impotency
Mercury thus processed through <s>kapardī</s> (cowrie-shell method) becomes impotent;

children.text: tanmuktaye'sya kriyate bodhanaṃ kathyate hi tat // RCint_3.30 //
children.translated_text: for its liberation, <s>bodhana</s> (awakening) is performed — that is now described. // RCint_3.30 //
In a <s>Viśvāmitra</s> skull-cup or in a glass flask,
placing <s>sṛṣṭyambuja</s> (a lotus preparation), and then immersing [the mercury] therein, // RCint_3.31 //
one should fill and bury it in the earth for three days to the depth of a royal cubit;
by this, the <s>Sūtarāja</s> (King Mercury) is freed from its impotent state. // RCint_3.32 //
<s>Dīpana</s> (kindling)? <s>Bodhana</s> (awakening)?
Mercury placed inside a pot, ground with salt and acid,

children.text: ācchādyāmlajalaṃ kiṃcit kṣiptvā śarāveṇa rodhayet // RCint_3.33 //
children.translated_text: covering it and adding some sour water, one should seal it with a saucer. // RCint_3.33 //
A light sealed heating should be given from above; the mercury will become revived.
<s>Svedana</s> for the restoration of mercury

children.text: kadarthanenaiva napuṃsakatvam evaṃ bhavedasya rasasya paścāt /
children.translated_text: By such harsh treatment, the mercury subsequently becomes impotent;

children.text: vīryaprakarṣāya ca bhūrjapattre svedyo jale saindhavacūrṇagarbhe // RCint_3.34 //
children.translated_text: for the restoration of its potency, it should be steamed in a birch-bark [container] in water containing <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt) powder. // RCint_3.34 //
<s>Niyamana</s> (restraining)
With the waters of <s>sarpākṣī</s>, <s>ciñcikā</s> (tamarind), <s>vandhyā</s> (barren plant), <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta), <s>abda</s> (Cyperus), and <s>kanaka</s> (Datura),

children.text: dinaṃ saṃsveditaḥ sūto niyamāt sthiratāṃ vrajet // RCint_3.35 //
children.translated_text: mercury steamed for one day attains stability through <s>niyamana</s> (restraint). // RCint_3.35 //
<s>Dīpana</s> (kindling/stimulation)
<s>Kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol), <s>pañcalavaṇa</s> (five salts), <s>rājikā</s> (mustard seeds), and <s>marica</s> (black pepper),
two parts of <s>śigru</s> (drumstick) seeds, all combined with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), // RCint_3.36 //

children.text: āloḍya kāñjike dolāyantre pākād dinais tribhiḥ /
children.translated_text: stirring in <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel), cooking in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus) for three days —

children.text: dīpanaṃ jāyate samyak sūtarājasya jāraṇe // RCint_3.37 //
children.translated_text: proper <s>dīpana</s> (kindling) of <s>Sūtarāja</s> (King Mercury) for <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation) is thus achieved. // RCint_3.37 //
<s>Dīpana</s> (kindling)
Alternatively, one should cook it in <s>kāñjika</s> with the juices of <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago) for three days;

children.text: dīpanaṃ jāyate tasya rasarājasya cottamam // RCint_3.38 //
children.translated_text: excellent <s>dīpana</s> (kindling) of <s>Rasarāja</s> (King Mercury) is thereby achieved. // RCint_3.38 //
<s>Anuvāsana</s> (oiling/lubrication)
<s>Rasarāja</s> (King Mercury), having been kindled, combined with lemon juice,

children.text: dinaikaṃ dhārayed gharme mṛtpātre vā śilodbhave // RCint_3.39 //
children.translated_text: should be held for one day in the sun in an earthen vessel or stone vessel. // RCint_3.39 //
<s>Jāraṇa</s> is indeed the state of returning to one's former condition after the feeding of dense gold and other substances, distinct from distillation and straining. // RCint_3.40 //
<s>Jāraṇa</s> (assimilation): definition

children.text: kiṃca ghanahemādijīrṇasya kṛtakṣetrīkaraṇānām eva śarīriṇāṃ bhakṣaṇe 'dhikāra ityabhihitam // RCint_3.41 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, it is stated that only those embodied beings who have had their field prepared (through <s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>) are eligible to ingest mercury that has assimilated dense gold and other substances. // RCint_3.41 //
<s>Jāraṇa</s>: religious significance
And its fruit has been declared by the Lord himself:
"When all sins are destroyed, <s>rasajāraṇā</s> (assimilation of mercury) is attained;
upon its attainment, the knowledge characterized by liberation is indeed obtained." // RCint_3.42 //
"<s>Jāraṇa</s> is the indicator of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) for the practitioner, O <s>Devī</s>;

children.text: khalvastu piṇḍikā devi rasendro liṅgamucyate // RCint_3.43 //
children.translated_text: the mortar is the pedestal, O <s>Devī</s>, and <s>Rasendra</s> (mercury) is called the <s>liṅga</s>. // RCint_3.43 //

children.text: mardanaṃ vandanaṃ caiva grāsaḥ pūjā vidhīyate /
children.translated_text: Grinding is worship, and the feeding is the offering that is performed;

children.text: yāvaddināni vahnistho jāraṇe dhāryate rasaḥ // RCint_3.44 //
children.translated_text: for as many days as the mercury is kept on fire during <s>jāraṇa</s>, // RCint_3.44 //
for that many thousands of years one is honored in the world of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: dinamekaṃ rasendrasya yo dadāti hutāśanam // RCint_3.45 //
children.translated_text: One who gives fire to <s>Rasendra</s> (mercury) for even a single day, // RCint_3.45 //

children.text: dravanti tasya pāpāni kurvannapi na lipyate /
children.translated_text: his sins melt away, and even while performing actions he is not tainted."
Those who desire excellent results from mercury without assimilating purified gold and sulphur,

children.text: kṣetrādanuptādapi sasyajātaṃ kṛṣīvalāste bhiṣajaśca mandāḥ // RCint_3.46 //
children.translated_text: they are like farmers expecting a harvest from an unsown field — such physicians are dull. // RCint_3.46 //

children.text: <jāraṇa:: medic. properties according to the weight of sulfur>
children.translated_text: <s>Jāraṇa</s>: medicinal properties according to the weight of sulphur

children.text: tulye tu gandhake jīrṇe śuddhācchataguṇo rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: When an equal amount of sulphur is assimilated, the mercury becomes pure and of hundredfold potency;

children.text: dviguṇe gandhake jīrṇe sarvakuṣṭhaharaḥ paraḥ // RCint_3.47 //
children.translated_text: when double the sulphur is assimilated, it becomes the supreme destroyer of all <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases). // RCint_3.47 //
When triple the sulphur is assimilated, it destroys all torpidity;
when quadruple is assimilated, it destroys wrinkles and grey hair. // RCint_3.48 //
When fivefold sulphur is assimilated, the mercury destroys consumptive diseases;
when sixfold sulphur is assimilated, the mercury destroys all diseases;
thus <s>Śrī Bhairava</s> himself spoke assuredly to <s>Devī</s>. // RCint_3.49 //
With a sulphur paste, a ball is formed in the sulphur <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation) process. // RCint_3.50 //
<s>Jāraṇa</s> (assimilation)
From that, when mica <s>sattva</s> (essence) of hundredfold [sulphur] is assimilated, or an equal amount,
when the <s>sattva</s> (essence) of <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites), <s>kharpara</s> (zinc), <s>tāla</s> (orpiment), etc. is assimilated, it becomes potency-bearing. // RCint_3.51 //
When gold is assimilated, it becomes a bestower of a thousandfold mass of virtues;

children.text: vajrādijīrṇasūtasya guṇān vetti śivaḥ svayam // RCint_3.52 //
children.translated_text: the qualities of mercury that has assimilated diamond and other substances — <s>Śiva</s> himself alone knows. // RCint_3.52 //

children.text: devyā rajo bhavedgandho dhātuḥ śukraṃ tathābhrakam /
children.translated_text: The menstrual fluid of <s>Devī</s> becomes sulphur; the semen of the mineral becomes mica;
in the embrace, both are equal, because of the dearness of <s>Śiva</s>'s semen. // RCint_3.53 //
From the union of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, the supreme state is obtained;

children.text: yathā syājjāraṇā bahvī tathā syādguṇado rasaḥ // RCint_3.54 //
children.translated_text: the more the <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation), the more the mercury becomes a bestower of virtues. // RCint_3.54 //
Mercury: <s>grāsārthin</s> (desirous of feeding)
A diamond-pointed needle pierced to eight finger-breadths, coated with clay,

children.text: vilipya gomayālpāgnau puṭitaṃ tatra śoṣitam // RCint_3.55 //
children.translated_text: heated with cow-dung in a mild fire, and then dried therein — // RCint_3.55 //

children.text: tryahaṃ vajribile kṣipto grāsārthī jāyate rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: mercury immersed for three days in diamond-bile becomes desirous of feeding;
it devours sulphur, gold, and other substances, as well as diamond <s>sattva</s> (essence), instantly. // RCint_3.56 //
Mercury: <s>grāsārthin</s> (desirous of feeding)

children.text: mūrchādhyāyoktaṣaḍguṇabalijīrṇaḥ piṣṭikotthitarasaḥ khalve'tyantaṃ bubhukṣito ghanahemavajrasattvādi tvaritameva grasatītyanyaḥ prakāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Mercury that has assimilated sixfold sacrificial substances as described in the <s>mūrcchana</s> chapter, extracted from the <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste), and made exceedingly hungry in the mortar — it swallows dense gold, diamond <s>sattva</s>, and other substances immediately; this is another method.
Some practitioners employ both these procedures together. // RCint_3.57 //
Mercury: <s>grāsārthin</s> (desirous of feeding)
In <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel) combined with <s>tuttha</s> (copper sulphate), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), <s>svarji</s> (soda ash), and pungent copper, soaked for three days,

children.text: kāñjikaṃ bhāvitaṃ tena gandhādyaṃ kṣarati kṣaṇāt // RCint_3.58 //
children.translated_text: treated with that, sulphur and other substances are consumed instantly. // RCint_3.58 //

children.text: viḍe sakāñjike kṣipto rasaḥ syād grāsalālasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Mercury placed in <s>viḍa</s> (a special salt preparation) with <s>kāñjika</s> becomes eager to devour;
it devours all metals, all <s>sattvas</s> (essences), and diamond. // RCint_3.59 //
<s>Viḍa</s> (special salt): <s>vaḍavānala</s> (submarine fire)
Conch-shell powder should be treated with <s>ravi</s> (Calotropis) milk in sunlight for a day;
likewise, <s>dhūmasāra</s> (smoke-essence) should be treated with lemon juice for one day. // RCint_3.60 //
<s>Sauvarcala</s> (sochal salt) should be treated with goat's urine for four <s>yāmas</s> (twelve hours);

children.text: kaṇṭakārīṃ ca saṃkvāthya dinaikaṃ naramūtrakaiḥ // RCint_3.61 //
children.translated_text: and <s>kaṇṭakārī</s> (Solanum xanthocarpum) should be boiled and treated with human urine for one day. // RCint_3.61 //
<s>Svarjikṣāra</s> (soda ash), <s>tintiḍīka</s> (tamarind), <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol), and <s>śilājatu</s> (shilajit),
should be treated separately with lemon juice for four <s>yāmas</s> each. // RCint_3.62 //
Dehusked <s>jayapāla</s> (Croton) and the juice of radishes for a day;

children.text: saindhavaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ guñjāṃ dinaṃ śigrujaṭāmbhasā // RCint_3.63 //
children.translated_text: <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus seeds) for a day with <s>śigru</s> (drumstick) root water. // RCint_3.63 //
All these in equal parts should be ground with lemon juice;
that ball should be carefully preserved — this <s>viḍa</s> is [called] <s>vaḍavānala</s> (submarine fire). // RCint_3.64 //
Mercury ground with this, placed on a heated mortar,
devours gold and all metals and <s>sattvas</s> (essences) instantly. // RCint_3.65 //
<s>Viḍa</s>: anonymous: production
The alkali of radish, ginger, and <s>vahni</s> (Plumbago), filtered through cow's urine —

children.text: vastrapūto dravo grāhyo gandhakaṃ tena bhāvayet /
children.translated_text: the cloth-filtered liquid should be collected; sulphur should be treated with it

children.text: śatavāraṃ khare gharme viḍo'yaṃ hemajāraṇe // RCint_3.66 //
children.translated_text: a hundred times in strong sunlight — this <s>viḍa</s> is for the assimilation of gold. // RCint_3.66 //
<s>Viḍa</s>: anonymous: production
With the alkalis of radish, ginger, and <s>citrā</s> (Plumbago), filtered through cow's urine,

children.text: gandhakaḥ śataśo bhāvyo viḍo'yaṃ jāraṇe mataḥ // RCint_3.67 //
children.translated_text: sulphur should be treated hundreds of times — this <s>viḍa</s> is approved for <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation). // RCint_3.67 //
<s>Viḍa</s>: anonymous: production
<s>Vāstūka</s> (Chenopodium), <s>eraṇḍa</s> (castor), <s>kadalī</s> (banana), <s>devadālī</s> (a creeper), <s>punarnavā</s>,
<s>vāsā</s> (Adhatoda), <s>palāśa</s> (Butea), <s>nicula</s> (Barringtonia), <s>tila</s> (sesame), <s>kāñcana</s> (Datura), and <s>mokṣaka</s> — // RCint_3.68 //
all parts, cut into pieces, not too dry, on a stone surface,

children.text: dagdhaṃ kāṇḍaṃ tilānāṃ ca pañcāṅgaṃ mūlakasya ca // RCint_3.69 //
children.translated_text: burnt stems of sesame, and the five parts of radish — // RCint_3.69 //
should be soaked with the group of urines; the water filtered therefrom
should be cooked in an iron vessel using the apparatus, by one who knows the <s>haṃsapāka</s> (swan-cooking) fire technique. // RCint_3.70 //
When abundant steam and many bubbles rise,
then <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol), <s>saurāṣṭrī</s> (alum), three alkalis, three pungents, // RCint_3.71 //

children.text: gandhakaśca sito hiṅgu lavaṇāni ca ṣaṭ tathā /
children.translated_text: sulphur, white <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), and six salts —
the powder of all these should be cast, O <s>Devī</s>, into the middle of an iron container. // RCint_3.72 //

children.text:
saptāhaṃ bhūgataṃ paścāddhāryas tu pracuro viḍaḥ /
atra sakalakṣāraiś ca sāmyaṃ tilakāṇḍānāṃ nityanāthapādā likhanti /
children.translated_text:
After seven days buried in the earth, this abundant <s>viḍa</s> should be preserved.
Here, <s>Nityanāthapāda</s> writes that all alkalis are equal to the sesame stems.
<s>Haṃsapākayantra</s> (swan-cooking apparatus)
Filling an earthen saucer with sand and placing [the substance] upon it,

children.text: tulyaṃ ca kharparaṃ tatra śanairmṛdvagninā pacet // RCint_3.73 //
children.translated_text: and placing an equal saucer on top, one should cook gently with a mild fire. // RCint_3.73 //

children.text: pañcakṣārais tathā mūtrair lavaṇaṃ ca viḍaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: With five alkalis, with urines, salt, and <s>viḍa</s> —
this is called the <s>haṃsapāka</s> (swan-cooking) apparatus by the best of commentators. // RCint_3.74 //
<s>Viḍa</s>: anonymous: production
Sulphur should be treated with cow's urine in sunlight a hundred times;
likewise, burnt conch-shell should be treated with <s>śigru</s> (drumstick) root juice. // RCint_3.75 //
With this sulphur and conch-shell in equal parts, together with <s>viḍa</s> and <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt),

children.text: etair vimarditaḥ sūto grasate sarvalohakam // RCint_3.76 //
children.translated_text: mercury ground with these devours all metals. // RCint_3.76 //
<s>Viḍa</s>: anonymous: production
One should treat lemon-alkali with the juice of <s>devadālī</s> (a creeper) fruit
twenty-one times — this <s>viḍa</s> is for the assimilation of <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence). // RCint_3.77 //
Thus, other types of <s>viḍa</s> should also be sought from other treatises. // RCint_3.78 //
<s>Jāraṇa</s>: procedure
A gold leaf of one sixty-fourth part, smeared with peacock bile,
should be placed upon the mercury in a heated mortar and ground

children.text: dinaṃ jambīratoyena grāse grāse tv ayaṃ vidhiḥ // RCint_3.79 //
children.translated_text: for a day with lemon juice — this is the procedure for each feeding. // RCint_3.79 //
Gently steaming it in birch-bark, tied up with pungent <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel),

children.text: bhāṇḍake tridinaṃ sūtaṃ jīrṇasvarṇaṃ samuddharet // RCint_3.80 //
children.translated_text: in a vessel for three days, one should extract the mercury that has assimilated the gold. // RCint_3.80 //
If it weighs more [than expected], it should be steamed again until the proper amount;
one should assimilate the substance in the sequence of one thirty-second, one sixteenth, and one eighth parts. // RCint_3.81 //
For silver and other <s>sattvas</s> (essences), the same procedure is prescribed;
[one should use] <s>cullikā</s> (furnace) salt and sulphur, or in its absence, peacock bile. // RCint_3.82 //
<s>Taptakhalva</s> (heated mortar)
Digging a pit in the earth, one should place goat-dung and husk-fire therein;

children.text: tasyopari sthitaṃ khalvaṃ taptakhalvamiti smṛtam // RCint_3.83 //
children.translated_text: the mortar placed upon that is known as the <s>taptakhalva</s> (heated mortar). // RCint_3.83 //
<s>Dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus)
The mercury with its feeding should be ground with five or six parts of <s>yavakṣāra</s> (barley alkali),
with sulphur in one-sixteenth or one-eighth part of the mercury; // RCint_3.84 //
then grinding it in lemon juice or <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel),
the <s>dolāpāka</s> (swing-cooking) should be performed — this is known as the <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus). // RCint_3.85 //
<s>Jāraṇa</s> in the <s>kacchapayantra</s> (tortoise apparatus) is described:
A fired crucible placed in the hole of a saucer that is positioned in a vessel constantly filled with water —
in that crucible submerged in water, the mercury is wrapped with one-eighth part of <s>viḍa</s>; // RCint_3.86 //
sealed in an iron vessel and heated by bellows, it devours gold;

children.text: vālukopari puṭo yuktyā mahāmudrayā ca nirvāhaḥ // RCint_3.87 //
children.translated_text: a sealed heating is applied skillfully over sand, and the process is completed with the <s>mahāmudrā</s> (great seal). // RCint_3.87 //
Covering with a very flat-bottomed vessel, sealing and applying fire.
<s>Jāraṇa</s> (assimilation)

children.text: kuṇḍāmbhasi lohamaye saviḍaṃ sagrāsam īśajaṃ pātre /
children.translated_text: In a <s>kuṇḍa</s> (basin) of water, in a metallic vessel, mercury with <s>viḍa</s> and its feeding, born of the Lord,

children.text: aticipiṭalohapātryā pidhāya saṃlipya vahninā yojyaḥ // RCint_3.88 //
children.translated_text: covering with a very flat iron vessel, sealing and applying fire. // RCint_3.88 //
<s>Jāraṇa</s>: importance for alchemy and <s>rasāyana</s>

children.text: iyataiva rasāyanatvaṃ paryavasiti kiṃtu vādasya na prādhānyam /
children.translated_text: To this extent alone does the status of <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) culminate; however, for <s>vāda</s> (alchemy/transmutation), it is not the primary concern;
but now, <s>jāraṇa</s> is taught as primary for both purposes. // RCint_3.89 //
<s>Pakṣacheda</s> (refutation of a view): aim
Those who, having achieved minor accomplishments like making leaves through assimilation of <s>bīja</s> (seed-metal) without dense [gold], think themselves accomplished —
they are misers who, having reached the ocean, are content with obtaining a cowrie shell. // RCint_3.90 //
Without mica <s>sattva</s> (essence) alone, no other substance is capable of clipping the wings of mercury;

children.text: tena niruddhaprasaro niyamyate badhyate ca sukham // RCint_3.91 //
children.translated_text: by that, its spreading is restrained, it is controlled, and it is easily bound. // RCint_3.91 //
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): subtypes: color

children.text: raktaṃ pītaṃ ca hemārthe kṛṣṇaṃ hemaśarīrayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Red and yellow [mica] are for gold-making; black is for both gold and the body;

children.text: tārakarmaṇi tacchuklaṃ kācakiṭṭaṃ sadā tyajet // RCint_3.92 //
children.translated_text: white is for silver-making; <s>kācakiṭṭa</s> (glass-slag mica) should always be rejected. // RCint_3.92 //
<s>Jāraṇa</s>: <s>samukha</s> (?)
Adding bit by bit and grinding in a warm mortar, mica <s>sattva</s>, gold, and other substances,
<s>Rasendra</s> (mercury) moves/assimilates with [the juices of] <s>kṣitikha</s>, <s>vetasa</s> (cane), lemon, <s>bījapūra</s> (citron), and sour substances,
or with previously prepared <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel). // RCint_3.96 //
One who knows to assimilate mica first and then to perform <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction) <s>jāraṇa</s> with gold at the end,

children.text: yo jānāti na vādī vṛthaiva so 'rthakṣayaṃ kurute // RCint_3.97 //
children.translated_text: but not a practitioner of <s>vāda</s> (alchemy) — he merely wastes his resources in vain. // RCint_3.97 //
<s>Garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction)
Mica <s>sattva</s> (essence) combined with an equal amount of <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites) <s>sattva</s>,
when assimilated in its entirety, O <s>Devī</s>, the mercury becomes capable of <s>garbhadrāva</s> (internal liquefaction). // RCint_3.98 //

children.text: evaṃ tārābhrādayaḥ svasvaripuṇā nirvyūḍhāḥ prayojanamavalokya prayojyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, silver, mica, and others, each overcome by its respective antagonist, should be employed after observing the purpose.
<s>Garbhadruti</s> (2); <s>śulvābhra</s> (copper-mica)
The powder of <s>kamala</s> (copper), <s>ghana</s> (mica), and <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrites), combined in equal parts, mixes together;

children.text: tacchulvābhraṃ śīghraṃ carati rasendro dravati garbhe // RCint_3.99 //
children.translated_text: that is <s>śulvābhra</s> (copper-mica) — <s>Rasendra</s> (mercury) quickly assimilates it and liquefies internally. // RCint_3.99 //
<s>Garbhadruti</s>: definition
Without <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction), <s>jāraṇa</s> itself cannot occur; therefore its definition is stated:

children.text: vahnivyatireke 'pi rasagrāsīkṛtānāṃ lohānāṃ dravatvaṃ garbhadrutiḥ // RCint_3.100 //
children.translated_text: <s>Garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction) is the liquefaction of metals that have been devoured by mercury, even without the application of fire. // RCint_3.100 //
<s>Bīja</s> (seed-metal): production
The <s>saṃskāra</s> (processing) of <s>bījas</s> (seed-metals) should be done through combination with <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites) <s>sattva</s>;
by that, the internal contents of <s>Rasarāja</s> (King Mercury) liquefy through combination with the sour group. // RCint_3.101 //
<s>Bīja</s>: anonymous: production

children.text: śilayā nihato nāgastāpyaṃ vā sindhunā hatam /
children.translated_text: Lead killed with <s>śilā</s> (realgar), or <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites) killed with <s>sindhu</s> (rock salt),

children.text: tābhyāṃ tu māritaṃ bījaṃ sūtake dravati kṣaṇāt // RCint_3.102 //
children.translated_text: the <s>bīja</s> (seed-metal) prepared from both — it liquefies in mercury instantly. // RCint_3.102 //
(unclear passage)
Coated with pungent acid, alkali, cow's urine, and <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia) milk,
and bound externally with cloth, wrapped in birch-bark, and placed with the feeding,
the physician should steam it in alkali, <s>āranāla</s> (sour gruel), and urines for three days. // RCint_3.103 //
Mercury: purification after <s>jāraṇa</s>
One should wash the assimilated mercury with hot <s>āranāla</s> (sour gruel);

children.text: taṃ ca kiṃcinmale'naṣṭe gharṣayedutthite rase // RCint_3.104 //
children.translated_text: and when some impurity remains undestroyed, one should grind the risen mercury. // RCint_3.104 //

children.text: malapraviṣṭaṃ rasamalpenaiva jambharasena siktaṃ yāvadutthānaṃ gharṣayedityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Mercury that has entered the impurity should be sprinkled with a small amount of lemon juice and ground until it rises — this is the meaning.
Then there is no loss — this is the teacher's instruction. // RCint_3.105 //
<s>Jāraṇa</s>: with <s>kacchapayantra</s> (tortoise apparatus)
By this method, four feedings should be assimilated in the <s>dolā</s> (swing apparatus);
then one should assimilate mercury on fire using the <s>kacchapayantra</s> (tortoise apparatus). // RCint_3.106 //
<s>Jāraṇa</s> (assimilation)
In <s>Nandī</s>'s milk, within the cavity of a saucer, in a metal container placed therein,
<s>Harayoni</s> (mercury, born of Hara) assimilates mica, sulphur, and other substances through sealed heatings, in between. // RCint_3.107 //
The sealed heating is given with charcoal or cow-dung cakes. // RCint_3.108 //

children.text: <jāraṇa:: weight of added substances, daṇḍadhārin etc.>
children.translated_text: <s>Jāraṇa</s>: weight of added substances, <s>daṇḍadhārin</s> (staff-bearer) etc.
The first [feeding] is one sixty-fourth part; the second is one thirty-second;

children.text: tṛtīyaḥ ṣoḍaśāṃśastu caturtho 'ṣṭāṃśa eva ca // RCint_3.109 //
children.translated_text: the third is one sixteenth; and the fourth is one eighth exactly. // RCint_3.109 //
By the feeding of one sixty-fourth, the mercury becomes a <s>daṇḍadhārin</s> (staff-bearer);

children.text: jalaukāvad dvitīye tu grāsayoge sureśvari // RCint_3.110 //
children.translated_text: at the second feeding combination, it becomes like a leech, O Queen of the gods. // RCint_3.110 //
By the third feeding, it becomes like crow's droppings;

children.text: grāsena tu caturthena dadhimaṇḍasamo bhavet // RCint_3.111 //
children.translated_text: by the fourth feeding, it becomes like buttermilk whey. // RCint_3.111 //
Beyond this is not written, due to the difficulty of assimilation. // RCint_3.112 //
<s>Jāraṇa</s>: weight of added substances
The blessed <s>Govindapāda</s> writes only a <s>kalā</s>-fraction as the feeding.
Thus, having first assimilated dense <s>sattva</s> (essence) with five feedings,

children.text: garbhadrāve nipuṇo jārayati bījaṃ kalāṃśena // RCint_3.113 //
children.translated_text: one skilled in <s>garbhadrāva</s> (internal liquefaction) assimilates the <s>bīja</s> (seed-metal) in a <s>kalā</s>-fraction. // RCint_3.113 //
According to that view, the five feedings are in fractions of one sixty-fourth, one fortieth, one thirtieth, one twentieth, and one sixteenth. // RCint_3.114 //
<s>Garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction): suitable <s>kṣāras</s> (alkalis)
From the combination of lemon, <s>bījapūra</s> (citron), <s>cāṅgerī</s> (sorrel), <s>vetasa</s> (cane), and sour [substances],

children.text: kṣārā bhavanti nitarāṃ garbhadrutijāraṇe śastāḥ // RCint_3.115 //
children.translated_text: these alkalis are highly recommended for <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction) <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation). // RCint_3.115 //
Mercury: <s>rañjana</s> (coloring)
For silver-making, not much application of this is observed;

children.text: kevalaṃ nirmalaṃ tāmraṃ vāpitaṃ daradena tu /
children.translated_text: pure copper alone, when deposited with <s>darada</s> (cinnabar),

children.text: kurute triguṇaṃ jīrṇaṃ lākṣārasanibhaṃ rasam // RCint_3.116 //
children.translated_text: when assimilated threefold, makes the mercury resemble lac-juice in color. // RCint_3.116 //
Mercury: <s>rañjana</s> (coloring)
Lead killed with sulphur should be assimilated in the copper interior;

children.text: etasya triguṇe jīrṇe lākṣābho jāyate rasaḥ // RCint_3.117 //
children.translated_text: when threefold of this is assimilated, the mercury becomes lac-colored. // RCint_3.117 //
But this is a lead-based combination, not for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) purposes. // RCint_3.118 //

children.text: kiṃvā yathoktasiddhabījopari triguṇatāmrajāraṇāt tadbījaṃ samajīrṇaṃ svātantryeṇaiva rañjayati // RCint_3.119 //
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, by assimilating threefold copper on top of the properly prepared <s>bīja</s> (seed-metal), that <s>bīja</s>, when equally assimilated, produces coloring by its own power. // RCint_3.119 //
Mercury: <s>rañjana</s> (coloring)
<s>Bīja</s> (seed-metal): production
One should prepare equal powder of <s>kuṭila</s> (tin), <s>vimalā</s> (iron), and <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron/steel);

children.text: puṭitaṃ pañcavāraṃ tu tāre vāhyaṃ śanairdhamet /
children.translated_text: after heating five times, it should be gently blown upon silver,

children.text: yāvaddaśaguṇaṃ tat tu tāvadbījaṃ bhavecchubham // RCint_3.120 //
children.translated_text: until it becomes tenfold — then the excellent <s>bīja</s> (seed-metal) is formed. // RCint_3.120 //
<s>Bīja</s> (seed-metal): production

children.text: sattvaṃ tālodbhavaṃ vaṅgaṃ samaṃ kṛtvā tu dhārayet /
children.translated_text: The <s>sattva</s> (essence) of <s>tāla</s> (orpiment) and <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) should be combined in equal parts and held;

children.text: taccūrṇaṃ vāhayettāre guṇān yāvattu ṣoḍaśa // RCint_3.121 //
children.translated_text: that powder should be driven into silver, up to sixteen times. // RCint_3.121 //
This <s>pratibīja</s> (counter-seed) is the best; it is the binding agent for mercury;
through <s>cāraṇa</s> (mobilizing) and <s>sāraṇa</s> (extraction), it transmutes at a thousandth part. // RCint_3.122 //
<s>Bīja</s>: producing <s>śatavedhī</s> (hundred-transmuting) mercury
One should drive <s>vaṅgābhra</s> (tin-mica alloy) into silver exactly twelve times;

children.text: etadbīje same jīrṇe śatavedhī bhavedrasaḥ // RCint_3.123 //
children.translated_text: when this <s>bīja</s> is assimilated equally, the mercury becomes <s>śatavedhī</s> (hundred-transmuting). // RCint_3.123 //
<s>Bīja</s>: <s>hemabīja</s> (gold seed-metal)
By <s>kunaṭī</s>-killed <s>kariṇa</s>, or by <s>ravi</s> (Calotropis), or by <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites) and sulphur-killed [metals],

children.text: daradanihatāsinā vā trir vyūḍhaṃ hema tadbījam // RCint_3.124 //
children.translated_text: or by <s>darada</s> (cinnabar)-killed iron — gold overcome thrice becomes that <s>bīja</s> (seed-metal). // RCint_3.124 //
Even plain <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) overcomes it when the potency-substance is strong.
<s>Bīja</s>: producing <s>rasabandhana</s> (mercury-binding)
One should drive <s>nāgābhra</s> (lead-mica alloy) into gold exactly twelve times;

children.text: pratibījamidaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ pāradasya tu bandhanam // RCint_3.125 //
children.translated_text: this <s>pratibīja</s> (counter-seed) is the best; it is for the binding of mercury. // RCint_3.125 //
<s>Nāgabīja</s> (lead seed-metal)

children.text: mākṣikeṇa hataṃ tāmraṃ nāgaṃ ca rañjayenmuhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Copper killed with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrites) should repeatedly color lead;

children.text: taṃ nāgaṃ vāhayedbīje dviṣoḍaśaguṇāni ca // RCint_3.126 //
children.translated_text: that lead should be driven into the <s>bīja</s>, thirty-two times. // RCint_3.126 //

children.text: bījaṃ tv idaṃ varaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ nāgabījaṃ prakīrtitam /
children.translated_text: This is the excellent and supreme <s>bīja</s>, known as <s>nāgabīja</s> (lead seed-metal);
merely by being mobilized equally, it transmutes at a thousandth part. // RCint_3.127 //
<s>Bīja</s>: coloring of seed-metals
<s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s> (madder), <s>kiṃśuka</s> (Butea flowers), <s>khadira</s> (catechu), <s>raktacandana</s> (red sandalwood),
<s>karavīra</s> (oleander), <s>devadāru</s> (deodar cedar), <s>sarala</s> (pine), and the two <s>rajanīs</s> (turmeric and dāruharidrā), // RCint_3.128 //
and other red-flowered [plants], ground with lac-juice,
sesame should be cooked with them, and the coloring of <s>bīja</s> and other [substances] should be done thereby. // RCint_3.129 //
<s>Sāraṇātaila</s> (extraction oil): production
In a decoction of double the amount of red-flowered and red-yellow groups,

children.text: kvāthe caturguṇaṃ kṣīraṃ tailamekaṃ sureśvari // RCint_3.130 //
children.translated_text: fourfold milk, and one part oil, O Queen of the gods, // RCint_3.130 //
derived from <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> (Celastrus), <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia), and bitter gourd,
with the juices of <s>pāṭalā</s> (Stereospermum), <s>kākatuṇḍā</s>, and <s>mahārāṣṭrī</s> separately, // RCint_3.131 //
combined with fats of frog, boar, ram, snake, fish, tortoise, and leech —

children.text: vasayā caikayā yuktaṃ ṣoḍaśāṃśaiḥ supeṣitaiḥ // RCint_3.132 //
children.translated_text: one of each, with one-sixteenth parts well ground, // RCint_3.132 //
with <s>bhūlatā</s> (a creeper), <s>māla</s>, <s>mākṣīka</s> (pyrites), and the <s>dvandvamelāpaka</s> (paired-combination) herbs,
cooked and strained — this is called <s>sāraṇātaila</s> (extraction oil). // RCint_3.133 //
Here, <s>gandharva</s> (castor) oil is also [used], according to the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s> text. // RCint_3.134 //
Wool, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), <s>girijatu</s> (shilajit), buffalo ear-wax, <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal insects), and crabs — these are the <s>dvandvamelāpaka</s> herbs. // RCint_3.135 //
<s>Dvandvamelāpaka</s> (paired-combination herbs)
"Coloring oil" (<s>rañjakataila</s>)
With available white flowers from various trees,
fourfold juice should be combined within <s>kaṅguṇī</s> (Celastrus) oil. // RCint_3.136 //
One should cook until only the oil remains; in that oil one should immerse

children.text: drāvitaṃ tārabījaṃ tu hy ekaviṃśativārakam // RCint_3.137 //
children.translated_text: the melted silver <s>bīja</s> (seed-metal) twenty-one times. // RCint_3.137 //
It becomes colored — that is the coloring of <s>Rasarāja</s> (King Mercury).

children.text: kuṭile balam atyadhikaṃ rāgastīkṣṇe ca pannage snehaḥ /
children.translated_text: In <s>kuṭila</s> (tin) there is exceptional potency, in <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron) color, and in <s>pannaga</s> (lead) lubrication;

children.text: rāgasnehabalāni tu kamale nityaṃ praśaṃsanti // RCint_3.138 //
children.translated_text: but in <s>kamala</s> (copper), color, lubrication, and potency are always praised together. // RCint_3.138 //
Potency resides in mica <s>sattva</s>; coloring properties are established in <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron);
binding is in <s>sāra</s> (steel), and <s>krāmaṇa</s> (progressive pervasion) goes through lead and tin. // RCint_3.139 //

children.text: krāmati tīkṣṇena rasastīkṣṇena ca jīryate grāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: Mercury pervades through <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron), and through <s>tīkṣṇa</s> the feeding is assimilated;

children.text: hemno yonistīkṣṇaṃ rāgān gṛhṇāti tīkṣṇena // RCint_3.140 //
children.translated_text: <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is the womb of gold — it takes on colors through <s>tīkṣṇa</s>. // RCint_3.140 //

children.text: tadapi ca daradena hataṃ kṛtvā vā mākṣikeṇa ravisahitam /
children.translated_text: That [iron] too, having been killed with <s>darada</s> (cinnabar) or combined with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrites) and <s>ravi</s> (sun-plant),

children.text: vāsitamapi vāsanayā ghanavaccāryaṃ ca jāryaṃ ca // RCint_3.141 //
children.translated_text: or treated by <s>vāsanā</s> (impregnation) — it should be mobilized and assimilated like dense [gold]. // RCint_3.141 //
Mercury: <s>bandhana</s> (binding)

children.text: sarvair ebhir lauhair mākṣikamṛditair drutaistathā garbhe /
children.translated_text: With all these metals, ground with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrites) and liquefied internally,

children.text: viḍayogena ca jīrṇe rasarājo bandham upayāti // RCint_3.142 //
children.translated_text: and assimilated with <s>viḍa</s> preparation, <s>Rasarāja</s> (King Mercury) attains binding. // RCint_3.142 //
(unclear passage)
Without <s>bīja</s>: when equally assimilated, with a quarter less, one-sixteenth part;

children.text: ardhena pādakanakaṃ pādenaikena tulyakanakaṃ ca // RCint_3.143 //
children.translated_text: with half [assimilation], quarter-gold; with one quarter, equal gold. // RCint_3.143 //
Mercury that has assimilated equal or more becomes fit for <s>sāraṇa</s> (extraction) and capable of hundredfold transmutation;
for mercury with lesser assimilation, only <s>patralepa</s> (leaf-coating) and <s>ardhakāra</s> (half-work) are possible. // RCint_3.144 //
<s>Patralepa</s> (leaf-coating)
A thoroughly cleaned leaf of silver-antimony or similar, made very acidic,

children.text: ālipya rasena tataḥ krāmaṇaliptaṃ puṭeṣu viśrāntam // RCint_3.145 //
children.translated_text: coated with mercury, then coated with <s>krāmaṇa</s> (pervasion) agent, and rested through sealed heatings. // RCint_3.145 //
The sealed heating is generally given below the <s>cullikā</s> (furnace). // RCint_3.146 //
<s>Puṭa</s> (sealed heating) method
<s>Varṇapuṭa</s> (color-heating)

children.text: ardhena miśrayitvā hemnā śreṣṭhena taddalaṃ puṭitam /
children.translated_text: Mixing with half quantity of the best gold, that leaf is subjected to sealed heating;
with <s>kṣitikhaga</s>, pungent substance, red clay — this color-heating should then be given. // RCint_3.147 //
'With half' is used as a general indication [other proportions are also possible]. // RCint_3.148 //
Gold: production
Silver, <s>arka</s> (sun-plant), monkey-head [plant], realgar, and sulphur should be powdered;

children.text: pacedbhūyaḥ kṣipan gandhaṃ yathā sūto na gacchati /
children.translated_text: one should cook repeatedly, adding sulphur so that the mercury does not escape;
when cooked and placed on a gold leaf, it attains the nature of gold. // RCint_3.149 //
(unclear passage)
With ropes of frog-dye and other [substances], between two pillars of <s>sāra</s> (steel),
the mercury-elephant is bound by the technique bestowed by the glorious <s>Guru</s>. // RCint_3.150 //
Gold: production
Four [types of] realgar, sulphur, and the Lord [of mercury] — in a glass flask they produce gold;
the preparation is made of molasses and iron, with the addition of chalk and salt. // RCint_3.151 //
Gold: production (?)
<s>Maṇḍūka</s> (frog-mineral), mercury, realgar, and iron in equal parts, ground with snake tongues (a plant),

children.text: yantrottamena gurubhiḥ pratipāditena svalpairdinairiha patati na vismayadhvam // RCint_3.152 //
children.translated_text: in the best apparatus taught by the teachers — in a few days it falls [as gold]; do not be astonished! // RCint_3.152 //

children.text:
<bīja:: lauhabheki>
lohaṃ gandhaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ bhrāmayitvā tenonmiśraṃ bhekam āvartayettu /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bīja</s>: <s>lauhabhekī</s> (iron-frog)
Iron, sulphur, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) are fused together; with that mixture, the <s>bheka</s> (frog-mineral) should be revolved;

children.text: tālaṃ kṛtvā turyavaṅgāntarāle rūpyasyāntastacca siddhoktabīje // RCint_3.153 //
children.translated_text: making <s>tāla</s> (orpiment) within a quarter portion of <s>vaṅga</s> (tin), placed inside silver — and that in the <s>bīja</s> taught by the <s>Siddhas</s>. // RCint_3.153 //
<s>Bīja</s>: <s>tāratālakī</s> (silver-orpiment)
Thus these two <s>bījas</s> — <s>lauhabhekī</s> (iron-frog) and <s>tāratālakī</s> (silver-orpiment) — are taught in the <s>Siddha</s> tradition. // RCint_3.154 //
(unclear passage)
Melted <s>dardura</s> (frog-mineral), <s>pūtilauha</s> (purified iron), and <s>tāpa</s> (heat) produce pieces of <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar) and wing-pieces;
moon, sun, gold, and <s>mūṣikā</s> (mouse-mineral) surely yield wealth for the intelligent, by this method. // RCint_3.155 //
Mercury (?): stabilization

children.text: daradaguṭikāś candrakṣodair nirantaram āvṛtās taraṇikanakaiḥ kiṃvā gandhāśmanā saha bhūriṇā /
children.translated_text: <s>Darada</s> (cinnabar) pills, continuously coated with silver and gold powder, or with abundant sulphur and stone,

children.text: racaya sikatāyantre yuktyā muhur muhur ityasau hutabhuji vasanna sthemānaṃ kathañcana muñcati // RCint_3.156 //
children.translated_text: placed skillfully in a <s>sikatāyantra</s> (sand-bath) again and again, dwelling in fire — it does not in any way lose its stability. // RCint_3.156 //

children.text:
<bāhyadruti>
atha bāhyadrutayaḥ /
etāstu kevalamāroṭameva militā nibadhnanti /
phalamasya kalpapramitamāyuḥ /

children.translated_text: Or, when assimilated through the previously described feeding sequence, they bestow the previously described fruits.

children.text: ucyate sa samajīrṇaścāyaṃ śatavedhī dviguṇajīrṇaḥ sahasravedhī /
children.translated_text: It is said that mercury equally assimilated is <s>śatavedhī</s> (hundred-transmuting); when doubly assimilated, <s>sahasravedhī</s> (thousand-transmuting);
thus <s>lakṣa</s>- (hundred-thousand), <s>ayuta</s>- (ten-thousand), and <s>koṭivedhī</s> (ten-million transmuting) should be understood accordingly.
Mercury that has assimilated sixty-four times transmutes even by smoke, touch, sight, and sound. // RCint_3.157 //

<s>Bāhyadruti</s> (external liquefaction)
Now the external liquefactions:
These, when combined merely with <s>āroṭa</s> (sublimate), effect binding.
The fruit of this is a lifespan measured by a cosmic age.
<s>Sāraṇa</s> (extraction): proper crucible
A blind crucible should be made, resembling the shape of a cow's teat,

children.text: saiva chidrānvitā madhye gambhīrā sāraṇocitā // RCint_3.158 //
children.translated_text: the same with a hole in the middle, deep — suitable for <s>sāraṇa</s> (extraction). // RCint_3.158 //

children.text:
<sāraṇa:: procedure>
asyāmeva mūṣāyāṃ tattailamapagatakalkavimalamāpūrya tasminnadhikam ūṣmātmani drutabījaprakṣepasamakālameva samāvartanīyaḥ sūtavarastadanu sadyo mūṣānanam ācchādanīyam etat tailāktapaṭakhaṇḍagranthibandhena aruṇasitabījābhyām amunā sāraṇakarmaṇā militaścetsāritaḥ samyak saṃyamitaśca vijñeyaḥ pratisāritastu dviguṇabījena tadvadanusāritastu triguṇabījena atra trividhāyāmeva sāraṇāyāmaruṇasitakarmaṇoḥ krāmaṇārtham īṣatpannagavaṅgau viśrāṇanīyāviti /
children.translated_text:
<s>Sāraṇa</s>: procedure
In this very crucible, that oil, free from residue and clear, should be filled; in that exceedingly hot [crucible], simultaneously with casting the melted <s>bīja</s> (seed-metal), the excellent mercury should be stirred in; then immediately the mouth of the crucible should be covered with a cloth-piece tied in a knot soaked in oil, with red and white <s>bījas</s>. If the mercury has combined through this <s>sāraṇa</s> process, it is properly extracted and well controlled. If it needs re-extraction, use double the <s>bīja</s>; if it needs further re-extraction, use triple the <s>bīja</s>. In these three types of <s>sāraṇa</s>, for the red and white operations, a little lead and tin should be added for the purpose of <s>krāmaṇa</s> (pervasion).
Producing <s>koṭivedhī</s> (ten-million transmuting) mercury
Extracted, then assimilated, then again extracted and assimilated —
through the sequence of seven chains, the mercury becomes <s>koṭivedhī</s> (ten-million transmuting);

children.text: ityādīni karmāṇi punaḥ kevalamīśvarānugrahasādhyatvānna prapañcitāni // RCint_3.159 //
children.translated_text: such further operations are not elaborated upon, as they are achievable only through the grace of the Lord. // RCint_3.159 //

children.text: śilayā nihato nāgo vaṅgaṃ vā tālakena śuddhena /
children.translated_text: Lead killed with <s>śilā</s> (realgar), or <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) with pure <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment),
successively in yellow and white — this is designated as <s>krāmaṇa</s> (progressive pervasion). // RCint_3.160 //
<s>Viḍavaṭī</s> (viḍa pills)
A <s>khoṭaka</s> (impure alloy) equal to gold should be revolved equally;

children.text: mākṣikaṃ kāntapāṣāṇaṃ śilāgandhaṃ samaṃ samam // RCint_3.161 //
children.translated_text: <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrites), <s>kāntapāṣāṇa</s> (magnetite), realgar, and sulphur in equal parts, // RCint_3.161 //
ground with earthworms for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours), formed into pills the size of a <s>valla</s> (berry);

children.text: eṣā viḍavaṭī khyātā yojyā sarvatra jāraṇe // RCint_3.162 //
children.translated_text: this is the renowned <s>viḍavaṭī</s> — it should be used everywhere in <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation). // RCint_3.162 //
Mercury: <s>rañjana</s> (coloring) producing <s>śatavedhin</s> (hundred-transmuting mercury)
<s>Darada</s> (cinnabar), <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrites), sulphur, <s>rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli), coral,

children.text: śilātutthaṃ ca kuṅkuṣṭhaṃ samacūrṇaṃ prakalpayet // RCint_3.163 //
children.translated_text: realgar, <s>tuttha</s> (copper sulphate), and <s>kuṅkuṣṭha</s> — these should be prepared in equal powder. // RCint_3.163 //
With both the yellow and red groups, together with <s>kaṅguṇī</s> (Celastrus) oil,

children.text: bhāvayeddivasān pañca sūryatāpe punaḥ punaḥ // RCint_3.164 //
children.translated_text: it should be treated in sunlight for five days, again and again. // RCint_3.164 //
The assimilated mercury-alloy, combined with this paste,
placed in the middle of a sand-bath pot, inside a saucer for sealed heating, // RCint_3.165 //

children.text: tridinaṃ pācayeccullyāṃ kalko deyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: should be cooked in a furnace for three days, with the paste added repeatedly;

children.text: rañjito jāyate sūtaḥ śatavedhī na saṃśayaḥ // RCint_3.166 //
children.translated_text: the mercury becomes colored — it is <s>śatavedhī</s> (hundred-transmuting), without doubt. // RCint_3.166 //
Mercury: <s>rañjana</s> (coloring) (?)

children.text: lauhaṃ gandhaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ dhmātametat tulyaṃ cūrṇair bhānubhekāhivaṅgaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Iron, sulphur, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), fused together — these equal in powder with <s>bhānu</s> (sun-plant), <s>bheka</s> (frog-mineral), <s>ahi</s> (snake-plant), and <s>vaṅga</s> (tin);

children.text: sūtaṃ gandhaṃ sarvasāmyena kūpyāmīṣatsādhyaṃ cātra no vismayadhvam // RCint_3.167 //
children.translated_text: mercury and sulphur in equal parts in a flask — this is easily accomplished; do not be astonished! // RCint_3.167 //
<s>Hemakṛṣṭi</s> (gold-attracting preparation): production
With mercury, <s>darada</s> (cinnabar), <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites), sulphur, and <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) in progressively increasing amounts,
copper that has been killed by sealed heating, driven into silver thrice — this is the <s>hemakṛṣṭi</s> (gold-attracting preparation). // RCint_3.168 //
<s>Śatāṃśavidhi</s> (hundredth-part method) (1)
Ninety-eight parts of silver, one part of gold,

children.text: sūtaikena ca vedhaḥ syācchatāṃśavidhir īritaḥ // RCint_3.169 //
children.translated_text: and transmutation by one part of mercury — this is called the <s>śatāṃśavidhi</s> (hundredth-part method). // RCint_3.169 //
<s>Śatāṃśavidhi</s> (hundredth-part method) (2)
