Forty-nine parts of the moon (silver), the same of pure sun-metal (<s>bhāsvata</s>),
one part of fire (copper), one part of <s>Śambhu</s> (mercury) — this is called the <s>śatāṃśavidhi</s>. // RCint_3.170 //
The two [methods] are treated as having silver-source and copper-source respectively;
thus <s>sahasravedha</s> (thousand-transmutation) and higher should be understood according to the <s>jāraṇa</s> and <s>bīja</s> used. // RCint_3.171 //
<s>Vedhavidhāna</s> (transmutation procedure)
Four <s>prativāpas</s> (counter-additions), with a well-observed [crucible] treated with fish bile,

children.text: tāre vā śulbe vā tārāriṣṭe'thavā kṛṣṭau // RCint_3.172 //
children.translated_text: in silver, or in copper, or in the silver-antimony [alloy], or in <s>kṛṣṭi</s> (gold-extract), // RCint_3.172 //
thereafter, ground with <s>krāmaṇa</s> agent, wrapped in beeswax, should be added;

children.text: atividrute ca tasmin vedho'sau kuntavedhena // RCint_3.173 //
children.translated_text: and when it is thoroughly melted, that transmutation is by the <s>kuntavedha</s> (lance-thrust) method. // RCint_3.173 //

children.text: tadanu siddhatailenāplāvya bhasmāvachādanapūrvakam avatārya svāṅgaśaityaparyantam apekṣitavyamiti // RCint_3.174 //
children.translated_text: Thereafter, immersing it in <s>siddha</s>-oil (accomplished oil) and covering with ashes, one should remove it and wait until it cools naturally. // RCint_3.174 //
The substance transmuted by mercury should be kept in the ground for half a fortnight (seven days);

children.text: tata ānīya nagare vikrīṇīta vicakṣaṇaḥ // RCint_3.175 //
children.translated_text: then bringing it to the city, the discerning one should sell it. // RCint_3.175 //
Selling factitious gold/silver
<s>Bubhukṣitavidhi</s> (hunger-inducing method)
Mercury placed within a hollow of <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt) chunk, made into a <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste), in a <s>sikatāyantra</s> (sand-bath apparatus),
with purified sulphur and other substances, by gentle fire — the offspring of the Lord consumes all that is to be consumed. // RCint_3.176 //
<s>Rañjana</s> (coloring) (??)

children.text: karṣāṣṭaṅkaṇakañjalīharirasair gandhasya ca dvau rajaḥ siddhākhyaṃ sakalaiḥ kṛtaṃ palamatha dvitraiśca lohaiḥ śritam /
children.translated_text: Three <s>karṣas</s> of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), <s>kajjalī</s> (black sulphide), <s>Hari</s>'s mercury, two <s>rajas</s> (parts) of sulphur — all this combined into one <s>pala</s>, called <s>siddha</s> (accomplished), then treated with two or three metals,

children.text: bhūyo gandhayutaṃ caturdaśapuṭaiḥ syādindragopāruṇaṃ tattāre laghunā puṭena dhamanenārkachavīm īhate // RCint_3.177 //
children.translated_text: again combined with sulphur, through fourteen sealed heatings it becomes red like an <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal insect); that, in silver, with a light sealed heating and blowing, assumes the luster of the sun. // RCint_3.177 //
'<s>Karṣās</s>' in the plural means three.
The operation of this is threefold, by <s>patralepa</s> (leaf-coating) — this should be known. // RCint_3.178 //
Gold: production

children.text: tulyaṃ tāraṃ tāmram ādāya svacchaṃ tāvattaptaṃ gandhacūrṇe kunaṭyām /
children.translated_text: Taking equal parts of pure silver and copper, heated repeatedly in sulphur powder and <s>kunaṭī</s>,

children.text: nyastaṃ yāvajjīryate khaṇḍaśo'tha prājyairgādhaiḥ pācayetkācakūpyām // RCint_3.179 //
children.translated_text: placed until it is assimilated in pieces, then cook abundantly and deeply in a glass flask. // RCint_3.179 //
That piece-like [substance] with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), placed inside gold within the interior of an ash-crucible,

children.text: dhmātaṃ sādhu syātsuvarṇaṃ satāraṃ hīne varṇe rañjayenmākṣikeṇa // RCint_3.180 //
children.translated_text: when properly blown, becomes gold with silver; if the color is deficient, one should color it with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrites). // RCint_3.180 //
Copper: preparing a <s>dravīkāraka</s> (liquefying agent)
If <s>darada</s> (cinnabar) combined with <s>tāla</s> (orpiment), copper, realgar, and sulphur

children.text: kūpikāyāṃ muhuḥ pakvaṃ dravakāri tadā matam // RCint_3.181 //
children.translated_text: is repeatedly cooked in a flask, then it is considered a liquefying agent. // RCint_3.181 //
<s>Kṣetrīkaraṇa</s> (preparation of the bodily field)
A body that has been oleated, steamed, purged, and made disease-free with proven medicines —
this is briefly the 'field' fit for the sowing of the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) and <s>bīja</s> (seed-metal). // RCint_3.182 //
The five procedures (<s>pañcakarma</s>)

children.text: snigdhaṃ prātastridinaṃ ghṛtasaindhavapānena svinnaṃ vastrādipuṭavahninā viriktam icchābhedinā vāntaṃ vacādirasena palāśabījaviḍaṅgaguḍamodakabhakṣaṇāt kīṭapātanam api kartavyam /
children.translated_text: Oleation is done by drinking ghee with rock salt for three mornings; steaming is done by fire wrapped in cloth and similar coverings; purgation is done with a chosen purgative; emesis is done with the juice of <s>vacā</s> (sweet flag) and similar substances; and elimination of intestinal worms should also be done through eating balls of <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) seeds, <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia), and jaggery.

children.text: nīrujaṃ saṃvatsaramayanaṃ vā pariśodhitaiḥ śṛṅgārābhralakṣmīvilāsādyabhrasattvapradhānaprayogair iti // RCint_3.183 //
children.translated_text: Making the body disease-free for a year or a season, with preparations primarily of mica <s>sattva</s> such as <s>Śṛṅgārābhralakṣmīvilāsa</s> and similar formulations. // RCint_3.183 //
One should drink a decoction of <s>nimba</s> (neem) with ash-mercury and <s>vacā</s> (sweet flag) powder;

children.text: pītāntaṃ vamanaṃ tena jāyate kleśavarjitam // RCint_3.184 //
children.translated_text: after drinking until yellow, emesis thereby occurs without distress. // RCint_3.184 //
For those delicate persons frightened by the five procedures,
this should be taken after purgation, for the removal of all <s>doṣas</s> (humoral imbalances). // RCint_3.185 //
Without <s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s> (field preparation), even killed mercury acts like poison;
how can it yield fruit? — like a good seed in barren soil. // RCint_3.186 //

children.text: akṛte kṣetrīkaraṇe rasāyanaṃ yo naraḥ prayuñjīta /
children.translated_text: A person who uses <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) without performing <s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>,

children.text: tasya krāmati na rasaḥ sarvāṅgadoṣakṛdbhavati // RCint_3.187 //
children.translated_text: mercury does not pervade his [body]; it becomes the cause of defects in all limbs. // RCint_3.187 //
<s>Kṣetrakaraṇa</s> (field preparation) must be done in every <s>rasāyana</s> treatment;

children.text: na kṣetrakaraṇāddevi kiṃcit kuryād rasāyanam // RCint_3.188 //
children.translated_text: without <s>kṣetrakaraṇa</s>, O <s>Devī</s>, no <s>rasāyana</s> should be administered at all. // RCint_3.188 //
Thus purified and strengthened, with rice, wild-meat, and <s>mudga</s> (green gram) soups,
the wise person whose body has been field-prepared should undertake <s>rasāyana</s>. // RCint_3.189 //
The discerning one should first consume killed mica for one month;
thereafter it should be applied to the body by one who desires field-preparation. // RCint_3.190 //
Mercury assimilated with a quarter of dense <s>sattva</s> (essence), half of <s>kānta</s> (magnetite), and equal <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron),

children.text: kṣetrīkaraṇāya rasaḥ prayujyate bhūya ārogyāya // RCint_3.191 //
children.translated_text: is used for <s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s> (field preparation), and further for health. // RCint_3.191 //
That which has attained fire-resistance and has become capable of making gold and silver,

children.text: śuddho rasaśca bhuktau vidhinā siddhiprado bhavati // RCint_3.192 //
children.translated_text: such purified mercury, when consumed according to the prescribed method, bestows perfection. // RCint_3.192 //
Mercury: assimilated: correct dosage
For mercury that has assimilated dense <s>sattva</s>, <s>kānta</s> (magnetite), copper, <s>saṅkara</s> (mixed metal), <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron), etc.,

children.text: sūtasya guñjāvṛddhyā māṣakamātraṃ parā mātrā // RCint_3.193 //
children.translated_text: the supreme dosage is one <s>māṣaka</s> (bean-weight), increasing by a <s>guñjā</s> (berry-weight) at a time. // RCint_3.193 //

children.text: guñjāmātraṃ rasaṃ devi hemajīrṇaṃ tu bhakṣayet /
children.translated_text: One should consume mercury assimilated with gold in a <s>guñjā</s> (berry-weight) dose, O <s>Devī</s>;

children.text: dviguṇaṃ tārajīrṇasya ravijīrṇasya ca trayam // RCint_3.194 //
children.translated_text: double that for silver-assimilated, and triple for sun-metal-assimilated. // RCint_3.194 //
For <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron), mica, and <s>kānta</s> (magnetite), one <s>māṣa</s> (bean-weight) is generally declared as the dose;
diamond and <s>vaikrānta</s>-assimilated [mercury] should be consumed in a mustard-seed amount. // RCint_3.195 //
Mercury bound with lead, tin, and similar [metals], or bound with poison and sub-poisons,
or forcibly bound with urine and semen — these should be rejected in the <s>rasāyana</s> regimen. // RCint_3.196 //
Mercury: assimilated: longevity
From consuming one <s>pala</s> of ash from iron-assimilated [mercury], one attains a hundred-thousand-year lifespan;
thus, having consumed ten <s>palas</s> of iron-assimilated [mercury], a human

children.text: tadā jīvenmahākalpaṃ pralayānte śivaṃ vrajet // RCint_3.197 //
children.translated_text: shall live for a great cosmic age, and at the end of dissolution, attain <s>Śiva</s>. // RCint_3.197 //
From consuming one <s>pala</s> of ash from copper-assimilated [mercury], one attains a hundred-thousand-year lifespan;
ten-million-year lifespan, the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>, that of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the life of <s>Rudra</s>,
and in the second, third, fourth, fifth, and sixth [palas], the Lord's lifespan of great cosmic ages. // RCint_3.198 //
From consuming one <s>pala</s> of ash from gold-assimilated [mercury], one attains a hundred-thousand-year lifespan;
and with two, three, and four [<s>palas</s>], one attains the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>. // RCint_3.199 //
Knowing a <s>guñjā</s>-measure of gold-assimilated [mercury], and knowing the strength or weakness of the digestive fire,

children.text: ghṛtena madhunā cādyāttāmbūlaṃ kāminīṃ tyajet // RCint_3.200 //
children.translated_text: one should take it with ghee and honey; and should avoid betel and women. // RCint_3.200 //

children.text: eko hi doṣaḥ sūkṣmo'sti bhakṣite bhasmasūtake /
children.translated_text: There is indeed one subtle defect when ash-mercury is consumed:
within three weeks, upon mounting an excellent woman, the man becomes blinded by desire. // RCint_3.201 //
Without the company of women, O <s>Devī</s>, indigestion arises for him;
but if semen is discharged through intercourse, there arises danger to life. // RCint_3.202 //

children.text: yuvatyā jalpanaṃ kāryaṃ tāvattanmaithunaṃ tyajet // RCint_3.203 //
children.translated_text: One should only converse with a young woman; that intercourse should be avoided. // RCint_3.203 //

children.text: brahmacaryeṇa vā yogī sadā seveta sūtakam /
children.translated_text: Or, with <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), the yogin should always consume mercury;

children.text: samādhikaraṇaṃ tasya krāmaṇaṃ paramaṃ matam // RCint_3.204 //
children.translated_text: complete concentration upon it — that is considered the supreme <s>krāmaṇa</s> (pervasion). // RCint_3.204 //
One should consume mercury in the morning; wholesome food [should be taken] after two <s>yāmas</s> (six hours);

children.text: na laṅghayet triyāmaṃ tu madhyāhne caiva bhojayet // RCint_3.205 //
children.translated_text: one should not fast for three <s>yāmas</s> (nine hours); at midday one should eat. // RCint_3.205 //
Having eaten <s>amṛtā</s> (Tinospora) with <s>kaṇā</s> (long pepper), one should sleep at night after bowel movements;

children.text: tāmbūlāntargate sūte kiṭṭabandho na jāyate // RCint_3.206 //
children.translated_text: when mercury is placed within betel, binding with slag does not occur. // RCint_3.206 //
Mercury: ingestion: rules of conduct
Excessive drinking, excessive eating, excessive sleeping, wakefulness,

children.text: strīṇām atiprasaṅgaṃ cāpyadhvānaṃ ca vivarjayet // RCint_3.207 //
children.translated_text: excessive association with women, and excessive traveling — these should be avoided. // RCint_3.207 //
Excessive anger, excessive joy, excessive sorrow, excessive desire,

children.text: śuṣkavādaṃ jalakrīḍām aticintāṃ ca varjayet // RCint_3.208 //
children.translated_text: dry debates, water-sports, and excessive worry — these should be avoided. // RCint_3.208 //
The eight 'K'-items (<s>kakārāṣṭaka</s>)
<s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> (winter melon), <s>karkaṭī</s> (cucumber), <s>kaliṅga</s> (watermelon), <s>kāravellaka</s> (bitter gourd),

children.text: kusumbhikāṃ ca karkoṭīṃ kadalīṃ kākamācikām // RCint_3.209 //
children.translated_text: <s>kusumbhikā</s> (safflower), <s>karkoṭī</s> (spiny gourd), <s>kadalī</s> (banana), and <s>kākamācikā</s> (Solanum nigrum) — // RCint_3.209 //
these eight items beginning with 'ka' should be avoided by the consumer of mercury;

children.text: pātakaṃ ca na kartavyaṃ paśusaṅgaṃ ca varjayet // RCint_3.210 //
children.translated_text: sinful acts should not be committed, and contact with animals should be avoided. // RCint_3.210 //

children.text: catuṣpathe na gantavyaṃ viṇmūtraṃ ca na laṅghayet /
children.translated_text: One should not go to crossroads, and should not step over feces or urine;

children.text: dhīrāṇāṃ nindanaṃ devi strīṇāṃ nindāṃ ca varjayet // RCint_3.211 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Devī</s>, disparaging the wise and disparaging women should be avoided. // RCint_3.211 //
One should speak truthfully; unpleasant words should not be spoken;
horse gram, sesame oil, tila (sesame), <s>māṣa</s> (black gram), and lentils, // RCint_3.212 //

children.text: kapotān kāñjikaṃ caiva takrabhaktaṃ ca varjayet /
children.translated_text: pigeons, <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel), buttermilk-rice — these should be avoided;
<s>Hemacandra</s> and others say that chicken should also be avoided. // RCint_3.213 //
Pungent, sour, bitter, salty, pitta-aggravating, and vāta-aggravating foods,

children.text: badaraṃ nārikelaṃ ca sahakāraṃ suvarcalam // RCint_3.214 //
children.translated_text: jujube, coconut, mango, and <s>suvarcala</s> (sochal salt), // RCint_3.214 //
orange, <s>kāmaraṅga</s> (star fruit), and <s>śobhāñjana</s> (drumstick) — these should be rejected;

children.text: na vādajalpanaṃ kuryāddivā cāpi na paryaṭet // RCint_3.215 //
children.translated_text: one should not engage in disputatious talk, nor wander about during the day. // RCint_3.215 //
One should not eat temple offerings; camphor should always be avoided;

children.text: kuṅkumālepanaṃ varjyaṃ na svapetkuśalaḥ kṣitau // RCint_3.216 //
children.translated_text: saffron application should be avoided; the wise person should not sleep on the ground. // RCint_3.216 //

children.text: na ca hanyātkumārīṃ ca mātulānīṃ ca varjayet /
children.translated_text: One should not harm a young girl, and should avoid one's maternal aunt;

children.text: kṣudhārto naiva tiṣṭheta hyajīrṇaṃ naiva kārayet /
children.translated_text: one should not remain hungry, nor cause indigestion;
one should recite mantras day and night, and should not speak untruthful words. // RCint_3.217 //
Beneficial foods are: <s>mudga</s> (green gram) with rice, milk, ghee, and rice —  always with care;

children.text: śākaṃ paunarnavaṃ devi meghanādaṃ savāstukam // RCint_3.218 //
children.translated_text: vegetables of <s>punarnavā</s>, O <s>Devī</s>, <s>meghanāda</s> (a plant), and <s>vāstuka</s> (Chenopodium); // RCint_3.218 //
<s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), <s>nāgara</s> (dry ginger), <s>mustā</s> (Cyperus), and lotus roots should be eaten;

children.text: ātmajñānaṃ kathā pūjā śivasya ca viśeṣataḥ // RCint_3.219 //
children.translated_text: self-knowledge, discourse, worship — especially of <s>Śiva</s>. // RCint_3.219 //
These rules, O blessed one, should not be violated while consuming mercury;

children.text: evaṃ caiva mahāvyādhīn rase'jīrṇe tu lakṣayet // RCint_3.220 //
children.translated_text: thus, when mercury remains undigested, one should observe these great diseases. // RCint_3.220 //
<s>Rasājīrṇaśamana</s> (treatment of mercury indigestion)
One <s>karṣa</s> of <s>svarjikakṣāra</s> (soda ash), soaked in <s>kāravellī</s> (bitter gourd) juice,

children.text: gomūtraṃ saindhavayutaṃ tasya saṃsrāvaṇaṃ param // RCint_3.221 //
children.translated_text: cow's urine with rock salt — this is the supreme evacuant for it. // RCint_3.221 //
<s>Sindhu</s> (rock salt), <s>karkoṭī</s> (spiny gourd), and cow's urine, soaked in bitter gourd juice,
combined with <s>sauvarcala</s> (sochal salt) — the wise one suffering from mercury indigestion should drink this. // RCint_3.222 //

children.text: śarapuṅkhāṃ suradālīṃ paṭolabījaṃ ca kākamācīṃ ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Śarapuṅkhā</s> (Tephrosia), <s>suradālī</s> (a plant), <s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd) seeds, and <s>kākamācī</s> (Solanum nigrum) —

children.text: ekatamāṃ tu kvathitām avijīrṇarasāyane tu pibet // RCint_3.223 //
children.translated_text: one should drink any one of these, boiled, in cases of mercury <s>rasāyana</s> indigestion. // RCint_3.223 //
If somehow, through ignorance, mercury tainted with lead and other [impurities] is consumed,
the knowledgeable one should drink the juice of <s>kāravella</s> (bitter gourd) shoots to evacuate it. // RCint_3.224 //
The wise one should prepare varied and wholesome meals, avoiding forbidden items,

children.text: sravati na yathā rasendro na ca naśyati jāṭharo vahniḥ // RCint_3.225 //
children.translated_text: so that mercury does not flow out, and the digestive fire is not extinguished. // RCint_3.225 //
Prepare alkali from alkali-yielding plants methodically and with care;

with <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol) and <s>svarjikā</s> (soda ash), and with the pungent, collected juices of <s>āraka</s>, <s>kṣapā</s> (night-shade), <s>pāka</s> (cooking-salt), <s>kṣi</s>, and <s>ṭaṅka</s> (borax), // RCint_3.226 //

children.text: kūpībhiḥ pātayadhvaṃ bahu bahulayavakṣāramambho hi kalpyam /
children.translated_text: distill through flasks; abundant water of barley alkali should be prepared;

children.text: tasminnādhatta dhīrāḥ sakavalam agajāvallabhaṃ jāraṇāya // RCint_3.227 //
children.translated_text: in that, O wise ones, place mercury with its feeding along with <s>agajā</s> (a plant) for <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation). // RCint_3.227 //
Now we expound the chapter on mica (<s>abhra</s>). // RCint_4.1 //
RCint, 4
It indeed accepts being equivalent to the nectar-juice by removing all old age and death;
among its many preparations described variously by many, we write one particular one from the <s>Rasamaṅgalīya</s>. // RCint_4.2 //
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): <s>vajra</s> (diamond-type)

children.text: yadañjananibhaṃ kṣiptaṃ na vahnau vikṛtiṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: That which resembles collyrium and does not undergo change when cast into fire

children.text: vajrasaṃjñaṃ hi tadyojyamabhraṃ sarvatra netarat // RCint_4.3 //
children.translated_text: is known by the name <s>vajra</s> (diamond-type) — only that mica should be used everywhere, not the other. // RCint_4.3 //
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): subtypes
Mica is considered to be of three kinds: <s>vajra</s> (diamond), <s>bhekavapu</s> (frog-bodied), and <s>kṛṣṇa</s> (black);

children.text: tataḥ kṛṣṇaṃ samādāya pācayet kāṇḍike rase // RCint_4.4 //
children.translated_text: of these, taking the black one, one should cook it in the <s>kāṇḍika</s> (tube-like vessel) process. // RCint_4.4 //
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): subtypes: quality

children.text: tataḥ kṛṣṇaṃ samādāyetyanena kṛṣṇatvasāmānyād vajrakṛṣṇābhrayor grahaṇam /
children.translated_text: By the statement 'taking the black one' — due to the general quality of blackness, both <s>vajra</s> and black mica are accepted;
but <s>bhekavapu</s> (frog-bodied), being of greenish-yellow and other colors, should not be taken. // RCint_4.5 //
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): <s>sattvapātana</s> (essence-extraction)

children.text: cūrṇīkṛtaṃ gaganapatramathāranāle dhṛtvā dinaikam avaśoṣya ca sūraṇasya /
children.translated_text: Powdered mica leaf, soaked in <s>āranāla</s> (sour gruel) for one day and then dried, with the juice of <s>sūraṇa</s> (elephant yam),

children.text: bhāvyaṃ rasaistadanu mūlarasaiḥ kadalyāḥ pādāṃśaṭaṅkaṇayutaṃ śapharaiḥ sametam // RCint_4.6 //
children.translated_text: should be treated with those juices, then with the root-juice of banana, combined with a quarter portion of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) and <s>śaphara</s> (fish). // RCint_4.6 //

children.text: piṇḍīkṛtaṃ tu bahudhā mahiṣīmalena saṃśoṣya koṣṭhagatamāśu dhameddhaṭhāgnau /
children.translated_text: Formed into lumps, dried thoroughly with buffalo dung, and placed in a crucible, one should quickly blow with intense fire;

children.text: sattvaṃ patatyatirasāyanajāraṇārthaṃ yogyaṃ bhavet sakalalauhaguṇādhikaṃ ca // RCint_4.7 //
children.translated_text: the <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence) falls — it becomes suitable for the purpose of superior <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) and <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation), and surpasses the qualities of all metals. // RCint_4.7 //
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): <s>sattva</s>: <s>ekīkaraṇa</s> (unification)
The <s>sattva</s> (essence) that comes in granular form should be placed in a crucible,
blown with the five friends (<s>pañcamitra</s>), it becomes unified with a resonant sound. // RCint_4.8 //
<s>Pañcamitra</s> (five friends)
Ghee, honey, <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium), <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus seeds), and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) — these are known as the <s>pañcamitra</s> (five friends).
It unifies all metals by blowing in a charcoal fire. // RCint_4.9 //
Mica <s>sattva</s> (essence) with equal sulphur and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), blown in a husk-crucible,
combined with that <s>sattva</s> powder and mercury — it becomes effective for all purposes. // RCint_4.10 //
Its purification and killing are the same as for iron. // RCint_4.11 //
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): <s>sattva</s>: purification and killing
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): <s>sattva</s>: ingestion
The powder of mica <s>sattva</s>, or of <s>kānta</s> (magnetite), or then
of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron), O Great Goddess, treated with <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits) decoction, // RCint_4.12 //
until it resembles collyrium, dried and covered with cloth,
with the essence of <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta) and <s>āmalaka</s> (gooseberry), and with the juice of <s>haridrā</s> (turmeric), // RCint_4.13 //
mixed with <s>krauñcaja</s> (Mucuna pruriens) ghee and honey,
placed inside a sealed iron container, stored in grain for a month, // RCint_4.14 //
should be licked with ghee and honey — this is the supreme <s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s> (field-preparation);
thus, by a year's regimen, a person attains a thousand-year lifespan. // RCint_4.15 //
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): <s>vajra</s> (diamond-type): purification

children.text: vajrābhraṃ ca dhamedvahnau tataḥ kṣīre vinikṣipet /
children.translated_text: <s>Vajra</s>-mica should be heated in fire and then immersed in milk;
making it into split leaves, it should be treated with the juices of <s>taṇḍulīya</s> (Amaranthus) and sour substances
for eight <s>yāmas</s> (twenty-four hours) — thus the mica is purified. // RCint_4.16 //
The application of grain-mica-ash is described in two methods, by the red and black distinction. // RCint_4.17 //
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): killing

children.text: kṛtvā dhānyābhrakaṃ tattu śoṣayitvā tu mardayet /
children.translated_text: Making <s>dhānyābhraka</s> (grain-mica), drying it and grinding,
it should be ground with <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) milk-gruel, or with <s>arka</s> root juice. // RCint_4.18 //
Wrapping it in <s>arka</s> leaves, one should cook properly in an elephant-dung sealed heating;

children.text: punarmardyaṃ punaḥ pācyaṃ saptavāraṃ prayatnataḥ // RCint_4.19 //
children.translated_text: grinding again and cooking again — seven times with effort. // RCint_4.19 //
Then with decoctions of banyan aerial roots, three more sealed heatings should be given likewise;

children.text: mriyate nātra sandehaḥ sarvarogeṣu yojayet // RCint_4.20 //
children.translated_text: it dies — there is no doubt in this; it should be employed in all diseases. // RCint_4.20 //
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): killing
Mica ground with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), cooked in a pan of clay and iron,

children.text: mriyate nātra sandeho guṇādhikyāya vauṣadhaiḥ // RCint_4.21 //
children.translated_text: it dies — there is no doubt; for greater potency, with herbs: // RCint_4.21 //

it should also be killed through grinding and sealed heating with <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s> (Amaranthus), <s>bṛhatī</s> (Solanum indicum), <s>nāgavallī</s> (betel leaf), <s>tagara</s> (Valeriana), <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>ahilamocikā</s>, <s>maṇḍūkaparṇī</s> (Centella), <s>tiktikā</s>, <s>khūparṇikā</s>, <s>madana</s>, <s>arka</s> (Calotropis), <s>ārdraka</s> (ginger), <s>palāśa</s> (Butea), <s>sūtamātṛkā</s>, and others. // RCint_4.22 //
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): killing (?)

children.text: dhānyābhrakasya bhāgaikaṃ dvau bhāgau ṭaṅkaṇasya ca /
children.translated_text: One part of <s>dhānyābhraka</s> (grain-mica) and two parts of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax),
ground together, sealed in a blind crucible, and cooked with intense fire;
the powder, cooled naturally, should be employed in all preparations. // RCint_4.23 //
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): killing
Taking <s>dhānyābhraka</s> (grain-mica), three sealed heatings with <s>mustā</s> (Cyperus) decoction;
likewise with <s>punarnavā</s> juices, and with <s>kāsamarda</s> (Cassia occidentalis) juices; // RCint_4.24 //
with <s>nāgavallī</s> (betel leaf) juice, with <s>sūrya</s> (Calotropis) milk — each separately,
grinding each day, with decoctions from banyan aerial roots, // RCint_4.25 //
after giving three sealed heatings, then three more sealed heatings with <s>musalī</s> (Chlorophytum) juice,
three with <s>gokṣura</s> (Tribulus) decoction, three sealed heatings with <s>vānarī</s> juice, // RCint_4.26 //
cooking with <s>mocakanda</s> (banana bulb) juice for three nights, with <s>kokilākṣa</s> (Asteracantha),

children.text: rasaiḥ puṭecca lodhrasya kṣīrādekapuṭaṃ tataḥ // RCint_4.27 //
children.translated_text: sealed heating with <s>lodhra</s> (Symplocos) juice, then one sealed heating with milk; // RCint_4.27 //

children.text: dadhnā ghṛtena madhunā svacchayā sitayā tathā /
children.translated_text: with curd, with ghee, with honey, with clear sugar —
one sealed heating with each should be given; thus the killing of mica is accomplished. // RCint_4.28 //
The mica becomes a destroyer of all diseases, a carrier of formulations,
a destroyer of the pride and arrogance of passionate women — recommended for those suffering from impotence. // RCint_4.29 //
It is an aphrodisiac, life-prolonging, semen-increasing, and progeny-bestowing.
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): killing (?)
Mica ground with banana stem water and salt, made into discs, with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) in the middle,

children.text: dagdhendhaneṣu vyajanānilena snuhyarkamūlāmbupuṭaṃ ca siddhyai // RCint_4.30 //
children.translated_text: [placed] in burnt fuel with fan-blown air, and a sealed heating with <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia) and <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) root water for perfection. // RCint_4.30 //
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): ash: formulations
Equal ghee and killed mica should be cooked in an iron vessel;

children.text: ghṛte jīrṇe tadabhraṃ tu sarvakāryeṣu yojayet // RCint_4.31 //
children.translated_text: when the ghee is absorbed, that mica should be employed in all preparations. // RCint_4.31 //
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): ash: formulations
Sixteen <s>palas</s> of <s>triphalā</s> decoction,

children.text: goghṛtasya palānyaṣṭau mṛtābhrasya palān daśa // RCint_4.32 //
children.translated_text: eight <s>palas</s> of cow's ghee, and ten <s>palas</s> of killed mica — // RCint_4.32 //
combining these and cooking in an iron vessel with gentle fire,

children.text: drave jīrṇe samādāya sarvarogeṣu yojayet // RCint_4.33 //
children.translated_text: when the liquid is absorbed, it should be taken and employed in all diseases. // RCint_4.33 //
For the red [variety], by the process of <s>amṛtīkaraṇa</s> (immortalizing), there is an increase in qualities but a loss of color. // RCint_4.34 //
(unclear passage)
Now, incidentally, the liquefaction processes are described. // RCint_4.35 //
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): liquefaction
Ground with the exudate of <s>agasti</s> (Sesbania) flowers, placed in the interior of <s>sūraṇa</s> (elephant yam),

children.text: goṣṭhabhūstho ghano māsaṃ jāyate jalasaṃnibhaḥ // RCint_4.36 //
children.translated_text: mica kept in a cow-pen for a month becomes water-like. // RCint_4.36 //
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): liquefaction
Mica ground with the juice of <s>vajravallī</s> (a creeper) and combined with <s>sauvarcala</s> (sochal salt),

children.text: pakvaṃ ca śarāvapuṭe bahuvāraṃ bhavati rasarūpam // RCint_4.37 //
children.translated_text: cooked in a saucer sealed heating many times, becomes mercury-like in form. // RCint_4.37 //
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): liquefaction
By the addition of <s>suradālī</s> powder treated a hundred times with its own juice,

children.text: dravati punaḥ saṃsthānaṃ bhajate gaganaṃ na kāle'pi // RCint_4.38 //
children.translated_text: mica liquefies and then does not return to its [solid] form even over time. // RCint_4.38 //
<s>Abhra</s> (mica): <s>sattva</s>: liquefaction
By the addition of the bulb of <s>kañcukī</s> (a plant), treated a hundred times with its own juice,
mica <s>sattva</s> remains liquefied, and likewise all metals. // RCint_4.39 //
Liquefaction: combination (<s>melāpana</s>)
These liquefied [substances], combined with black aloe-wood, garlic, white <s>rāmaṭha</s>,
combine when warm; they should be ground with woman's menstrual blood and <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) seed juice. // RCint_4.40 //
Jewels: liquefaction
Pearls should be treated with <s>vetasa</s> (cane) acid for seven days;
placed inside a lemon, it should be stored in a heap of grain. // RCint_4.41 //
By the sealed-heating cooking, that powder liquefies like water;

children.text: kurute yogarājo'yaṃ ratnānāṃ drāvaṇaṃ priye // RCint_4.42 //
children.translated_text: this king of preparations effects the liquefaction of gems, O beloved. // RCint_4.42 //
<s>Abhra</s> (?): <s>sattva</s>: extraction

children.text: guḍaḥ purastathā lākṣā piṇyākaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Jaggery first, then lac, oil-cake, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax),
wool, <s>sarja</s> (Shorea) resin, combined with small fish — // RCint_4.43 //
all these powdered and made into lumps with goat's milk,

children.text: kṛtā dhmātāḥ kharāṅgāraiḥ sattvaṃ muñcanti nānyathā // RCint_4.44 //
children.translated_text: when blown with fierce charcoal, they release the <s>sattva</s> (essence), not otherwise. // RCint_4.44 //
Stones, earths, and all metals separately —

children.text: anyāni yānyasādhyāni vyomasattvasya kā kathā // RCint_4.45 //
children.translated_text: for what cannot otherwise be achieved, what question is there about mica <s>sattva</s>? // RCint_4.45 //
Sulphur: purification (mechanical)
First, sulphur, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), etc., should be washed with lemon juice;
the firmly adhering dust and impurity are loosened thereby. // RCint_5.1 //
RCint, 5

Sulphur: purification
Sulphur placed in a milk-vessel, purified through cloth in a <s>kūrmapuṭa</s> (tortoise sealed-heating), becomes clean.
Alternatively, likewise in <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel) with ghee, it attains purification. // RCint_5.2 //
Sulphur: purification
Here the sulphur called 'butter-like' should be preferred. // RCint_5.3 //
Sulphur: purification
Placing ghee in an iron vessel, one should heat it on fire;

children.text: tapte ghṛte tatsamānaṃ kṣipedgandhakajaṃ rajaḥ // RCint_5.4 //
children.translated_text: in the hot ghee, one should cast an equal amount of sulphur powder. // RCint_5.4 //
Knowing that the sulphur has melted, one should cast it into milk;
thus the purification of sulphur is achieved — it should be employed in all preparations. // RCint_5.5 //
Sulphur: removal of odor

children.text: gandhakasya ca pādāṃśaṃ dattvā ca ṭaṅkaṇaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Adding a quarter portion of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) to the sulphur,
one should grind with sour lemon juice and treat with <s>ruvu</s> oil,

children.text: cūrṇaṃ pāṣāṇagaṃ kṛtvā śanair gandhaṃ kharātape // RCint_5.6 //
children.translated_text: making it into a stone-like powder, gently [drying] the sulphur in strong sunlight. // RCint_5.6 //
Powdering the sulphur, one should cook it in milk until it solidifies;
then adding <s>sūryāvartta</s> (sunflower/heliotrope) juice, one should cook gently again. // RCint_5.7 //
Thereafter the skillful one should immerse it in water derived from <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits);

children.text: jahāti gandhako gandhaṃ nijaṃ nāstīha saṃśayaḥ // RCint_5.8 //
children.translated_text: the sulphur abandons its natural odor — there is no doubt in this. // RCint_5.8 //
Sulphur: removal of odor
<s>Devadālī</s> or <s>amlaparṇī</s> (sorrel-leaf plant), or <s>nāgara</s> (dry ginger), or pomegranate,

children.text: mātuluṅgaṃ yathālābhaṃ dravamekasya vā haret // RCint_5.9 //
children.translated_text: or lemon — the juice of whichever is available should be taken. // RCint_5.9 //
A quarter portion of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) relative to the sulphur, combined with that juice,

children.text: anayorgandhakaṃ bhāvyaṃ tribhirvārais tataḥ punaḥ // RCint_5.10 //
children.translated_text: the sulphur should be treated with these three times; then again: // RCint_5.10 //
<s>Dhūstūra</s> (Datura), <s>tulasī</s> (holy basil), <s>kṛṣṇā</s> (black pepper), garlic, <s>devadālikā</s>,
<s>śigru</s> (drumstick) root, <s>kākamācī</s> (Solanum nigrum), camphor, and the two <s>śaṅkhinīs</s>, // RCint_5.11 //
black aloe-wood, musk, and the two <s>vandhyākarkoṭakīs</s>,
ground with lemon juice and cast into castor oil. // RCint_5.12 //
With this, the previously [purified] sulphur placed in an iron vessel should be treated

children.text: trivāraṃ kṣaudratulyaṃ tu jāyate gandhakavarjitam // RCint_5.13 //
children.translated_text: three times — it becomes honey-like, freed from the sulphur smell. // RCint_5.13 //
<s>Gandhataila</s> (sulphur oil)
A cloth should be smeared seven times with <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) milk and <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia) milk;

children.text: gandhakaṃ navanītena piṣṭvā vastraṃ vilepayet // RCint_5.14 //
children.translated_text: sulphur ground with butter should be applied to the cloth. // RCint_5.14 //
That wick, lit and held on a stick, should be held downward;

children.text: tailaṃ patatyadhobhāṇḍe grāhyaṃ yogeṣu yojayet // RCint_5.15 //
children.translated_text: oil drips into the vessel below — it should be collected and employed in preparations. // RCint_5.15 //
<s>Gandhataila</s> (sulphur oil)
While churning milk, sulphur powder should be added;
the ghee obtained from that curd yields <s>gandhataila</s> (sulphur oil). // RCint_5.16 //
<s>Gandhataila</s>: medicinal properties
<s>Gandhataila</s> (sulphur oil) destroys <s>galatkuṣṭha</s> (leprosy with flesh falling) through both application and ingestion;
with this, pills should be made for <s>Rasendra</s> (mercury) in the prescribed procedures. // RCint_5.17 //
Sulphur: binding
One <s>pala</s> of purified mercury and one <s>karṣa</s> of sulphur,
placed in a heated mortar, soaked with <s>devadālī</s> juice,
and ground with the fingers — <s>gandhabandha</s> (sulphur-binding) is produced. // RCint_5.18 //
Sulphur: <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste)

children.text: bhāgā dvādaśa sūtasya dvau bhāgau gandhakasya ca /
children.translated_text: Twelve parts of mercury and two parts of sulphur,
ground with the addition of ghee — <s>gandhapiṣṭikā</s> (sulphur paste) is produced. // RCint_5.19 //
Sulphur: binding

children.text: aṣṭau bhāgā rasendrasya bhāga ekastu gāndhikaḥ /
children.translated_text: Eight parts of <s>Rasendra</s> (mercury) and one part of sulphur,
ground with poison-oil and similar substances — <s>gandhabandha</s> (sulphur-binding) is produced. // RCint_5.20 //
Sulphur: <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste)
Ten <s>niṣkas</s> of purified mercury and one <s>niṣka</s> of purified sulphur,

children.text: stokaṃ stokaṃ kṣipetkhalve mardayecca śanaiḥ śanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: should be added little by little to the mortar and ground slowly, slowly;
by pounding, a paste is produced — this is <s>gandhakapiṣṭikā</s> (sulphur paste). // RCint_5.21 //
Its applications are: sulphur <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation), lead killing, etc. // RCint_5.22 //
Sulphur: purified: medicinal properties
Purified sulphur removes diseases such as <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), death-threatening conditions, fevers, and the like;

children.text: agnikārī mahānuṣṇo vīryavṛddhiṃ karoti ca // RCint_5.23 //
children.translated_text: it is a digestive stimulant, greatly heating, and increases virility. // RCint_5.23 //
Now we expound the chapter on all metals. // RCint_6.1 //
RCint, 6
Metals, when killed, become like mercury, O goddess worshipped by the gods;

children.text: vinighnanti jarāvyādhīn rasayuktāni kiṃ punaḥ // RCint_6.2 //
children.translated_text: they destroy old age and disease — how much more so when combined with mercury! // RCint_6.2 //
Metals: purification
Leaves of gold, silver, antimony, copper, and iron should be heated in fire;

children.text: niṣiñcettaptatailāni taile takre gavāṃ jale // RCint_6.3 //
children.translated_text: they should be quenched in hot oil, then in oil, in buttermilk, in cow's water, // RCint_6.3 //

children.text: kāñjike ca kulatthānāṃ kaṣāye saptadhā pṛthak /
children.translated_text: in <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel), and in <s>kulattha</s> (horse gram) decoction — seven times separately;
thus the purification of gold and other metals is accomplished. // RCint_6.4 //
Metals: purification
All metals heated and quenched seven times
in banana root water attain the highest purification. // RCint_6.5 //
Lead, tin: purification

children.text: nāgavaṅgau prataptau ca gālitau tau niṣecayet /
children.translated_text: Lead and tin, heated and melted, should be poured and quenched

children.text: saptadhaiva viśuddhiḥ syādravidugdhe ca saptadhā // RCint_6.6 //
children.translated_text: seven times — thus purification occurs; also seven times in <s>ravi</s> (Calotropis) milk. // RCint_6.6 //
Gold: purification
Gold, coated with <s>varṇavṛttikā</s> (a coloring paste) and blown seven times,

children.text: viśudhyati varaṃ kiṃcid varṣavṛddhiśca jāyate // RCint_6.7 //
children.translated_text: is well purified; and there is some increase in weight. // RCint_6.7 //
Gold: purification
Ant-hill earth, soot, red ochre, brick powder, and a pungent substance —
these five earths, with lemon juice and <s>āranāla</s> (sour gruel), // RCint_6.8 //

children.text: piṣṭvā lepyaṃ svarṇapatraṃ śreṣṭhaṃ puṭena śudhyati /
children.translated_text: ground and applied to gold leaf — the finest is purified by sealed heating.
Silver: purification
Silver, melted with lead and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), attains purification;

children.text: rajataṃ doṣanirmuktaṃ kiṃ vā kṣārāmlapācitam // RCint_6.9 //
children.translated_text: silver freed from defects, or cooked with alkali and acid. // RCint_6.9 //
Copper: purification
Copper leaf, smeared with <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia) milk, <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) milk, salt, and <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel),
heated and then quenched repeatedly in <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex) juice,
twelve times — the copper is purified through coating, heating, and quenching. // RCint_6.10 //
Copper: purification
Copper leaf should be cooked in cow's urine for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours) with strong fire;
with acid and alkali, copper attains complete purification. // RCint_6.11 //
<s>Rājarīti</s> (a copper alloy), bronze: purification and killing
The physician should purify <s>rājarīti</s> (a copper alloy) and <s>ghoṣa</s> (bronze/bell-metal) in the same manner as copper;
they should be killed like copper too, and their qualities are like copper's. // RCint_6.12 //
Bronze, brass, lead, tin: purification
<s>Ghoṣa</s> (bell-metal), <s>āra</s> (brass), lead, and tin

children.text: nirguṇḍīrasamadhye tu śudhyante nātra saṃśayaḥ // RCint_6.13 //
children.translated_text: are purified by quenching seven times in <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex) juice — there is no doubt in this. // RCint_6.13 //
Iron: purification: <s>adri</s> (mineral) [defect]
In water of eightfold <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits) — sixteen <s>palas</s> of <s>triphalā</s>,

children.text: tatkvāthe pādaśeṣe tu lohasya palapañcakam // RCint_6.14 //
children.translated_text: in that decoction reduced to one quarter, five <s>palas</s> of iron — // RCint_6.14 //
making leaves and heating them, one should quench seven times;

children.text: evaṃ pralīyate doṣo girijo lohasambhavaḥ // RCint_6.15 //
children.translated_text: thus the <s>girija</s> (mineral) defect born of iron is dissolved. // RCint_6.15 //
Iron: purification
The accomplished <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, a knower of truth, prescribed

children.text: prakṣepaṃ prāha tattvajñaḥ siddho nāgārjunastataḥ // RCint_6.16 //
children.translated_text: the addition of iron in the water of herbs appropriate for the respective diseases. // RCint_6.16 //
Iron: purification
In the absence of all [the above], it should be quenched in milk, oil, ghee, and cow's water;
this purification of already-pure [iron] is recommended for increasing its qualities. // RCint_6.17 //
Various <s>sattvas</s> (metallic essences): purification
Mica <s>sattva</s> should be purified like iron; <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites) <s>sattva</s> like copper;
the <s>sattvas</s> of <s>rasa</s> (mercury), <s>kāla</s>, realgar, and <s>tuttha</s> (copper sulphate) — by cooking with alkali and acid;
they are purified in one day; and earthworms and similar [substances] likewise. // RCint_6.18 //
A physician skilled in the procedures taught by the <s>Siddhalakṣmīśvara</s> [text]

children.text: lohānāṃ sarasaṃ bhasma sarvotkṛṣṭaṃ prakalpayet // RCint_6.19 //
children.translated_text: should prepare the ash of metals as juicy [well-processed] and of the highest quality. // RCint_6.19 //
The seven metals: killing
The seven metals beginning with gold, coated with realgar, sulphur, and <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) milk,

children.text: mriyante dvādaśapuṭaiḥ satyaṃ guruvaco yathā // RCint_6.20 //
children.translated_text: are killed by twelve sealed heatings — truly, as the words of the teacher state. // RCint_6.20 //
The seven metals: killing
The seven metals beginning with gold, mixed with mercury,
are killed in a <s>sikatāyantra</s> (sand-bath) for four <s>yāmas</s> (twelve hours) with sulphur and additional <s>amṛtā</s> (Tinospora). // RCint_6.21 //
They are cooked with sulphur one, two, or three times as observed from the results;
and sixfold or more sulphur is assimilated here for increasing the qualities. // RCint_6.22 //
Gold: killing
Making a <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste) with equal mercury, one should destroy the mercury by fire;

children.text: svarṇaṃ tatsamatāpyena puṭitaṃ bhasma jāyate // RCint_6.23 //
children.translated_text: that gold, heated with an equal amount of <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites) in a sealed heating, becomes ash. // RCint_6.23 //
Gold: killing, removal of lead
Fine gold leaves with lemon juice, coated with lead ash,
should be reduced to ash by sealed heating three times;

children.text: punaḥ puṭe trivāraṃ tanmlecchato nāgahānaye // RCint_6.24 //
children.translated_text: then three more sealed heatings of the <s>mleccha</s> (purging) type for the removal of lead. // RCint_6.24 //
Gold: killing

children.text: śuddhasūtasamaṃ svarṇaṃ khalve kṛtvā tu golakam /
children.translated_text: Making gold equal to purified mercury into a ball in the mortar,

children.text: ūrdhvādho gandhakaṃ dattvā sarvatulyaṃ nirudhya ca // RCint_6.25 //
children.translated_text: placing sulphur above and below in equal total amount, and sealing, // RCint_6.25 //
fourteen sealed heatings should be given with thirty <s>vanopalas</s> (forest stones/cow-dung cakes);

children.text: nirutthaṃ jāyate bhasma gandho deyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ // RCint_6.26 //
children.translated_text: the ash becomes <s>niruttha</s> (non-rising); sulphur should be added repeatedly. // RCint_6.26 //
Gold: killing
Covering one <s>tola</s> of gold, one <s>māṣa</s> of purified sulphur

children.text: kṣiptvā cāmlena saṃcūrṇya tattulyau gandhamākṣikau // RCint_6.27 //
children.translated_text: should be cast and powdered with acid; equal amounts of sulphur and <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrites) to that, // RCint_6.27 //
ground with acid for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours), sealed and cooked in a light sealed heating;

children.text: gandhaḥ punaḥ punardeyo mriyate daśabhiḥ puṭaiḥ // RCint_6.28 //
children.translated_text: sulphur should be added repeatedly — it dies in ten sealed heatings. // RCint_6.28 //
Silver: killing
Making a <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste) of silver with mercury, then combining
equal <s>tāla</s> (orpiment) and sulphur, one should grind with lemon juice;
in two or three sealed heatings it becomes ash — it should be employed thus in mercury preparations and the like. // RCint_6.29 //
'With equal mercury' is the meaning.

children.text: atra sūtarakṣārthaṃ gandhaḥ punar adhiko deyaḥ // RCint_6.30 //
children.translated_text: Here, for the preservation of mercury, additional sulphur should be given. // RCint_6.30 //
Copper: killing
Copper leaf, coated with sulphur equal to the copper, ground with acid,

children.text: kaṇṭavedhyaṃ tāmrapatram andhayitvā puṭe pacet // RCint_6.31 //
children.translated_text: pierced with a needle-point, sealed in a blind [crucible], should be cooked in a sealed heating. // RCint_6.31 //
After removing and powdering it, one should add a quarter portion of sulphur;

children.text: pācyaṃ jambhāmbhasā piṣṭaṃ samo gandhaścatuḥpuṭe // RCint_6.32 //
children.translated_text: ground with lemon juice, it should be cooked; equal sulphur in four sealed heatings. // RCint_6.32 //
Ground with lemon juice, one sealed heating should be given;
with white sugar also, through such sealed-heating administration, killing is accomplished. // RCint_6.33 //
Copper: killing
Mercury in a quarter portion of the copper, sulphur equal to the copper,
should be ground for two <s>yāmas</s> (six hours) until <s>kajjalī</s> (black sulphide) is formed. // RCint_6.34 //

children.text: tāṃ tu kanyārasaiḥ piṣṭvā tāmrapatrāṇi lepayet /
children.translated_text: That [kajjalī], ground with <s>kanyā</s> (aloe) juice, should be coated on copper leaves;
when dried, those [leaves], within the remaining <s>kajjalī</s>, // RCint_6.35 //
should be placed inside a pot and sealed with a saucer;
the junction of both should be sealed with water-ash coating. // RCint_6.36 //
The pot should be filled with a pungent substance or ash up to the neck;
covering it and placing on a furnace, fire should be kindled firmly;
after four <s>yāmas</s> (twelve hours), when naturally cooled, it should be removed. // RCint_6.37 //

children.text: na rasena vinā lauhaṃ na rasaṃ cābhrakaṃ vinā /
children.translated_text: Without mercury, metal [does not transform]; without mica, mercury [is incomplete];

children.text: ekatvena śarīrasya bandho bhavati dehinaḥ // RCint_6.38 //
children.translated_text: only by the unity of both does the binding in the body of the embodied being occur. // RCint_6.38 //

children.text: capalena vinā lauhaṃ yaḥ karoti pumāniha /
children.translated_text: A man who uses metal without <s>capala</s> (mercury) in this world,

children.text: udare tasya kiṭṭāni jāyante nātra saṃśayaḥ // RCint_6.39 //
children.translated_text: slag is produced in his abdomen — there is no doubt in this. // RCint_6.39 //
In truth, for excellence, the combination with mercury and the combination of mercury with mica [are essential];

children.text: anayormātrā yuktyanusāriṇī tato mriyata iti śeṣaḥ // RCint_6.40 //
children.translated_text: their dosage follows the principles, and thereby killing [of metals] is accomplished — this is the remainder. // RCint_6.40 //
Remedy against vomiting
Killed copper ground with acid, placed in a container, coated with clay,
should be cooked with <s>pañcāmṛta</s> (five nectars), or thrice for the pacification of vomiting and similar [side effects]. // RCint_6.41 //
In the case of <s>sūraṇa</s> (elephant yam), a large sealed heating should be given.
Copper: killing
Copper leaf should be placed with sulphur and rock salt in lemon juice;

children.text: paṅkāyamānaṃ puṭayetsuyuktyā vāntyādikaṃ yāvadupaiti śāntim // RCint_6.42 //
children.translated_text: when it becomes mud-like, it should be sealed-heated skillfully, until vomiting and similar [effects] subside. // RCint_6.42 //
Copper: <s>mṛtottha</s> (re-killing of killed copper)
A copper disc that has been killed, purified, and heated, placed with the sacrificial [substance],
becomes [truly] killed; <s>Sūtendra</s> (mercury) should be added according to the defect. // RCint_6.43 //
Copper: killing
Making <s>kajjalī</s> (black sulphide) from half portions each of mercury and sulphur,

children.text: vārā limpet kaṇṭavedhyaṃ mriyate tāmramātape // RCint_6.44 //
children.translated_text: repeatedly coating needle-pierced [copper leaves] — copper dies in sunlight. // RCint_6.44 //
Gold: production from copper

children.text: ārkaṃ bhasma sthālikāyāṃ nidhāya jvālāṃ dattvā nāśayettatra gandham /
children.translated_text: Placing <s>ārka</s> (Calotropis) ash in a pan, kindling a flame, one should destroy sulphur therein;
revolving this and killing it seven times — thus copper becomes equal to gold. // RCint_6.45 //
(unclear passage)
Silver, gold, sun-gem leaf, combined with mercury-potency, ground together with the sacrificial substance,
from the desired mercury paste, making a thin layer — one should then offer it. // RCint_6.46 //
The <s>sattva</s> (essence) of <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrites), <s>rasa</s> (mercury-ore), and others should be killed like copper. // RCint_6.47 //
<s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrites): <s>sattva</s>: killing
Tin: killing

children.text: vaṅgaṃ kharparake kṛtvā cullyāṃ saṃsthāpayet sudhīḥ /
children.translated_text: The wise one should place tin in an earthen dish and set it on a furnace;
when it melts, these powders should be added to it: // RCint_6.48 //
first, turmeric powder; second, <s>yavānikā</s> (bishop's weed);
third, <s>jīvaka</s> (a plant); then, derived from tamarind bark, // RCint_6.49 //
and powder derived from <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) bark should be added therein;

children.text: evaṃ vidhānato vaṅgo mriyate nātra saṃśayaḥ // RCint_6.50 //
children.translated_text: by this method, tin dies — there is no doubt in this. // RCint_6.50 //
Lead: killing

children.text: nāgaṃ kharparake nidhāya kunaṭīcūrṇaṃ dadīta drute nimbūtthadravagandhakena puṭitaṃ bhasmībhavatyāśu tat /
children.translated_text: Lead placed in an earthen dish, <s>kunaṭī</s> powder should be added when melted; sealed with lemon juice and sulphur, it quickly becomes ash.

children.text: evaṃ tālakavāpatastu kuṭilaṃ cūrṇīkṛtaṃ tatpuṭed gandhāmlena samastadoṣarahitaṃ yogeṣu yojyaṃ bhavet // RCint_6.51 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by the addition of <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment), <s>kuṭila</s> (tin) too, when powdered and sealed-heated with sulphur and acid, becomes free from all defects and fit for use in preparations. // RCint_6.51 //
<s>Sindūra</s> (vermilion): production
Grinding <s>bhūbhujaṅga</s> (earthworm) and <s>agasti</s> (Sesbania), one should coat the vessel;
in that, when lead has melted, the alkali derived from <s>vāsā</s> (Adhatoda) and <s>apāmārga</s> (Achyranthes) // RCint_6.52 //
should be mixed therein in one-fourth part, as prescribed by the teacher;
cooking on a furnace for one <s>prahara</s> (three hours), stirring with a <s>vāsā</s> ladle, // RCint_6.53 //
then removing that powder, one should grind it with <s>vāsā</s> juice;
giving a sealed heating, removing again, and grinding with its juice,

children.text: evaṃ saptapuṭairnāgaḥ sindūro jāyate dhruvam // RCint_6.54 //
children.translated_text: thus in seven sealed heatings, lead assuredly becomes <s>sindūra</s> (vermilion). // RCint_6.54 //
Iron: killing

children.text: lauhaṃ patrasatīvataptam asakṛt kvāthe kṣipettraiphale cūrṇībhūtam ataḥ punastriphalaje kvāthe paced gojale /
children.translated_text: Iron leaves, heated thin and hot, should be repeatedly quenched in <s>triphalā</s> decoction; then powdered, it should again be cooked in <s>triphalā</s> decoction and cow's water;

children.text: matsyākṣītriphalā etena puṭayedyāvannirutthaṃ bhavet paścādājyamadhuplutaṃ supuṭitaṃ siddhaṃ bhaved āyasam // RCint_6.55 //
children.translated_text: with <s>matsyākṣī</s> and <s>triphalā</s>, it should be sealed-heated until it becomes non-rising; thereafter, dipped in ghee and honey and well sealed-heated, the iron is perfected. // RCint_6.55 //
Here <s>matsyākṣī</s> means <s>machechī</s> (a plant).
In the present three or four sealed heatings, a little <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) should be added. // RCint_6.56 //
Iron: killing
Iron powder, soaked in pomegranate leaf water, in a small pan,

children.text: mriyeta vastrāvṛtamarkabhāsā yojyaṃ puṭaiḥ syāt triphalādikānām // RCint_6.57 //
children.translated_text: dies by the heat of the sun covered with cloth; it should be used with sealed heatings of <s>triphalā</s> and other substances. // RCint_6.57 //

children.text: puṭabāhulyaṃ guṇādhikyāya śatādipuṭapakṣe mudganibhaṃ kṛtvā puṭān dadyādvastrapūtaṃ ca na kuryāt /
children.translated_text: For greater quality, in the method of a hundred or more sealed heatings, making [the pellets] the size of <s>mudga</s> (green gram), sealed heatings should be given, and cloth-filtering should not be done.
The <s>triphalā</s> and other [substances] for <s>amṛtasāra</s> (nectar-essence) iron will be described later. // RCint_6.58 //
Iron: killing: <s>vāritara</s> (water-floating) state

children.text: sūtakāddviguṇaṃ gandhaṃ dattvā kṛtvā ca kajjalīm /
children.translated_text: Adding double the sulphur to the mercury and making <s>kajjalī</s> (black sulphide),
equal iron powder to both should be ground with <s>kanyakā</s> (aloe) juice. // RCint_6.59 //

children.text: yāmayugmaṃ tataḥ piṇḍaṃ kṛtvā tāmrasya pātrake /
children.translated_text: Grinding for two <s>yāmas</s> (six hours), then making it into a ball and placing in a copper vessel,
the wise one should hold it in sunlight and cover with <s>uruvūka</s> (castor) leaves. // RCint_6.60 //
In half a <s>yāma</s> (ninety minutes) it will become hot; then it should be placed in a heap of grain;

children.text: dattvopari śarāvaṃ tu tridinānte samuddharet // RCint_6.61 //
children.translated_text: covering it with a saucer, it should be removed after three days. // RCint_6.61 //
Grinding and filtering through cloth — thus it becomes <s>vāritara</s> (water-floating);

children.text: evaṃ sarvāṇi lohāni svarṇādīnyapi mārayet // RCint_6.62 //
children.translated_text: thus all metals, including gold and others, should be killed. // RCint_6.62 //
Iron: checking the <s>vāritara</s> (water-floating) state
All killed metal should be blown with the <s>mitrapañcaka</s> (five friends);

children.text: yadyevaṃ syānnirutthānaṃ sevyaṃ vāritaraṃ hi tat // RCint_6.63 //
children.translated_text: if it thus becomes <s>nirutthāna</s> (non-rising), that <s>vāritara</s> is fit for use. // RCint_6.63 //
<s>Mitrapañcaka</s> (five friends)
Honey, ghee, <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus seeds), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium) —
these are counted as the <s>mitrapañcaka</s> (five friends) in metal combination. // RCint_6.64 //
Iron: killed: checking the killed state

children.text: madhvājyaṃ mṛtalauhaṃ ca sarūpyaṃ sampuṭe kṣipet /
children.translated_text: Honey-ghee and killed iron, together with equal silver, should be placed in a sealed container;

children.text: ruddhvā dhmāte ca saṃgrāhyaṃ rūpyaṃ vai pūrvamānakam /
children.translated_text: when sealed and blown, the silver should be recovered in its original measure;

children.text: tadā lauhaṃ mṛtaṃ vidyādanyathā mārayetpunaḥ // RCint_6.65 //
children.translated_text: then the iron is known to be [truly] killed; otherwise it should be killed again. // RCint_6.65 //
Iron: killing: <s>nirutthāna</s> (non-rising)
Iron that has risen [revived] with sulphur should be ground equally in the mortar
for one day with <s>kanyakā</s> (aloe) juice, sealed, and cooked in an elephant-dung sealed heating;
thus for all metals, this <s>nirutthiti</s> (non-revival) procedure should be performed. // RCint_6.66 //
Gold should be used in increasing barley[-weight] doses; eight <s>guñjā</s>-weights of <s>ravi</s> (Calotropis);
silver is double that; iron is more than triple. // RCint_6.67 //
<s>Kiṭṭa</s> (rust): age determines quality
Rust over a hundred years old is the best; eighty-year-old is middling;
sixty-year-old is inferior; anything younger than that is like poison. // RCint_6.68 //
<s>Maṇḍūra</s> (iron oxide): production
One should blow iron rust with <s>akṣa</s> (Terminalia) charcoal; then with cow's water

children.text: secayettaptataptaṃ ca saptavāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ // RCint_6.69 //
children.translated_text: one should quench the heated [substance] again and again, seven times. // RCint_6.69 //
Then powdering it and stirring it in double the quantity of <s>triphalā</s> decoction,

children.text: āloḍya bharjayedvahnau maṇḍūraṃ jāyate varam // RCint_6.70 //
children.translated_text: one should roast it on fire — excellent <s>maṇḍūra</s> (iron oxide) is produced. // RCint_6.70 //
Gold bestows longevity, wealth, radiance, intellect, and memory; it destroys all diseases; it is meritorious;
it pacifies spirit-possession, gives the happiness born of love, and manifests well-being, nourishment, and brilliance.

children.text: gāṅgeyaṃ cātha rūpyaṃ gadaham ajarākāri mehāpahāri /
children.translated_text: And silver (<s>gāṅgeya</s>) destroys diseases, prevents aging, removes urinary disorders,

children.text: kṣīṇānāṃ puṣṭikāri sphuṭam atikaraṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ vīryavṛddheḥ // RCint_6.71 //
children.translated_text: nourishes the emaciated, is clearly most effective, and is the cause of increasing virility. // RCint_6.71 //
Gold, silver
Gold: medicinal properties
Gold is sweet, pungent in post-digestive effect, cool in potency;
it pacifies all <s>doṣas</s> (humoral imbalances), destroys poison, and removes toxic preparations. // RCint_6.72 //
Its use destroys misfortune, strife, and sins;
it promotes longevity, intellect, and memory, and increases nourishment and radiance. // RCint_6.73 //
Those diseases which are not conquered by all herbal treatments

children.text: karmabhiḥ pañcabhiścāpi suvarṇaṃ teṣu yojayet // RCint_6.74 //
children.translated_text: and even by the five procedures (<s>pañcakarma</s>) — gold should be employed for them. // RCint_6.74 //
With <s>śilājatu</s> (shilajit) preparations, and with <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites) and mercury,

children.text: anyai rasāyanaiścāpi prayogo hemna uttamaḥ // RCint_6.75 //
children.translated_text: and with other <s>rasāyanas</s> (rejuvenating agents), the application of gold is supreme. // RCint_6.75 //
By '<s>tāpya</s> and mercury' here, ordinarily processed mercury is meant;
for specially processed mercury bestows the power of sky-walking and such [supernatural abilities]. // RCint_6.76 //
Honey, <s>āmalaka</s> (gooseberry) powder, and gold — these three
when consumed, even one seized by death-symptoms is freed from mortal danger. // RCint_6.77 //
One desiring intellect [should take it] with <s>vacā</s> (sweet flag); one desiring wealth, with lotus stamens;

children.text: śaṅkhapuṣpyā vayo'rthī ca vidāryā ca prajārthakaḥ // RCint_6.78 //
children.translated_text: one desiring longevity, with <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s> (Convolvulus); one desiring progeny, with <s>vidārī</s> (Pueraria). // RCint_6.78 //
Copper: medicinal properties
It is a scraping agent for tumors, anemia, acid-gastritis, pain, and heart [conditions]; it removes worms and purifies;
it conquers splenic disorders, skin diseases, abdominal ailments, and colic; it removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s> — this is copper (named after the sun). // RCint_6.79 //

children.text: rītikā śleṣmapittaghnī kāṃsyamuṣṇaṃ ca lekhanam // RCint_6.80 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rītikā</s> (brass) destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>; <s>kāṃsya</s> (bronze) is heating and a scraping agent. // RCint_6.80 //
Brass (<s>pittala</s>), bronze (<s>kāṃsya</s>)
<s>Vaṅga</s> (tin) removes burning sensation and destroys anemia, worms, and urinary disorders. // RCint_6.81 //
Tin: medicinal properties
Lead: medicinal properties
It possesses the strength of ten, increases virility, lifespan, and radiance;

children.text: rogān hanti mṛto nāgaḥ sevyo raṅgo'pi tadguṇaḥ // RCint_6.82 //
children.translated_text: killed lead destroys diseases; <s>raṅga</s> (zinc) too, if used, has the same qualities. // RCint_6.82 //
It conquers thirst, tumors, swelling, colic, hemorrhoids, skin diseases, anemia, and urinary disorders;
it is rejuvenating, heavy, eye-benefiting; <s>sāra</s> (steel) removes fat and wind;
lead is the coloring agent for silver; it removes <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>. // RCint_6.83 //
Iron: medicinal properties
It is a bestower of longevity, a producer of strength and virility, a remover of diseases, a destroyer of suffering;

children.text: ayaḥsamānaṃ nahi kiṃcidasti rasāyanaṃ śreṣṭhatamaṃ narāṇām // RCint_6.84 //
children.translated_text: there is nothing equal to iron — it is the supreme <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenating agent) for humans. // RCint_6.84 //
Iron: hierarchy of qualities
Compared to the ordinary [iron], <s>krauñca</s> (crane-type) is double; <s>kaliṅga</s> is eightfold from that;
ten times <s>kali</s> is <s>bhadra</s>; from <s>bhadra</s>, <s>vajra</s> (diamond-type) is a thousandfold. // RCint_6.85 //
From <s>vajra</s>, <s>pāṇḍi</s> is a hundredfold; <s>niraṅga</s> (pure iron) is tenfold from that;

children.text: tasmāt sahasraguṇitam ayaḥ kāntaṃ mahābalam // RCint_6.86 //
children.translated_text: and a thousandfold from that is <s>kānta</s> (magnetic iron), of great potency. // RCint_6.86 //

children.text: yallohaṃ yadguṇaṃ proktaṃ tatkiṭṭaṃ cāpi tadguṇam // RCint_6.87 //
children.translated_text: Whatever qualities a metal has, its rust (<s>kiṭṭa</s>) also has those same qualities. // RCint_6.87 //
Now we expound the chapter on poisons and subsidiary substances. // RCint_7.1 //
RCint, 7

children.text: viṣaṃ hi nāma nikhilarasāyanānām ūrjasvalam akhilavyādhividhvaṃsavidhāyakatām āsādayati // RCint_7.2 //
children.translated_text: Poison indeed, among all <s>rasāyanas</s> (rejuvenating agents), powerfully achieves the capacity to destroy all diseases. // RCint_7.2 //
It is indeed of eighteen types,

of which <s>saktuka</s>, <s>mustaka</s>, <s>kaurma</s>, <s>dārvīka</s>, <s>sārṣapa</s>, <s>saikata</s>, <s>vatsanābha</s>, and <s>śvetaśṛṅgī</s> — these varieties should be obtained for practical use. // RCint_7.3 //
<s>Saktuka</s>
Resembling the bulb of a spotted lotus, well-rounded like <s>saktu</s> (roasted flour) —
that should be known as <s>saktuka</s>; it is of long duration and greatly powerful. // RCint_7.4 //

<s>Mustaka</s>
<s>Mustaka</s> is of short duration and disease-destroying, shaped like <s>mustaka</s> (Cyperus).
<s>Kaurma</s> is tortoise-shaped; <s>dārvīka</s> is shaped like a serpent's hood. // RCint_7.5 //
<s>Kaurma</s>, <s>dārvīka</s>
<s>Sārṣapa</s>
<s>Sārṣapa</s>, which destroys fever, is covered with mustard-like hairy granules;
with coarse and fine granules, white and yellow, without hairs — that is the hairless variety. // RCint_7.6 //
The bulb that destroys fever and all diseases is called <s>saikata</s>. // RCint_7.7 //
<s>Saikata</s>
<s>Vatsanābha</s> (aconite)

children.text: yaḥ kando gostanākāro na dīrghaḥ pañcamāṅgulāt /
children.translated_text: A bulb shaped like a cow's teat, not longer than five finger-breadths,

children.text: na sthūlo gostanādūrdhvaṃ dvividho vatsanābhakaḥ // RCint_7.8 //
children.translated_text: not thicker than a cow's teat above — <s>vatsanābhaka</s> is of two kinds. // RCint_7.8 //
It is fast-acting, light, easily eliminated; [it comes in] white and black — the other [colors] are different;
it should be used for disease-removal, for <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation), and in <s>rasāyana</s>. // RCint_7.9 //

children.text: gośṛṅgavaddvidhā śṛṅgī śvetaḥ syād bahirantare // RCint_7.10 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgī</s> (horn-shaped poison) is of two kinds, like a cow's horn; it is white both outside and inside. // RCint_7.10 //
<s>Śvetaśṛṅgī</s> (white-horned [poison])

children.text: etāni saktukādyāni vātādau raktamelanenonmādasannipātādau ca prayojyāni // RCint_7.11 //
children.translated_text: These [eight], beginning with <s>saktuka</s>, should be used in <s>vāta</s> and other [conditions], in blood-related disorders, insanity, and <s>sannipāta</s> (combined humoral disturbance). // RCint_7.11 //

<s>Kālakūṭa</s>, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>dardura</s>, <s>hālāhala</s>, <s>karkoṭa</s>, <s>granthi</s>, <s>hāridra</s>, <s>raktaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>keśara</s>, and <s>yamadaṃṣṭrā</s> — these ten poisons should be avoided. // RCint_7.12 //
<s>Kālakūṭa</s>
A round, black bulb, resembling a lemon fruit —
that should be known as <s>kālakūṭa</s>; it causes death merely by smelling. // RCint_7.13 //

<s>Meṣaśṛṅgī</s>
A bulb shaped like a ram's horn is called <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>.

children.text: dardurākṛtikaḥ kando darduraḥ kathitastu saḥ // RCint_7.14 //
children.translated_text: A bulb shaped like a frog is called <s>dardura</s>. // RCint_7.14 //
<s>Dardura</s>

<s>Hālāhala</s>
Internally blue and externally white — that should be known as <s>hālāhala</s>.

children.text: karkoṭābhaṃ tu karkoṭaṃ kharaṃ bāhye'ntare mṛdu // RCint_7.15 //
children.translated_text: Resembling <s>karkoṭa</s> (spiny gourd), rough on the outside and soft inside. // RCint_7.15 //
<s>Karkoṭa</s>
<s>Hāridra</s>
A knotted [bulb] like a turmeric knot, black in color, very fearsome;
well-rounded at both root and tip, elongated, with a yellow interior;

children.text: kañcukāḍhyaḥ snigdhaparvā hāridraḥ syācca kandakaḥ // RCint_7.16 //
children.translated_text: covered with sheaths, with smooth joints — that is the <s>hāridra</s> poison bulb. // RCint_7.16 //
<s>Raktaśṛṅgī</s> (red-horned poison)
When the tip is pressed like a cow's horn, blood exudes;

children.text: kando laghur gostanavad raktaśṛṅgīti tadviṣam // RCint_7.17 //
children.translated_text: a light bulb shaped like a cow's teat — that poison is <s>raktaśṛṅgī</s>. // RCint_7.17 //

<s>Keśara</s>
That which has white hair-like [filaments] inside — that is known as <s>keśara</s>.
Shaped like a dog's fang — it is called <s>yamadaṃṣṭrā</s>. // RCint_7.18 //
<s>Yamadaṃṣṭrā</s> (Yama's fang)
In <s>rasavāda</s> (mercury-alchemy), <s>dhātuvāda</s> (metal-alchemy), and <s>viṣavāda</s> (poison-craft), here and there,

children.text: daśaitāni prayujyante na bhaiṣajye rasāyane // RCint_7.19 //
children.translated_text: these ten are employed — but not in medicinal <s>rasāyana</s>. // RCint_7.19 //

children.text: uddharet phalapāke tu navaṃ snigdhaṃ ghanaṃ guru /
children.translated_text: One should collect [poison] at the time of fruit-ripening: fresh, oily, dense, heavy,
unimpaired by poison-antidotes, undried by wind and other [agents]. // RCint_7.20 //
Poison: purification
Making the poison into thick pieces like chickpeas in a vessel,

children.text: tatra gomūtrakaṃ kṣiptvā pratyahaṃ nityanūtanam // RCint_7.21 //
children.translated_text: adding fresh cow's urine daily, // RCint_7.21 //

children.text: śoṣayet tridinād ūrdhvaṃ dhṛtvā tīvrātape tataḥ /
children.translated_text: one should dry [it] after three days, keeping it in strong sunlight; then
one should use that poison in preparations according to proper measure. // RCint_7.22 //
Poison: purified: storage
It should be kept in cloth smeared with red mustard oil;

children.text: viṣaṃ śuddhaṃ prayatnena nānyatra guṇahānitaḥ // RCint_7.23 //
children.translated_text: purified poison should be [stored] carefully, not elsewhere, due to loss of quality. // RCint_7.23 //
Poison: killing
That poison ground with equal <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) is said to be killed;

children.text: yojayet sarvarogeṣu na vikāraṃ karoti tat // RCint_7.24 //
children.translated_text: it should be employed in all diseases — it does not cause adverse effects. // RCint_7.24 //
Poison: subtypes: color and caste
White, red, yellow, and black — these are the four types;

children.text: brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ kramājjñeyaśca śūdrakaḥ // RCint_7.25 //
children.translated_text: Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, and Śūdra should be known in order. // RCint_7.25 //
The Brāhmaṇa [type] removes all diseases; the Kṣatriya is used in mercury-alchemy;

children.text: vaiśyo'pi rogahartā syācchūdraḥ sarvatra ninditaḥ // RCint_7.26 //
children.translated_text: the Vaiśya also removes diseases; the Śūdra is condemned in all uses. // RCint_7.26 //
The Brāhmaṇa is given in disease; the Kṣatriya in poison-consumption;

children.text: vaiśyo vyādhiṣu sarveṣu sarpadaṃṣṭre ca śūdrakaḥ // RCint_7.27 //
children.translated_text: the Vaiśya in all diseases; and the Śūdra in snakebite. // RCint_7.27 //
It should be given in autumn, summer, and spring — but not in the rainy season;
in the four months [of the rains], it removes diseases such as <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), <s>lūtā</s> (spider-poison), and others. // RCint_7.28 //
Poison: quantities
Starting with eight barley[-weights], gradually increasing by a sesame-seed measure,
it becomes a pacifier of all diseases and a promoter of vision and nourishment. // RCint_7.29 //
On the first [day], a mustard-seed dose; on the second, two mustard-seeds;

children.text: tṛtīye ca caturthe ca pañcame divase tathā // RCint_7.30 //
children.translated_text: on the third, fourth, and fifth days likewise, // RCint_7.30 //

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe ca saptame caiva kramavṛddhyā vivardhayet /
children.translated_text: and on the sixth and seventh, one should increase by progressive increment;
by a seven-mustard-seed dose, one should complete the first week. // RCint_7.31 //
Poison: rules for consumption

children.text: kramahānyā tathā deyaṃ dvitīye saptake viṣam /
children.translated_text: In the second week, poison should be given with progressive decrease;

children.text: yavamātraṃ viṣaṃ deyaṃ tṛtīye saptake kramāt // RCint_7.32 //
children.translated_text: a barley-weight of poison should be given in the third week by progressive [increase]. // RCint_7.32 //

children.text: vṛddhahānyā ca dātavyaṃ caturthe saptake tathā /
children.translated_text: In the fourth week, it should be given with progressive increase and decrease;

children.text: yavamātraṃ grasetsvastho guñjāmātraṃ tu kuṣṭhavān // RCint_7.33 //
children.translated_text: a healthy person should swallow a barley-weight; a person with <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease), a <s>guñjā</s>-weight. // RCint_7.33 //
For one who is eighty years old or eight years old,

children.text: viṣaṃ tasmai na dātavyaṃ dattaṃ vai doṣakārakam // RCint_7.34 //
children.translated_text: poison should not be given — if given, it causes harm. // RCint_7.34 //
It should be given in all diseases to one who eats ghee, who eats wholesome food,
to one who drinks milk — to a person devoted to <s>rasāyana</s>. // RCint_7.35 //
<s>Brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) should be the primary [observance] in the poison regimen;

children.text: pathyaiḥ susthamanā bhūtvā tadā siddhirna saṃśayaḥ // RCint_7.36 //
children.translated_text: with wholesome diet and a content mind — then success [comes], without doubt. // RCint_7.36 //
Poison: eight <s>vegas</s> (paroxysms)
When a mortal, through carelessness, consumes poison in excessive dose,

children.text: aṣṭau vegāstadā caiva jāyante tasya dehinaḥ // RCint_7.37 //
children.translated_text: then eight paroxysms arise in that embodied being. // RCint_7.37 //
In the first paroxysm, burning; in the second, trembling;

children.text: vege tṛtīye dāhaḥ syāccaturthe patanaṃ bhuvi // RCint_7.38 //
children.translated_text: in the third, scorching heat; in the fourth, falling to the ground. // RCint_7.38 //

children.text: phenaṃ tu pañcame vege ṣaṣṭhe vikalatā bhavet /
children.translated_text: In the fifth, frothing; in the sixth, paralysis;

children.text: jaḍatā saptame vege maraṇaṃ cāṣṭame bhavet // RCint_7.39 //
children.translated_text: in the seventh, stupor; and in the eighth, death. // RCint_7.39 //
Knowing these poison-paroxysms, one should destroy them with mantras and tantric methods. // RCint_7.40 //
Poison: healing the paroxysms

children.text: atimātraṃ yadā bhuktaṃ vamanaṃ kārayettadā // RCint_7.41 //
children.translated_text: When an excessive amount has been consumed, emesis should be induced. // RCint_7.41 //
One should give goat's milk until vomiting occurs;
when the goat's milk becomes stable in the abdomen of the person,
the skilled physician should know that the poison-paroxysm has been overcome. // RCint_7.42 //
The juice of <s>rajanī</s> (turmeric) and <s>meghanāda</s> (a plant) drunk with mercury destroys poison;

children.text: sarpākṣī ṭaṅkaṇaṃ vāpi ghṛtena viṣahṛtparam // RCint_7.43 //
children.translated_text: <s>sarpākṣī</s> or <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) with ghee is the supreme poison-remover. // RCint_7.43 //
The marrow of <s>putrajīvaka</s> (Putranjiva), drunk with lemon water,
destroys the poison-paroxysm — just as rain [extinguishes] a forest fire. // RCint_7.44 //

children.text: na krodhite na pittārte na klībe rājayakṣmaṇi /
children.translated_text: Not to one who is angry, nor to one afflicted by <s>pitta</s>, nor to an impotent person, nor in <s>rājayakṣma</s> (consumption),
not to one afflicted by hunger, thirst, exhaustion, heat, or travel, nor in wasting disease,
not to pregnant women, children, or the elderly — and not in the royal palace. // RCint_7.45 //

children.text: na dātavyaṃ na bhoktavyaṃ viṣaṃ vāde kadācana /
children.translated_text: Poison should never be given or consumed in alchemical practice;
but the teacher should consume it to generate confidence in the student. // RCint_7.46 //
Poison: subtypes
<s>Kālakūṭa</s>, <s>vatsanābha</s>, <s>śṛṅgika</s>, and <s>pradīpana</s>,
<s>hālāhala</s>, <s>brahmaputra</s>, <s>hāridra</s>, <s>saktuka</s>,

children.text: saurāṣṭrikaḥ iti proktā viṣabhedā amī nava // RCint_7.47 //
children.translated_text: and <s>saurāṣṭrika</s> — these are declared as the nine varieties of poison. // RCint_7.47 //
<s>Upaviṣa</s> (sub-poisons)
<s>Arka</s> (Calotropis), <s>sehuṇḍa</s> (Euphorbia), <s>dhustūra</s> (Datura), <s>lāṅgalī</s>, and <s>karavīraka</s> (oleander),
<s>guñjā</s> (Abrus) and <s>ahiphena</s> (opium) — these are the seven types of <s>upaviṣa</s> (sub-poisons). // RCint_7.48 //
Mercury: wing-clipping by poison
Mercury ground with these [sub-poisons] becomes wing-clipped;

children.text: mukhaṃ ca jāyate tasya dhātūṃśca grasatetarām // RCint_7.49 //
children.translated_text: it develops a mouth and devours metals all the more. // RCint_7.49 //
<s>Vajra</s> (diamond): subtypes: color
White, red, yellow, and black — Brāhmaṇa and so forth — are the types of diamond;
female, male, and neuter in nature — they should be identified by their characteristics. // RCint_7.50 //
<s>Vajra</s>: male diamond
Round, full-faceted, lustrous, and large —
these are declared as male [diamonds], free from lines and spots. // RCint_7.51 //
Those with lines and spots, six-pointed, are considered female. // RCint_7.52 //
<s>Vajra</s>: female diamond

children.text: trikoṇāḥ pattalā dīrghā vijñeyāste napuṃsakāḥ // RCint_7.53 //
children.translated_text: Those that are triangular, flat, and elongated should be known as neuter. // RCint_7.53 //
<s>Vajra</s>: neuter diamond
<s>Vajra</s>: properties of genders
Among all, males are the best — they are transmuters and mercury-binders;
female diamond is for bodily perfection; neuter is for <s>krāmaṇa</s> (pervasion). // RCint_7.54 //
The Brāhmaṇa [type] is prescribed for <s>rasāyana</s>; the Kṣatriya for disease-destruction;

children.text: vāde vaiśyaṃ vijānīyād vayaḥstambhe turīyakam // RCint_7.55 //
children.translated_text: the Vaiśya should be known for <s>vāda</s> (alchemy); the fourth for age-stabilization. // RCint_7.55 //

children.text: strī tu strīṇāṃ pradātavyā klībe klībaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Female [diamond] should be given to women; neuter to the impotent — likewise;

children.text: sarveṣāṃ sarvadā yojyāḥ puruṣā balavattarāḥ // RCint_7.56 //
children.translated_text: male [diamonds], being more potent, should be used for all, always. // RCint_7.56 //
<s>Vajra</s> (diamond): purification
Placing [the diamond] inside the tuber of <s>vyāghrī</s> (Solanum), subjected to sealed heating seven times,
quenching in horse's urine — it becomes purified with each sealed heating. // RCint_7.57 //
<s>Vajra</s> (diamond): killing
Taking the root of three-year-old <s>nāgavallī</s> (betel) or <s>kārpāsī</s> (cotton plant),

children.text: piṣṭvā tanmadhyagaṃ vajraṃ kṛtvā mūṣāṃ nirodhayet /
children.translated_text: grinding it and placing the diamond in the middle, one should seal it in a crucible;
with seven elephant-dung sealed heatings, it invariably dies. // RCint_7.58 //
<s>Vajra</s> (diamond): killing
The wise one should catch a frog and place it in a bronze vessel;
frightened, it urinates therein — one should immerse the diamond in that urine;

children.text: taptaṃ taptaṃ ca bahudhā vajrasyaivaṃ mṛtirbhavet // RCint_7.59 //
children.translated_text: heating it repeatedly many times — thus the killing of diamond is accomplished. // RCint_7.59 //
<s>Vajra</s> (diamond): killing
In <s>kulattha</s> (horse gram) decoction combined with <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida) and <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), one should cast

children.text: taptaṃ taptaṃ punarvajraṃ bhavedbhasma trisaptadhā // RCint_7.60 //
children.translated_text: the diamond, heating it repeatedly — it becomes ash in twenty-one times. // RCint_7.60 //
<s>Vajra</s> (diamond): ash: use
Wherever diamond is present in mercury, that mercury is called <s>amṛta</s> (nectar);

children.text: bhasmībhāvagataṃ yuktyā vajravat kurute tanum // RCint_7.61 //
children.translated_text: diamond ash, [combined] skillfully, makes the body diamond-like. // RCint_7.61 //

children.text:
<vaikrānta:: śodhana>
vaikrāntaṃ vajravacchodhyaṃ nīlaṃ śvetaṃ ca lohitam /
children.translated_text:
<s>Vaikrānta</s>: purification
<s>Vaikrānta</s> should be purified like diamond; it comes in blue, white, and red.
It possesses the characteristics of diamond but cannot withstand burning or striking. // RCint_7.62 //
<s>Vaikrānta</s>: physical properties
<s>Vaikrānta</s>: killing
One should quench it, heated repeatedly, in horse's urine twenty-one times;
coated with the five parts of the <s>uttaravāruṇī</s> (a plant), placed in a crucible, with sealed heatings // RCint_7.63 //
called elephant[-dung type], <s>vaikrānta</s> dies in seven [sealed heatings].

children.text: bhasmībhūtaṃ tu vaikrāntaṃ vajrasthāne niyojayet // RCint_7.64 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s> reduced to ash should be used in place of diamond. // RCint_7.64 //
<s>Vaikrānta</s>: substitute for diamond
The nine gems (<s>navaratna</s>)
Male diamond, <s>garuḍodgāra</s> (emerald), <s>māṇikya</s> (ruby), <s>vāsavopala</s> (sapphire),
<s>vaidūrya</s> (cat's eye), <s>puṣpa</s> (topaz), <s>gomedha</s> (hessonite), pearl, and coral —
these are the nine gems, comparable to the nectar-essence. // RCint_7.65 //
Jewels: purification
One should steam in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus) with the juice of <s>jayantī</s> (a plant);
