for <s>maṇi</s> (gems), pearls, and corals, purification occurs in one <s>yāma</s> (three hours). // RCint_7.66 //
Jewels: special purification
<s>Māṇikya</s> (ruby) is purified by acid; pearls by <s>jayantī</s> [juice];
coral by the alkali group; <s>tārkṣya</s> (emerald) by cow's milk. // RCint_7.67 //
<s>Puṣyarāga</s> (topaz) by [fermented] preparations combined with <s>kulattha</s> (horse gram) decoction;
diamond by <s>taṇḍulīya</s> (Amaranthus) water; <s>nīla</s> (sapphire) by indigo juice. // RCint_7.68 //
<s>Gomedha</s> (hessonite) by <s>rocanā</s> (bile-stone); <s>vaidūrya</s> (cat's eye) by <s>triphalā</s> water.
Jewels: purification imparts additional qualities
Even if unpurified, pearls and others have no defect according to the treatises;
but even so, purification specifically increases their qualities. // RCint_7.69 //
Metals and subsidiary minerals: purification

children.text: amlakṣāravipācitaṃ tu sakalaṃ lauhaṃ viśuddhaṃ bhavenmākṣīko'pi śilāpi tutthagaganaṃ tālaṃ ca samyaktathā /
children.translated_text: All metals cooked with acid and alkali become purified; likewise <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrites), realgar, <s>tuttha</s> (copper sulphate), mica, <s>tāla</s> (orpiment) properly;

children.text: muktāvidrumaśuktikātha capalāḥ śaṅkhā varāṭāḥ śubhā jāyante'mṛtasannibhāḥ payasi ca kṣiptaḥ śubhaḥ syādbaliḥ // RCint_7.70 //
children.translated_text: pearls, coral, shells, mercury, conch, and cowries become auspicious and nectar-like when cooked in milk; and the sacrificial offering should be auspicious. // RCint_7.70 //
Jewels: killing
With realgar, sulphur, and <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment) ground with <s>lakuca</s> (breadfruit) juice,
gems other than diamond are killed in eight sealed heatings indeed. // RCint_7.71 //
Jewels: killing
With <s>kumārī</s> (aloe), <s>taṇḍulīya</s> (Amaranthus), and breast-milk, one should quench

children.text: pratyekaṃ saptavelaṃ ca taptataptāni kṛtsnaśaḥ // RCint_7.72 //
children.translated_text: each one, heated repeatedly seven times, completely. // RCint_7.72 //
Pearls, corals, and all gems without exception
of various colors die instantly — there is no doubt in this. // RCint_7.73 //
All gems should be purified and killed like diamond. // RCint_7.74 //
Jewels: purification and killing
<s>Haritāla</s> (orpiment): purification

children.text: tālakaṃ poṭṭalīṃ baddhvā sacūrṇe kāñjike kṣipet /
children.translated_text: Orpiment, tied in a poultice, should be placed in <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel) with powder;

children.text: dolāyantreṇa yāmaikaṃ tataḥ kūṣmāṇḍaje rase // RCint_7.75 //
children.translated_text: in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus) for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours); then in <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s> (winter melon) juice, // RCint_7.75 //
cooked in sesame oil for one <s>yāma</s>, then in <s>triphalā</s> water for one <s>yāma</s>;

children.text: dolāyantre caturyāmaṃ pakvaṃ śudhyati tālakam // RCint_7.76 //
children.translated_text: cooked in a <s>dolāyantra</s> for four <s>yāmas</s> (twelve hours), the orpiment is purified. // RCint_7.76 //

children.text: sa śuddhaḥ kāntivīrye ca kurute mṛtyunāśanaḥ // RCint_7.77 //
children.translated_text: Purified, it produces radiance and virility, and destroys death. // RCint_7.77 //
<s>Haritāla</s>: purified: medicinal properties
<s>Haritāla</s>: <s>sattva</s> (essence): extraction
Lac, <s>rājī</s> (mustard), sesame, <s>śigru</s> (drumstick), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), salt, and jaggery,
mixed with half the amount of orpiment, should be sealed in a perforated crucible;
heated in a <s>pātāla</s> (underground) apparatus, the <s>sattva</s> (essence) certainly falls. // RCint_7.78 //
<s>Haritāla</s>: <s>sattva</s>: extraction
<s>Jaipāla</s> (Croton) <s>sattva</s>, <s>vātāri</s> (castor) seeds, mixed with orpiment,

children.text: kūpīsthaṃ vālukāyantre sattvaṃ muñcati yāmataḥ // RCint_7.79 //
children.translated_text: placed in a flask in a <s>vālukāyantra</s> (sand-bath), releases its <s>sattva</s> in one <s>yāma</s> (three hours). // RCint_7.79 //
<s>Indusundarī</s> (a preparation)
Roasted <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) and <s>tāla</s> (orpiment), wrapped in iron leaf,

children.text: guṭikā gurumārgeṇa dhmātā syād indusundarī // RCint_7.80 //
children.translated_text: formed into a pill, blown by the teacher's method, becomes <s>indusundarī</s>. // RCint_7.80 //
(unclear passage)
For the binding of <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar), <s>dāra</s> (lead), and <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment),
the outer coating on iron leaf is with rice-charcoal juice. // RCint_7.81 //

children.text: tālavacca śilāsattvaṃ grāhyaṃ taireva bheṣajaiḥ // RCint_7.82 //
children.translated_text: Realgar <s>sattva</s> should be extracted like orpiment, with the same medicines. // RCint_7.82 //
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> (realgar): <s>sattva</s>: extraction

children.text: tulyaṃ ṭaṅkaṇakaṃ grāhyaṃ dhmāte sattvaṃ ca tutthake // RCint_7.83 //
children.translated_text: An equal amount of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) should be taken; when blown, the <s>sattva</s> of <s>tuttha</s> is obtained. // RCint_7.83 //
<s>Tuttha</s> (copper sulphate): <s>sattva</s>: extraction
<s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrites): <s>sattva</s>: extraction
Wool, lac, and jaggery, together with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax),
should be ground together and made into pills carefully with goat's milk;

children.text: dhmātāstāpyasya tīvrāgnau sattvaṃ muñcati lohitam // RCint_7.84 //
children.translated_text: when blown in intense fire, <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites) releases its red <s>sattva</s> (essence). // RCint_7.84 //
Great minerals (<s>mahārasa</s>): <s>sattva</s>: extraction
Thus orpiment, realgar, minerals, <s>vimalā</s> (iron), <s>kharpara</s> (zinc), and others
release their respective <s>sattvas</s> (essences) by blowing in a crucible fire. // RCint_7.85 //
<s>Kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol): <s>sattva</s> extraction (?), softening (?)
<s>Khaga</s> (kāsīsa), roasted with realgar or sulphur, pounded,

children.text: mudritastāmrapātreṇa liptaḥ syād dhmāpito mṛduḥ // RCint_7.86 //
children.translated_text: sealed with a copper vessel, coated and blown — it becomes soft. // RCint_7.86 //
<s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrites): <s>sattva</s>: extraction

children.text: samagandhaṃ caturyāmaṃ paktvā tāpyaṃ tataḥ pacet /
children.translated_text: Cooking <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites) with equal sulphur for four <s>yāmas</s> (twelve hours), then cooking further
with half sulphur for two <s>yāmas</s> (six hours), combined with half roasted <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,

children.text: andhamūṣāgataṃ dhmātaṃ sattvaṃ muñcati śulvavat // RCint_7.87 //
children.translated_text: placed in a blind crucible and blown — it releases <s>sattva</s> like copper. // RCint_7.87 //
Pill from various substances for color enhancement (gold production)
<s>Tāpya</s> (pyrites), sulphur, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) should be revolved in an ash-crucible;
a yellow pill is produced that effects color enhancement. // RCint_7.88 //
Pill for color enhancement
Seven pieces of <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites) should be burnt between lead and clay;
blown with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) alone, it becomes a pill as before. // RCint_7.89 //
<s>Bhūnāga</s> (earthworm): <s>sattva</s>: extraction
The wise one should immediately take earthworms and feed them to a peacock,

children.text: athavā kukkuṭaṃ vīraṃ kṛtvā mandiramāgatam // RCint_7.90 //
children.translated_text: or to a brave rooster, and bring it home. // RCint_7.90 //
Taking its excrement and urine, discarding the first portion,

children.text: āloḍya kṣāramadhvājyair dhamet sattvārtham ādarāt // RCint_7.91 //
children.translated_text: mixing with alkali, honey, and ghee, one should blow for the purpose of extracting the <s>sattva</s> with care. // RCint_7.91 //
It releases <s>sattva</s> like copper; by drinking the water sealed with its imprint,

children.text: naśyati jaṅgamaviṣaṃ sthāvaraṃ ca na saṃśayaḥ // RCint_7.92 //
children.translated_text: both animal and vegetable poisons are destroyed — there is no doubt. // RCint_7.92 //
<s>Bhūnāga</s> (earthworm): <s>sattva</s>: extraction
Earthworms cooked in milk, with their clay and roasted <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,

children.text: bhṛṣṭaiścakrīṃ vidhāyātha pātyaṃ sattvaṃ prayatnataḥ // RCint_7.93 //
children.translated_text: made into discs — the <s>sattva</s> should be extracted with effort. // RCint_7.93 //
Wherever there is a subsidiary mineral component in mercury, the combination with its <s>sattva</s>
should be done; one who desires mastery of mercury [should know that] this produces greater results. // RCint_7.94 //
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> (realgar): purification
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) is purified in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus) with <s>jayantikā</s> juice,
for one day in goat's urine or in <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta) juice. // RCint_7.95 //

children.text: śilā snigdhā kaṭustiktā kaphaghnī lekhanī sarā // RCint_7.96 //
children.translated_text: Realgar is unctuous, pungent, bitter; it destroys <s>kapha</s>, is a scraping agent, and laxative. // RCint_7.96 //
<s>Manaḥśilā</s>: purified: medicinal properties

<s>Manaḥśilā</s>: removes blackness
By cooking in a flask and similar vessels, it removes the blackness of gold.
In pungent oil, realgar flows even within <s>campaka</s> (Michelia) and banana [stems]. // RCint_7.97 //
<s>Manaḥśilā</s>: liquefaction
<s>Rasaka</s> (zinc carbonate): purification

children.text: naramūtre ca gomūtre jalāmle vā sasaindhave /
children.translated_text: In human urine, cow's urine, or sour water with rock salt,

children.text: saptāhaṃ tridinaṃ vāpi pakvaḥ śudhyati kharparaḥ // RCint_7.98 //
children.translated_text: for seven days or three days, when cooked, <s>kharpara</s> (zinc ore) is purified. // RCint_7.98 //
<s>Tuttha</s> (copper sulphate): purification
One mercury, one <s>pīti</s> (yellow), four <s>bhekas</s> (frog-minerals), three <s>dārakas</s>,
ground with seed-paste, the frog[-mineral] bound in a dark chamber with <s>pika</s> (crow) flames. // RCint_7.99 //
<s>Tuttha</s> should be ground with its excrement, equally or in one-tenth proportion;
or grinding with equal <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), one should cook in a light sealed heating;

children.text: tutthaṃ śuddhaṃ bhavetkṣaudre puṭitaṃ vā viśeṣataḥ // RCint_7.100 //
children.translated_text: <s>tuttha</s> becomes purified; sealed-heated in honey is especially [effective]. // RCint_7.100 //

children.text: vāntirbhrāntiryadā na stastadā śuddhiṃ vinirdiśet // RCint_7.101 //
children.translated_text: When vomiting and dizziness do not occur, then purification should be declared. // RCint_7.101 //
<s>Tuttha</s>: purified: bodily reaction

children.text: lekhanaṃ bhedi ca jñeyaṃ tutthaṃ kaṇḍukrimipraṇut // RCint_7.102 //
children.translated_text: <s>Tuttha</s> should be known as a scraping and breaking agent; it removes itching and worms. // RCint_7.102 //
<s>Tuttha</s>: purified: medicinal properties
<s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrites): purification
With the exudate of <s>agastya</s> (Sesbania) leaves, well-ground <s>śigru</s> (drumstick) root,

children.text: tanmadhye puṭitaṃ śudhyet tāpyaṃ tvamlena pācitam // RCint_7.103 //
children.translated_text: <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites) sealed-heated in their midst is purified; or cooked with acid. // RCint_7.103 //
<s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrites): purification
One part of <s>sindhu</s> (rock salt) and three parts of <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrites),
with lemon juice or citron juice, // RCint_7.104 //

children.text: kṛtvā tadāyase pātre lauhadarvyā ca cālayet /
children.translated_text: placing that in an iron vessel and stirring with an iron ladle,
one should cook with gentle fire until it becomes vermilion-colored;
the <s>mākṣika</s> should be known as well-purified — it should be employed in all diseases. // RCint_7.105 //
<s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrites): killing
Adding a quarter part of sulphur to <s>mākṣika</s>, one should grind;
with <s>uruvūka</s> (castor) oil, then one should make a good disc. // RCint_7.106 //
Holding it in a saucer-container, one should give an elephant-dung sealed heating;

children.text: sindūrābhaṃ bhavedbhasma mākṣikasya na saṃśayaḥ // RCint_7.107 //
children.translated_text: the ash of <s>mākṣika</s> becomes vermilion-colored — there is no doubt. // RCint_7.107 //
<s>Mākṣika</s>: killed: medicinal properties
<s>Mākṣika</s> is bitter-sweet; it removes delusion, hemorrhoids, worms, and <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases);
it destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, is strengthening, a carrier of formulations, and a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenating agent). // RCint_7.108 //
<s>Vimalā</s> (iron ore): purification
Steaming in lemon juice, or in <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s> juice,

children.text: rambhātoyena vā pāko ghasraṃ vimalaśuddhaye // RCint_7.109 //
children.translated_text: or cooking in banana-stem water for a day — for the purification of <s>vimalā</s>. // RCint_7.109 //

children.text: sakṛdbhṛṅgāmbunā svinnaṃ kāsīsaṃ nirmalaṃ bhavet // RCint_7.110 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kāsīsa</s> steamed once in <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta) water becomes pure. // RCint_7.110 //
<s>Kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol): purification
<s>Kāsīsa</s>: purified: medicinal properties
<s>Kāsīsa</s> is cooling, unctuous; it removes <s>śvitra</s> (leucoderma) and eye-diseases;
it pacifies <s>pitta</s> and epilepsy, and produces qualities like mercury. // RCint_7.111 //
<s>Kānta</s> (magnetite): purification
Salts and alkalis should be cast in <s>śobhāñjana</s> (drumstick) juice;
combined with the sour group, first it should be treated in sunlight for a day. // RCint_7.112 //
With those juices, the wise one should cook in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus) for a day;
for the purification of <s>kāntapāṣāṇa</s> (magnetite), one should then proceed with mercury operations. // RCint_7.113 //

children.text:
<money cowrie:: phys. properties>
pītābhā granthilā pṛṣṭhe dīrghavṛttā varāṭikā /
children.translated_text:
Cowrie shell: physical properties
A cowrie that is yellowish, knotted on the back, elongated-oval.
Cowrie shell: optimal weight
One weighing one and a half <s>niṣkas</s> is the best; one <s>niṣka</s> is middling;
one weighing three-quarters of a <s>niṣka</s> is declared the lowest. // RCint_7.114 //
A cowrie steamed in <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel) for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours) attains purification. // RCint_7.115 //
Cowrie shell: purification
Cowrie shell: purified: medicinal properties
It destroys acid-gastritis and similar colics, and removes <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption) and wasting;
it is pungent, heating, a digestive stimulant, aphrodisiac, bitter, and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>;
it is prescribed for the <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation) of mercury, and is recommended among <s>viḍa</s> substances. // RCint_7.116 //
<s>Darada</s> (cinnabar): purification
<s>Darada</s> (cinnabar) treated with ewe's milk and the sour group
seven times carefully, certainly attains purification. // RCint_7.117 //
<s>Darada</s>: purified: medicinal properties
<s>Hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar), born from mercury and sulphur, is bitter, hot, and divine;
it removes urinary disorders and <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), promotes taste, and increases intellect and digestive fire. // RCint_7.118 //
Purification of various substances

children.text: sauvīraṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ śaṅkhaṃ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ gairikaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Sauvīra</s> (antimony), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), conch-shell, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, and <s>gairika</s> (red ochre) —
these should be purified like cowrie shell; they become free from defects. // RCint_7.119 //
<s>Kāsīsa</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and others are purified by lemon juice. // RCint_7.120 //
<s>Kāsīsa</s>: purification
<s>Srotoñjana</s> (stream-collyrium): purification
<s>Srotoñjana</s>, treated with cow's urine, ghee, honey, and fat,

children.text: vibhāvitaṃ ca śuddhaṃ syādrasabandhakaraṃ param // RCint_7.121 //
children.translated_text: becomes purified — it is the supreme mercury-binding agent. // RCint_7.121 //
<s>Nīlāñjana</s> (blue collyrium): purification
<s>Nīlāñjana</s>, powdered and treated with lemon juice,
for one day in sunlight, becomes purified — it should be employed in preparations. // RCint_7.122 //
Extraction of oil from seeds
Taking the juice of well-ripened <s>bhānu</s> (sun-plant) leaves, one should keep it;
the powder of all seeds, whether mentioned or unmentioned, separately,

children.text: ātape muñcate tailaṃ sādhyāsādhyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ // RCint_7.123 //
children.translated_text: releases oil in sunlight — [even] the seemingly impossible becomes possible, without doubt. // RCint_7.123 //
Now we expound the chapter on practical applications. // RCint_8.1 //
RCint, 8
Herein, four verses are to be understood first. // RCint_8.2 //
For those with active digestive fire, the view of <s>Caraka</s> is that non-contradictory medicines of fruits, roots, and other herbs

children.text: tadyadi rasānupītaṃ bhavettadā tvaritam ullāghaḥ // RCint_8.3 //
children.translated_text: if taken along with mercury preparations, then recovery is swift. // RCint_8.3 //
The dose should be increased by the learned when there is benefit to both [medicine and patient] progressively;

children.text: mātrāhrāsaḥ kāryo vaiguṇye tyāgasamaye ca // RCint_8.4 //
children.translated_text: the dose should be decreased when there is adverse effect, and at the time of discontinuation. // RCint_8.4 //
Herbs growing at ant-hills, wells, tree-bases, roadways, temples, and cremation grounds,

children.text: jātā vidhināpi hṛtā oṣadhyaḥ siddhidā na syuḥ // RCint_8.5 //
children.translated_text: even if collected according to proper method, do not bestow efficacy. // RCint_8.5 //

children.text: kacakaciti na dantāgre kurvanti samāni ketakīrajasā /
children.translated_text: Powders of mercury, subsidiary minerals, and metals, which do not make a 'crunch' sound between the teeth like <s>ketakī</s> (screwpine) pollen,
should be used in preparations. // RCint_8.6 //
For its suitability in all preparations and for the killing of mercury, we describe the <s>śāmbhavīmudrā</s> (Śambhu's seal). // RCint_8.7 //
<s>Antardhūma</s> (internal fumigation) (?)
Heat below, water above, mercury and sulphur in the middle —

children.text: yadi syātsudṛḍhā mudrā mandabhāgyo'pi sidhyati // RCint_8.8 //
children.translated_text: if the seal is very firm, even the unfortunate one succeeds. // RCint_8.8 //

children.text: yadi kāryam ayoyantraṃ tadā tatsāra iṣyate // RCint_8.9 //
children.translated_text: If the apparatus is to be made of iron, then it should be of <s>sāra</s> (steel). // RCint_8.9 //

children.text: same gandhe tu rogaghno dviguṇe rājayakṣmanut /
children.translated_text: With equal sulphur assimilated, it destroys diseases; with double, it removes <s>rājayakṣma</s> (consumption);
when threefold sulphur is assimilated, it destroys the pride of lustful women. // RCint_8.10 //
With fourfold, one becomes brilliant, versed in all treatises;
with fivefold, one becomes a <s>Siddha</s> (perfected being); with sixfold, one conquers death. // RCint_8.11 //

children.text: ṣaḍguṇe rogaghna itiyaduktaṃ tattu bahirdhūmamūrcchāyām evādhigantavyam tatra gandhasya samagrajāraṇābhāvāt svarṇādipiṣṭikāyāmapi rītiriyam // RCint_8.12 //
children.translated_text: The statement 'sixfold destroys diseases' is to be understood only in the context of <s>bahirdhūma-mūrcchā</s> (external fumigation solidification), because there the sulphur is not completely assimilated; this procedure also applies to gold <s>piṣṭikā</s> (paste) and the like. // RCint_8.12 //

children.text: vaṃśe vā māhiṣe śṛṅge sthāpayet sādhitaṃ rasam // RCint_8.13 //
children.translated_text: The prepared mercury should be stored in a bamboo [container] or in a buffalo horn. // RCint_8.13 //
Medicine: storage

children.text: amṛtaṃ ca viṣaṃ proktaṃ śivena ca rasāyanam /
children.translated_text: It is declared by <s>Śiva</s> that [mercury properly prepared] is <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) and <s>rasāyana</s>;

children.text: amṛtaṃ vidhisaṃyuktaṃ vidhihīnaṃ tu tadviṣam // RCint_8.14 //
children.translated_text: it is nectar when prepared with proper method; without method, it is poison. // RCint_8.14 //
<s>Gandhāmṛta</s> (sulphur-nectar preparation)
Ash-mercury and double sulphur, ground a hundred times with <s>kanyā</s> (aloe) water,
sealed and cooked in a light sealed heating; after removal, with honey and ghee, // RCint_8.15 //
in a <s>niṣka</s> dose, it destroys old age and death — this mercury is <s>gandhāmṛta</s> (sulphur-nectar).

children.text: samūlaṃ bhṛṅgarājaṃ tu chāyāśuṣkaṃ vimardayet // RCint_8.16 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta) with roots, dried in shade, should be ground; // RCint_8.16 //
with an equal amount of <s>triphalā</s> powder, and white sugar equal to all,
one <s>pala</s> consumed [along with it] — within a year it removes death and old age. // RCint_8.17 //
<s>Hemasundararasa</s> (Beautiful Gold Mercury)
One-quarter portion of killed mercury should be combined with gold ash;
mixed with milk, ghee, and honey, one <s>māṣa</s> in a <s>kānta</s> (magnetic iron) vessel, // RCint_8.18 //
licked [in doses] up to six <s>māṣas</s> — it destroys old age and death.
One <s>karṣa</s> of <s>vākucī</s> (Psoralea) powder, soaked in <s>dhātrī</s> (gooseberry) juice,
as an adjuvant, should be licked daily — this is the mercury [called] <s>Hemasundara</s>. // RCint_8.19 //
<s>Candrodayarasa</s> (Moonrise Mercury)
One <s>pala</s> of soft gold leaf, eight <s>palas</s> of mercury, sixteen of sulphur,

children.text: śoṇaiḥ sukārpāsabhavaprasūnaiḥ sarvaṃ vimardyātha kumārikādbhiḥ // RCint_8.20 //
children.translated_text: with red flowers of the good cotton plant, all ground with <s>kumārikā</s> (aloe) water. // RCint_8.20 //

children.text: tatkācakumbhe nihitaṃ sugāḍhe mṛtkarpaṭais taddivasatrayaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Placed in a well-sealed glass jar, [sealed] with clay and cloth, for three days

children.text: pacetkramāgnau sikatākhyayantre tato rasaḥ pallavarāgaramyaḥ // RCint_8.21 //
children.translated_text: cooked with progressive fire in a <s>sikatāyantra</s> (sand-bath) — then a mercury of the beautiful color of a tender leaf [is produced]. // RCint_8.21 //

children.text: saṃgṛhya caitasya palaṃ palaṃ palāni catvāri karpūrarajas tathaiva /
children.translated_text: Taking one <s>pala</s> of this, and separately four <s>palas</s> of camphor powder,

children.text: jātīphalaṃ śoṣaṇam indrapuṣpaṃ kastūrikāyā iha śāṇa ekaḥ // RCint_8.22 //
children.translated_text: nutmeg, <s>śoṣaṇa</s> (dried ginger), <s>indrapuṣpa</s> (Indian hemp), and one <s>śāṇa</s> (a measure) of musk. // RCint_8.22 //
This is called <s>Candrodaya</s> (Moonrise); one <s>valla</s> (pill) of it, consumed as a pill within a betel leaf,
suddenly shatters the excessive arrogance of hundreds of women intoxicated with passion. // RCint_8.23 //

children.text: śṛtaṃ ghanībhūtam atīvadugdhaṃ gurūṇi māṃsāni samaṇḍakāni /
children.translated_text: Boiled and thickened concentrated milk, heavy meats with eggs,
and cakes made of <s>māṣa</s> (black gram) flour are the suitable diet; other [foods are also] bliss-giving here. // RCint_8.24 //
At the time of love-making and after intercourse, this lord of mercury should be consumed;
it certainly destroys the pride of women. // RCint_8.25 //

children.text: kṛtrimaṃ sthāvaraṃ caiva jaṅgamaṃ caiva yad viṣam /
children.translated_text: Artificial, vegetable, and animal poisons —

children.text: na vikārāya bhavati sādhakendrasya vatsarāt // RCint_8.26 //
children.translated_text: within a year, they do not cause harm to the supreme practitioner. // RCint_8.26 //
Just as <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s> (death-conqueror mantra) by practice conquers death for embodied beings,
so too this [preparation] destroys old age and death for the supreme practitioner. // RCint_8.27 //
It is a destroyer of wrinkles and grey hair, a stabilizer of youth for the embodied,
a shatterer of all diseases, a lion against the multitude of ailments;

children.text: gṛhe ca rasarāḍayaṃ bhavati yasya candrodayaḥ /
children.translated_text: one in whose house this <s>Candrodaya</s> mercury-king resides,

children.text: sa pañcaśaradarpito mṛgadṛśāṃ bhaved vallabhaḥ // RCint_8.28 //
children.translated_text: he, with the pride of the five-arrowed one (Kāmadeva), becomes the beloved of doe-eyed women. // RCint_8.28 //
<s>Mṛtyuñjayarasa</s> (Death-Conquering Mercury)

children.text: baliḥ sūto nimbūrasavimṛdito bhasmasikatāhvaye yantre kṛtvā samaravikaṇāṭaṅkaṇarajaḥ /
children.translated_text: Mercury with its sacrificial substance, ground with lemon juice, placed in a <s>bhasma-sikatā</s> (ash sand-bath) apparatus, with equal <s>ravi</s> (Calotropis) seed and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) powder,

children.text: trighasraṃ luṅgāmbholavakadalitaḥ kṣaudrahaviṣā vilīḍho māṣaiko dalayati samastaṃ gadagaṇam // RCint_8.29 //
children.translated_text: for three days, softened with clove-banana water; licked in one <s>māṣa</s> dose with honey and ghee — it shatters the entire host of diseases. // RCint_8.29 //

children.text: jarāṃ varṣaikena kṣapayati ca puṣṭiṃ vitanute tanau tejaskāraṃ ramayati vadhūnāmapi śatam /
children.translated_text: It removes old age in one year, produces nourishment, creates brilliance in the body, and delights even a hundred women;

children.text: rasaḥ śrīmānmṛtyuñjaya iti girīśena gaditaḥ prabhāvaṃ ko vānyaḥ kathayitumapāraṃ prabhavati // RCint_8.30 //
children.translated_text: this glorious mercury is called <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s> (Death-Conqueror) by Lord <s>Girīśa</s> (Śiva); who else can describe its boundless power? // RCint_8.30 //
<s>Gandhadāha</s> (sulphur-burning procedure)

children.text: piṣṭiḥ kāryā gandhakenendumauler ūrdhvaṃ cādho gandhamādāya tulyam /
children.translated_text: A <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste) should be made with sulphur of the moon-crested one (mercury); taking equal sulphur above and below,

children.text: dhāryā madhye pakvamūṣā tuṣāgnau sthāpyā cetthaṃ manyate gandhadāhaḥ // RCint_8.31 //
children.translated_text: held in the middle in a fired crucible, placed in a husk-fire — this is considered the <s>gandhadāha</s> (sulphur-burning). // RCint_8.31 //
<s>Ānandasūtarasa</s> (Bliss Mercury)

children.text: śuddhaṃ rasaṃ samaviṣaṃ praharaṃ vimardya tadgolakaṃ kanakacāruphale nidhāya /
children.translated_text: Purified mercury with equal poison, ground for one <s>prahara</s> (three hours), formed into a ball and placed in a beautiful golden fruit [container],

children.text: dolāgataṃ pañcadinaṃ viṣamuṣṭitoye prakṣālya tatpunarapīha tathā dvivāram // RCint_8.32 //
children.translated_text: placed in a <s>dolā</s> (swing apparatus) for five days in poison-decoction water, washed, then again likewise twice. // RCint_8.32 //

children.text: tatsūtake giriśalocanayugmagandhaṃ yuktyāvajārya kuru bhasma samaṃ ca tasya /
children.translated_text: To that mercury, assimilate by proper method sulphur equal to three eyes of <s>Śiva</s> (i.e., three parts); and make ash equal to it;

children.text: vaikrāntabhasma jayapālanavāṃśakārdhaṃ sarvair viṣaṃ dviguṇitaṃ mṛditaṃ ca khalve // RCint_8.33 //
children.translated_text: <s>vaikrānta</s> ash, half a ninth part of <s>jayapāla</s> (Croton), and double the poison of all — ground in the mortar. // RCint_8.33 //

children.text: ghasratrayaṃ kanakabhṛṅgarasena gāḍham āveśya bhājanatale viṣadhūpabhāji /
children.translated_text: For three days, thoroughly saturated with golden <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta) juice, deposited at the bottom of a vessel that holds poison-fumigation,

children.text: bhṛṅgadraveṇa śithilaṃ laghukācakūpyām āpūrya ruddhavadanāṃ sikatākhyayantre // RCint_8.34 //
children.translated_text: loosened with <s>bhṛṅga</s> juice, filled in a small glass flask, sealing its mouth, in a <s>sikatāyantra</s> (sand-bath). // RCint_8.34 //

children.text: tāṃ vāsarārtham upadīpya nisargaśītāṃ dṛṣṭvā vicūrṇya gadaśāliṣu śālimātram /
children.translated_text: Heating it for half a day, observing it naturally cooled, powdering it — among the host of diseases, a rice-grain measure

children.text: ānandasūtam akhilāmayakumbhisiṃhaṃ gadyāṇakārdhasitayā saha dehi paścāt // RCint_8.35 //
children.translated_text: [of this] <s>Ānandasūta</s> (Bliss Mercury), a lion to the pot-elephant of all diseases, should be given afterwards with half a <s>gadyāṇaka</s> of white sugar. // RCint_8.35 //
Employ openly the adjuvant suitable to each disease; obtain abundant worship from kings;

children.text: kīrtyā diśo dhavalaya sphuradindukāntyā vaidyeśvareti virudaṃ bhaja vaidyarāja // RCint_8.36 //
children.translated_text: whiten the directions with fame of shining moon-radiance; embrace the title <s>Vaidyeśvara</s> (Lord of Physicians), O King of Physicians! // RCint_8.36 //
<s>Arkānaleśvararasa</s> (Sun-Fire Lord Mercury)
<s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrites) and gold should be revolved with sulphur and powdered;

children.text: rasaṃ gandhād dvibhāgaṃ ca sikatāyantragaṃ pacet // RCint_8.37 //
children.translated_text: mercury double the sulphur should be cooked in a <s>sikatāyantra</s> (sand-bath). // RCint_8.37 //

children.text: dinamevaṃ ca tāraṃ vā jarārogaharaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: For one day thus — or silver — it is a great destroyer of old age and disease.

children.text: rasena piṣṭvā svarṇaṃ vā tāpyaṃ paścād vimiśrayet // RCint_8.38 //
children.translated_text: Gold ground with mercury, or <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites) should then be mixed. // RCint_8.38 //
<s>Ravicandreśvararasa</s> (Sun-Moon Lord Mercury)
In place of <s>tāpya</s>, killed <s>tāla</s> (orpiment) may be used by some for silver-work;
sealed heatings equal to the mercury should be given; or with sulphur for increasing potency. // RCint_8.39 //
<s>Prāṇikalpadrumagutī</s> (Life Wish-Tree Pill)

children.text: sūtaṃ gandhaṃ kāntapāṣāṇamiśraṃ brāhmair bījair mardayed ekaghasram /
children.translated_text: Mercury, sulphur, and <s>kāntapāṣāṇa</s> (magnetite) mixed, should be ground with <s>brāhmī</s> (Bacopa) seeds for a whole day;

children.text: golaṃ kṛtvā ṭaṅkaṇena praveṣṭya paścānmṛtsnāgomayābhyāṃ dhamettam // RCint_8.40 //
children.translated_text: making a ball, enclosing it with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), then covering with clay and cow-dung, one should blow. // RCint_8.40 //

children.text: śuṣkaṃ yantre sattvapātapradhāne kiṭṭaḥ sūto baddhatāmeti nūnam /
children.translated_text: Dried in an apparatus designed primarily for <s>sattva</s> extraction, the slag — mercury certainly attains binding;

children.text: baddhaṃ paścāt sārakācaprayogāddhemnā tulyaṃ sūtamāvartayettu // RCint_8.41 //
children.translated_text: the bound [mercury] should then be revolved with gold in equal amount, using <s>sārakāca</s> (quartz) preparation. // RCint_8.41 //

children.text: vaktre golaḥ sthāpito vatsarārthaṃ rogān sarvānhanti saukhyaṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: The pill placed in the mouth for a year destroys all diseases and produces happiness;

children.text: yadvā dugdhe golakaṃ pācayitvā dadyād dugdhaṃ pippalībhiḥ kṣaye tat // RCint_8.42 //
children.translated_text: or, cooking the pill in milk, one should give that milk with <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper) in consumption. // RCint_8.42 //

children.text: lauhe pātre pācayitvā tu deyaṃ śuṣke pāṇḍau kāmale pittaroge /
children.translated_text: Cooked in an iron vessel, it should be given in dry conditions, anemia, jaundice, and <s>pitta</s> diseases;

children.text: vāte golaṃ vyoṣavātāritaile paktvā tailaṃ gandhayuktaṃ dadīta // RCint_8.43 //
children.translated_text: for <s>vāta</s> [disorders], the pill cooked in <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents) and <s>vātāri</s> (castor) oil — that sulphur-infused oil should be given. // RCint_8.43 //
For the removal of <s>kapha</s>, the pill should be cooked in the juices of <s>bhārṅgī</s> (Clerodendrum), <s>muṇḍī</s>, <s>kāsamarda</s> (Cassia), and <s>aṭarūṣa</s> (Adhatoda);

children.text: kāse śvāse taṃ ca dadyāt kaṣāyaṃ mādhvīkāktaṃ pippalīcūrṇayuktam // RCint_8.44 //
children.translated_text: in cough and asthma, that decoction should be given, combined with honey and <s>pippalī</s> powder. // RCint_8.44 //

children.text: yasmin roge yaḥ kaṣāyo'sti coktastasmin golaṃ pācayitvā kaṣāye /
children.translated_text: In whichever disease whichever decoction is prescribed, the pill should be cooked in that decoction

children.text: dadyāttattadroganāśāya pathyaṃ tattadroge kīrtitaṃ yattadeva // RCint_8.45 //
children.translated_text: and given for the destruction of that disease; the diet prescribed for that disease is the same. // RCint_8.45 //

children.text: ukto golaḥ prāṇikalpadrumo'yaṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā yojayedbhaktiyogāt /
children.translated_text: This pill is called <s>Prāṇikalpadruma</s> (Life Wish-Tree); having performed worship, one should employ it with devotion.
<s>Rasaśārdūlarasa</s> (Tiger Mercury)

children.text: rasasya dviguṇaṃ gandhaṃ śuddhaṃ saṃmardayed dinam /
children.translated_text: Sulphur double the quantity of mercury, purified, should be ground for one day;
for each metal, add killed metal equal to the mercury — eight metals [in total]. // RCint_8.46 //
<s>Brāhmī</s> (Bacopa), <s>jayantī</s> (Sesbania), <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex), <s>madhuyaṣṭī</s> (licorice), <s>punarnavā</s> (Boerhavia),
<s>nīlikā</s> (indigo), <s>girikarṇī</s>, <s>arka</s> (Calotropis), <s>kṛṣṇadhattūra</s> (black Datura), and <s>yava</s> (barley); // RCint_8.47 //
<s>āṭarūṣa</s> (Adhatoda) and <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade) — with the juices of these it should be ground.
Three or four <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus seeds) doses should be employed in all diseases;

children.text: rogoktamanupānaṃ vā kavoṣṇaṃ vā jalaṃ pibet // RCint_8.48 //
children.translated_text: the adjuvant stated for the disease should be used, or lukewarm water should be drunk. // RCint_8.48 //
<s>Trinetrarasaḥ</s> (Three-Eyed Mercury)
Mercury, sulphur, copper, and <s>sindhuvāra</s> (Vitex) juice-cooked rice —
these should be ground in sunlight, then placed inside a <s>vālukāyantra</s> (sand-bath apparatus). // RCint_8.49 //
Having sealed it in a crucible, it should be cooked for three <s>yāmas</s> (nine hours) with intense fire.
One <s>guñjā</s> dose of that [should be given] in all diseases, along with <s>parṇakhaṇḍikā</s> (betel leaf piece). // RCint_8.50 //
It should be given for the perfection of the body, and for nourishment, virility, and strength.

children.text: raso'yaṃ hematārābhyām api sidhyati kanyayā // RCint_8.51 //
children.translated_text: This mercury also accomplishes [transformation] of gold and silver, [even] by a maiden. // RCint_8.51 //
<s>Amṛtārṇavarasaḥ</s> (Ocean of Nectar Mercury)
Mercury ash four parts, iron ash eight parts,

children.text: meghabhasma ca ṣaḍbhāgaṃ śuddhagandhasya pañcakam // RCint_8.52 //
children.translated_text: <s>megha</s> (tin) ash six parts, and purified sulphur five parts. // RCint_8.52 //
All that should be saturated with <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits) decoction, with <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta) juices,
and with the juices of <s>śigru</s> (Moringa), <s>vahni</s> (Plumbago), and <s>kaṭukī</s> (Picrorhiza) — each saturated seven times separately. // RCint_8.53 //
Long pepper equal to all [the above] should be added, mixed with aged <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery);

children.text: niṣkamātraṃ sadā khādejjarāṃ mṛtyuṃ nihantyalam // RCint_8.54 //
children.translated_text: one should always consume a <s>niṣka</s>-measure dose — it indeed destroys old age and death. // RCint_8.54 //
One attains the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s> in four months; this mercury is [called] <s>Amṛtārṇava</s> (Ocean of Nectar).
Sesame and <s>kauraṇṭa</s> leaves should be eaten afterwards with jaggery. // RCint_8.55 //
<s>Ratneśvararasaḥ</s> (Lord of Gems Mercury)
Silver equal to half the mercury should be combined with copper;
it should be killed in a sand-bath apparatus with <s>śilā</s> (realgar), <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar), and sulphur. // RCint_8.56 //
This is <s>Ratneśvara</s> (Lord of Gems) mercury; it is employed everywhere.
When introduced within gold, it indeed attains the nature of gold. // RCint_8.57 //
The remainder, if with <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) or sulphur, or with <s>kunaṭī</s> (alum) or <s>vāhata</s> elephants [dung],

children.text: śodhayet kanakaṃ samyag anyair vā kālikāpahaiḥ /
children.translated_text: one should properly purify the gold with other impurity-removing [substances];
in case of color diminishment, the best color should be produced using <s>tāpya</s> (pyrites). // RCint_8.58 //
<s>Durnāmāri</s> (Destroyer of Hemorrhoids)
Having bowed to <s>Śaṅkara</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, the staff-bearing <s>Maheśvara</s>,
<s>Nārada</s>, seeking longevity and health, asked <s>Īśvara</s>: // RCint_8.59 //
"By easy means, O Lord, without instruments, alkalis, or fire,

children.text: durbalānāṃ ca bhīrūṇāṃ cikitsāṃ vaktumarhasi // RCint_8.60 //
children.translated_text: please describe the treatment for the weak and the timid." // RCint_8.60 //
Hearing that disciple's words, desiring the welfare of the people,

children.text: arśasāṃ nāśanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bhaiṣajyam idam īritam // RCint_8.61 //
children.translated_text: [the Lord] proclaimed this best medicine for the destruction of hemorrhoids (<s>arśas</s>): // RCint_8.61 //
Taking any one auspicious metal from among <s>pāṇḍu</s> (pale), <s>vajra</s> (hard), and other iron types,

children.text: kṛtvā nirmalam ādau tu kunaṭyā mākṣikeṇa ca // RCint_8.62 //
children.translated_text: first making it pure with <s>kunaṭī</s> (alum) and <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrites), // RCint_8.62 //
then burning it with the paste and juice of <s>pattūra</s> (Caesalpinia) root;
placing it in fire and blowing it properly with <s>śālā</s> (Sal tree) charcoal. // RCint_8.63 //

children.text: jvālā ca tasya roddhavyā triphalāyā rasena ca /
children.translated_text: Its flame should be restrained with the juice of <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits);

children.text: tato vijñāya galitaṃ śaṅkunordhvaṃ samutkṣipet // RCint_8.64 //
children.translated_text: then, recognizing that it has melted, one should lift the spike upward. // RCint_8.64 //

children.text: triphalāyā rase pūte tadākṛṣya tu nirvapet /
children.translated_text: Having extracted it in purified <s>triphalā</s> juice, one should quench it.

children.text: na samyaggalitaṃ yattu tenaiva vidhinā punaḥ // RCint_8.65 //
children.translated_text: That which has not melted properly — by that same method again, // RCint_8.65 //
having blown, one should quench the iron in that <s>triphalā</s> juice.

children.text: yallauhaṃ na mṛtaṃ tatra pācyaṃ bhūyo'pi pūrvavat // RCint_8.66 //
children.translated_text: Iron that has not been killed there should be cooked again as before. // RCint_8.66 //

children.text: māraṇānna mṛtaṃ yacca tat tyaktavyam alauhavat /
children.translated_text: That which is not killed even by [repeated] killing should be discarded as non-iron.
Then, having properly dried it, one should powder it in an iron vessel. // RCint_8.67 //
It should be ground in an iron mortar and finely powdered on a grinding stone.

children.text: kṛtvā lohamaye pātre sārdre vā liptarandhake // RCint_8.68 //
children.translated_text: Placing it in an iron vessel, or in a moist sealed pot, // RCint_8.68 //
making it mud-like with juices, one should cook it over cow-dung fire.
Heatings (<s>puṭa</s>) should be given successively, each separately according to the prescribed method: // RCint_8.69 //
the wise one [uses] <s>triphalā</s>, fresh ginger, <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta),
<s>keśarāja</s> (Eclipta), <s>mānakanda</s>, <s>bhallāta</s> (marking nut), <s>vahni</s> (Plumbago), and <s>sūraṇa</s> (elephant yam); // RCint_8.70 //
also <s>hastikarṇa</s> (castor) leaf, <s>palāśa</s> (Butea), and <s>kuliśa</s> likewise —

children.text: puṭe puṭe cūrṇayitvā lohātṣoḍaśikaṃ palam // RCint_8.71 //
children.translated_text: powdering at each heating, sixteen <s>palas</s> of iron. // RCint_8.71 //
That measure of <s>triphalā</s> should be taken with one <s>pala</s> extra.

children.text: aṣṭabhāgāvaśiṣṭe tu rase tasyāḥ paced budhaḥ // RCint_8.72 //
children.translated_text: The wise one should cook in the decoction of that reduced to one-eighth. // RCint_8.72 //

children.text: aṣṭau palāni dattvā tu sarpiṣo lohabhājane /
children.translated_text: Having added eight <s>palas</s> of ghee in an iron vessel,

children.text: tāmre vā lohadarvyā tu cālayed vidhipūrvakam // RCint_8.73 //
children.translated_text: in a copper one, it should be stirred with an iron ladle according to proper method. // RCint_8.73 //

children.text: tataḥ pākavidhānajñaḥ svacche cordhve ca sarpiṣi /
children.translated_text: Then the one skilled in cooking methods, when the ghee is clear and risen to the top,
should take the cooking [off the fire] at the appropriate stage — soft, medium, etc. // RCint_8.74 //
One should begin according to the prescribed method, having performed auspicious rites;

children.text: ghṛtabhrāmarasaṃyuktaṃ lihed ā raktikaṃ kramāt // RCint_8.75 //
children.translated_text: one should lick [the medicine] combined with ghee and honey, gradually up to one <s>raktikā</s> dose. // RCint_8.75 //
Cow's milk is considered the best increasing adjuvant;
in the absence of cow's [milk], goat's [milk], with unctuous and aphrodisiac diet. // RCint_8.76 //

children.text: sadyo vahṇikaraṃ caiva bhasmakaṃ ca niyacchati /
children.translated_text: It immediately kindles the digestive fire and controls <s>bhasmaka</s> (excessive digestion);

children.text: hanti vātaṃ tathā pittaṃ kuṣṭhāni viṣamajvaram // RCint_8.77 //
children.translated_text: it destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), skin diseases, and irregular fever. // RCint_8.77 //
Abdominal tumors, eye diseases, anemia, drowsiness, laziness, loss of appetite,
<s>pariṇāma</s>-born colic, urinary disorders, and <s>apabāhuka</s> (arm paralysis); // RCint_8.78 //
swelling, bleeding, and especially hemorrhoids (<s>durnāman</s>);

children.text: balakṛd bṛṃhaṇaṃ caiva kāntidaṃ svaravardhanam // RCint_8.79 //
children.translated_text: it produces strength, is nourishing, gives radiance, and improves the voice. // RCint_8.79 //
It produces lightness of body, health, and increases nourishment;

children.text: āyuṣyaṃ śrīkaraṃ caiva vayastejaskaraṃ tathā // RCint_8.80 //
children.translated_text: it promotes longevity, brings prosperity, and enhances youth and vitality. // RCint_8.80 //
It produces handsome and prosperous sons, and destroys wrinkles and grey hair.

children.text: durnāmārir ayaṃ nāmnā dṛṣṭo vārān sahasraśaḥ /
children.translated_text: This [preparation], named <s>Durnāmāri</s> (Destroyer of Hemorrhoids), has been seen [effective] thousands of times;

children.text: nirmūlaṃ dahyate śīghraṃ yathā tūlaṃ ca vahṇinā // RCint_8.81 //
children.translated_text: it quickly burns [hemorrhoids] from the root, just as fire [burns] cotton. // RCint_8.81 //
For those with delicate constitutions and small bodies, the practice of taking wine should be adopted;

children.text: jīrṇamadyāni yuktāni bhojanaiḥ saha pāyayet // RCint_8.82 //
children.translated_text: well-matured wines, properly combined, should be given along with food. // RCint_8.82 //
<s>Lāva</s> (quail), <s>tittiri</s> (partridge), <s>vartīra</s> (bush quail), peacock, rabbit, and such;
<s>caṭaka</s> (sparrow), <s>kalaviṅka</s> (Indian robin), <s>vartaka</s> (quail), and <s>haritālaka</s> (green pigeon); // RCint_8.83 //
<s>śyenaka</s> (hawk), large <s>lāva</s> (quail), wild <s>viṣkira</s> (gallinaceous) birds, and others;
also the flesh of pigeons, deer, and other <s>jāṅgala</s> (arid-land) animals. // RCint_8.84 //
<s>Madgura</s> (catfish), <s>rohita</s> (rohu), and especially <s>śakula</s> (shad) are the best;

children.text: matsyarājā ime proktā hitamatsyeṣu yojayet // RCint_8.85 //
children.translated_text: these are declared kings among fish — one should employ them among beneficial fish. // RCint_8.85 //
Eggplant fruit is recommended, also <s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd) and <s>bṛhatī</s> (Solanum) fruit;
<s>pralamba</s>, <s>abhīru</s> (Asparagus), <s>vetrāgra</s> (cane tip), <s>jātuka</s>, and <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s> (Amaranthus); // RCint_8.86 //
<s>vāstuka</s> (lamb's quarters), <s>dhānyaśāka</s> (coriander greens), <s>karṇāluka</s> and <s>punarnavā</s> (Boerhavia);

children.text: nārikelaṃ ca kharjūraṃ dāḍimaṃ lavalīphalam // RCint_8.87 //
children.translated_text: coconut, dates, pomegranate, and <s>lavalī</s> fruit; // RCint_8.87 //

children.text: śṛṅgāṭakaṃ ca pakvāmraṃ drākṣā tālaphalāni ca /
children.translated_text: <s>śṛṅgāṭaka</s> (water chestnut), ripe mango, grapes, and <s>tāla</s> (palm) fruits;
<s>jātīkoṣa</s> (nutmeg), clove, <s>pūga</s> (betel nut), and betel leaf —
these are the beneficial items for those consuming this iron [preparation]. // RCint_8.88 //
One should not eat <s>lakuca</s> (breadfruit), <s>kola</s> (jujube), <s>karkandhu</s> (wild jujube), and <s>badara</s> (Indian jujube);
nor <s>jambīra</s> (citron), <s>bījapūra</s> (citrus), <s>tintiḍīka</s> (tamarind), and <s>āmardaka</s> (unripe mango); // RCint_8.89 //
nor the flesh of <s>ānūpa</s> (marshy-land) animals, <s>krakara</s> (type of bird), <s>puṇḍraka</s>, and others;
nor <s>haṃsa</s> (goose), <s>sārasa</s> (crane), <s>dātyūha</s> (gallinule), <s>cāṣa</s> (blue jay), <s>krauñca</s> (curlew), and <s>balākikā</s> (heron). // RCint_8.90 //
Also <s>māṣa</s> (black gram), <s>kanda</s> (tubers), <s>karīra</s> (caper), <s>caṇaka</s> (chickpea), and <s>kaliṅgaka</s> (watermelon);

children.text: kūṣmāṇḍakaṃ ca karkoṭīṃ kebukaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ // RCint_8.91 //
children.translated_text: <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s> (ash gourd), <s>karkoṭī</s> (spiny gourd), and especially <s>kebuka</s> (costus); // RCint_8.91 //

children.text: kañcaṭaṃ kāravellaṃ ca kaśeruṃ karkaṭīṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>kañcaṭa</s>, <s>kāravella</s> (bitter gourd), <s>kaśeru</s> (water chestnut), and <s>karkaṭī</s> (cucumber) likewise;

children.text: vidalāni ca sarvāṇi kakārādīṃśca varjayet // RCint_8.92 //
children.translated_text: all <s>vidala</s> (split pulses) and items beginning with 'ka' should be avoided. // RCint_8.92 //
This was declared by <s>Śaṅkara</s> out of compassion for <s>Yakṣarāja</s> (Kubera),
for the benefit of the world — this <s>Durnāmāri</s> (Destroyer of Hemorrhoids) is certain [in its effects]. // RCint_8.93 //
<s>Meru</s> may move from its place, the earth may be swept away by wind,
the moon and stars may fall — [but] what I have stated is not false. // RCint_8.94 //
Slayers of Brahmins, ingrates, cruel ones, and speakers of falsehood —
these should be avoided by the wise physician, as well as those who slander medicine and the teacher. // RCint_8.95 //
Iron defect removal
<s>Viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia) paste ground with aloe juice, licked with aloe juice and left long in the sun,
dissolves iron defects just as fire [melts] a lump of fresh butter. // RCint_8.96 //
<s>Kṛmiripu</s> (Viḍaṅga) powder licked with the juice of <s>Vaṅgasena</s>'s [prescribed herb],
quickly and certainly eliminates colic arising from undigested iron. // RCint_8.97 //

children.text: jīrṇe lauhe tvapatati cūrṇaṃ bhuñjīta siddhisārākhyam /
children.translated_text: When the iron is digested, if [indigestion] recurs, one should consume the powder called <s>Siddhisāra</s> (Essence of Success);
the iron ailment is destroyed and the gastric fire increases. // RCint_8.98 //
<s>Siddhisāra</s> (Essence of Success)
Equal parts separately of <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia), <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), <s>śuṇṭhī</s> (dry ginger), and <s>māgadhikā</s> (long pepper);
two parts of <s>trivṛt</s> (Operculina), saturated with lemon [juice] — this is called <s>Siddhisāra</s>. // RCint_8.99 //
Purging with the pulp of <s>āragvadha</s> (Cassia fistula) is for the removal of slag;

children.text: bhavedyadatisārastu dugdhaṃ pītvā tu taṃ jayet // RCint_8.100 //
children.translated_text: if diarrhea occurs, one should drink milk and overcome it. // RCint_8.100 //
Above twelve <s>raktikā</s> doses, the increase becomes dangerous. // RCint_8.101 //
Timely bowel evacuation, lightness in the abdomen, purity in belching,
no lethargy in the limbs, and cheerfulness of mind — [these are signs] of its proper digestion. // RCint_8.102 //
<s>Nāgārjuna</s>, the chief among sages, taught the exceedingly profound iron science;
for the remembrance of its meaning, we state this in clear words. // RCint_8.103 //

children.text: mene muniḥ svatantre yaḥ pākaṃ na palapañcakādarvāk /
children.translated_text: The sage considered in his treatise that cooking should not be less than five <s>palas</s>,
due to the defect of too many applications; nor more than thirteen <s>palas</s>. // RCint_8.104 //
In cooking iron therein, starting from five <s>palas</s> and ending at thirteen <s>palas</s>,

children.text: lauhāttriguṇā triphalā grāhyā ṣaḍbhiḥ palairadhikā // RCint_8.105 //
children.translated_text: <s>triphalā</s> should be taken three times the iron, with six <s>palas</s> extra. // RCint_8.105 //
The killings, heatings, and pan-cookings should be accomplished with one part of <s>triphalā</s>;
two parts of <s>triphalā</s> should be taken for the cooking of iron. // RCint_8.106 //
Everywhere, for the purpose of iron heating etc., for each one-part share, the number of saucers [of water],
three times per <s>pala</s>, should be taken for the decoction. // RCint_8.107 //
Starting from the seven-<s>pala</s> portion and ending at fifteen, with saucers of water,
from three to eleven — additional water should be added. // RCint_8.108 //

children.text: tatrāṣṭamo vibhāgaḥ śeṣaḥ kvāthasya yatnataḥ sthāpyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The eighth portion remaining of the decoction should be carefully preserved;
with that, the killings, heatings, and pan-cookings will be performed. // RCint_8.109 //
For the cooking purpose, with two portions of <s>triphalā</s>, the number of saucers [of water],

children.text: pratipalamambu samaṃ syādadhikaṃ dvābhyāṃ śarāvābhyām // RCint_8.110 //
children.translated_text: equal water per <s>pala</s>, with two additional saucers. // RCint_8.110 //

children.text: tatra caturtho bhāgaḥ śeṣo nipuṇaiḥ prayatnato grāhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The fourth portion remaining should be carefully taken by the skilled;

children.text: ayasaḥ pākārthatvātsa ca sarvasmāt pradhānatamaḥ // RCint_8.111 //
children.translated_text: that is the most important of all, being for the cooking of iron. // RCint_8.111 //
For cooking in a stone mortar, starting from five <s>palas</s> and ending at thirteen <s>palas</s>,
two saucers of milk, increased by one quarter [per pala]. // RCint_8.112 //
The dose starts from five <s>palas</s>; in its absence, it should be taken proportionately;
starting from four to one, and if able, more than thirteen. // RCint_8.113 //
Iron <s>prakṣepacūrṇa</s> (supplementary powder)
Powders of <s>triphalā</s>, <s>trikaṭu</s> (three pungents), <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago), <s>kānta</s> (magnetite), <s>krāmaka</s>, and <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia);
of <s>jātīphala</s> (nutmeg), <s>jātīkoṣa</s> (mace), <s>elā</s> (cardamom), <s>kaṅkola</s> (cubeb), and <s>lavaṅga</s> (clove);

children.text: sitakṛṣṇajīrakayor api cūrṇānyayasā samāni syuḥ // RCint_8.114 //
children.translated_text: also powders of white and black <s>jīraka</s> (cumin) — these should be equal to the iron. // RCint_8.114 //
<s>Triphalā</s>, <s>trikaṭu</s>, and <s>viḍaṅga</s> are fixed; the others should be understood according to the constitution.
For removing the defects of wrought iron, [one uses] <s>jātīphala</s> (nutmeg), etc., and <s>lavaṅga</s> (clove) and <s>kānta</s> (magnetite);
the addition should be proportionate to availability, with one etc. for whatever is lacking. // RCint_8.115 //
A single <s>kāntakrāmaka</s> (magnetite-krāmaka combination) removes the entire defect of iron. // RCint_8.116 //
Ghee should be taken in double, triple, or quadruple quantity according to the nature [of the substance]. // RCint_8.117 //

children.text: yadi bheṣajabhūyastvaṃ stokatvaṃ vā tathāpi cūrṇānām /
children.translated_text: If there is an excess or deficiency of medicine, then of the powders,

children.text: ayasā sāmyaṃ saṃkhyā bhūyo'lpatvena bhūyo'lpā // RCint_8.118 //
children.translated_text: the quantity equal to iron should be adjusted — more or less according to the greater or lesser amount. // RCint_8.118 //
Thus, according to the metal, by the binding of the prescribed medicine for each,
everywhere the calcination of the prescribed medicine for each should be performed. // RCint_8.119 //
<s>Lauhamāraṇam</s> (Calcination of Iron)
Now the entire procedure for the calcination of iron beginning with <s>kānta</s> (magnetite) is described.

children.text: yasya kṛte tallauhaṃ paktavyaṃ tasya śubhe divase // RCint_8.120 //
children.translated_text: The iron for which [the calcination is intended] should be cooked on an auspicious day. // RCint_8.120 //
In a ground area made level, adorned with glowing charcoal, having worshipped <s>Śiva</s>,
establishing the fire according to Vedic injunctions and offering oblations therein — // RCint_8.121 //
From <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct) everything succeeds; for the accomplishment of that <s>dharma</s>, something

children.text: śaktyanurūpaṃ dadyād dvijāya saṃtoṣiṇe guṇine // RCint_8.122 //
children.translated_text: according to one's ability should be given to a contented, virtuous <s>dvija</s> (Brahmin). // RCint_8.122 //
Having pleased the blacksmith with gifts of betel-nut, good drinks, and other favors,
first, one should make that steel pure and isolated. // RCint_8.123 //
Then, with preparations of <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), <s>girikarṇikā</s>, and bone cut with an axe,
with <s>karikarṇa</s> (Grewia) leaf-stalk, <s>śatāvarī</s> (Asparagus racemosus), and <s>keśarāja</s> (Eclipta alba) — // RCint_8.124 //
and with <s>śāli</s> (rice), <s>mūlaka</s> (radish), <s>āśīmūla</s>, rainy-season-born <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta),
having smeared [the iron], it should be heated by an experienced ironsmith. // RCint_8.125 //
Covering all around with clean charcoal from long-soaked <s>śālā</s> (Sal tree),
with wind continuously released by bellows skillfully operated — // RCint_8.126 //
The external flame of the fire should be observed; never with tongs,
but rather with a vessel of clay, salt, and water — one filled with clear water. // RCint_8.127 //
<s>Dravya</s> (Drugs): Loss of Potency by Impurities
By contact with other substances, medicines lose their own potency;
therefore, everything contaminated with dirt and dust should be discarded everywhere. // RCint_8.128 //
Metals: Method for Melting
Grasping with tongs, bringing it into the midst of blazing fire,

children.text: galati yathāyathamagre tathaiva mṛdu vardhayennipuṇaḥ // RCint_8.129 //
children.translated_text: as it melts progressively, the skilled [worker] should gradually increase [the heat] gently. // RCint_8.129 //
<s>Nirvāpaṇa</s> (Quenching): Method
Placing [the metal] upward-facing on the palm, hooked with a hook, casting it into <s>triphalā</s> water,
one should quench it completely; the remaining <s>triphalā</s> water should be preserved. // RCint_8.130 //

children.text: yallauhaṃ na mṛtaṃ tatpunarapi paktavyam uktamārgeṇa /
children.translated_text: Whatever iron is not calcined should be cooked again by the prescribed method;

children.text: yanna mṛtaṃ tathāpi tat tyaktavyam alauhameva hi yat // RCint_8.131 //
children.translated_text: that which is still not calcined should be discarded, for it is indeed not [true] iron. // RCint_8.131 //
Iron/Metals: <s>Parīkṣā</s> (Testing): Unmeltable
<s>Jāraṇā</s> (Assimilation) => <s>Kṣālana</s> (Washing)
Then, crushing in a thick iron vessel with a steel pestle,

children.text: dattvā bahuśaḥ salilaṃ prakṣālyāṅgāram uddhṛtya // RCint_8.132 //
children.translated_text: adding water repeatedly, washing, and removing the charcoal — // RCint_8.132 //
that iron alone, having dried it in fire or in sunlight, afterwards
should be ground on an iron stone or on a black stone if the former is unavailable. // RCint_8.133 //
<s>Sthālīpāka</s> (Pot-cooking Process)

children.text: atha kṛtvāyo bhāṇḍe dattvā triphalāmbu śeṣamanyadvā /
children.translated_text: Now, placing the iron in a vessel, adding <s>triphalā</s> water or other remaining [liquid],

children.text: prathamaṃ sthālīpākaṃ dadyād ā tatkṣayāt tadanu // RCint_8.134 //
children.translated_text: one should first give a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (pot-cooking) until that [liquid] is exhausted; then — // RCint_8.134 //
with the juices of <s>gajakarṇa</s> (Cassia alata) leaf-stalk, <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta), and <s>keśarāja</s>,
one should perform <s>sthālīpāka</s> as before, with each separately or combined. // RCint_8.135 //
<s>Puṭapāka</s> (Sealed Heating Process)
Making a pit with an opening the size of a hand, one hand-depth deep, even in the middle,

children.text: kṛtvā kaṭāhasadṛśaṃ tatra karīṣaṃ tuṣaṃ ca kāṣṭhaṃ ca // RCint_8.136 //
children.translated_text: shaped like a bowl — there, cow-dung cakes, husks, and wood [should be placed]. // RCint_8.136 //
Filling the inner half densely and the [outer] half loosely, setting fire to it,
afterwards one should make the iron powder smooth like mud. // RCint_8.137 //
With the juices of <s>triphalā</s> water, <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta), <s>keśara</s>, <s>śatāvarī</s> root, <s>māṇa</s>, and natural [juices],
with the juices of <s>bhallātaka</s> (marking nut), <s>karikarṇa</s> (Grewia) leaf-stalk, <s>punarnava</s> (Boerhavia) — // RCint_8.138 //
Placing then in an iron vessel — or in an earthen one — with two [vessels] of iron or earthen [material],
covering with the back [of the second vessel], sealing the opening at the edges — // RCint_8.139 //
that sealed vessel should be placed in the pit-fire; then with more
wood, cow-dung cakes, and husks, covering it, the wise one should heat it day and night. // RCint_8.140 //
Thus, with nine [substances] — <s>amī</s> and <s>meṣajarāja</s> — one should perform the sealed heating,
each one separately or combined, three, four times. // RCint_8.141 //
<s>Puṭapāka</s>: Grinding after Each [Cycle]

children.text: prati puṭanaṃ tatpiṃṣyāt sthālīpākaṃ vidhāya tathaiva tat /
children.translated_text: After each sealing, one should grind it, performing <s>sthālīpāka</s> likewise;

children.text: tādṛśi dṛṣadi na piṃṣyād vigaladrajasā tu yujyate yatra // RCint_8.142 //
children.translated_text: one should not grind on such a stone from which particles fall off, but [use one] where [it stays]. // RCint_8.142 //
That iron powder, ground, rubbed, [passed through] thick fine cloth, smooth —

children.text: yadi rajasā sadṛśaṃ syātketakyāstarhi tadbhadram // RCint_8.143 //
children.translated_text: if it becomes like the pollen of <s>ketakī</s> (Pandanus), then it is excellent. // RCint_8.143 //
In sealed heating and pot-cooking, from understanding the natural constitution of the appointed person,

children.text: kathitamapi heyam auṣadham ucitam upādeyam anyad api // RCint_8.144 //
children.translated_text: even the prescribed medicine should be abandoned [if unsuitable], and a suitable one adopted, even if not prescribed. // RCint_8.144 //
Imperceptible to those with hair-tip-sharp intelligence trained in practical procedures,
we now describe the cooking of iron as taught by <s>Nāgārjuna</s>. // RCint_8.145 //
In a strong clay-coated bowl made of ironmonger's copper alloy, having bowed to <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: tadayaḥ pacedacapalaḥ kāṣṭhendhanena vahṇinā mṛdunā // RCint_8.146 //
children.translated_text: one should cook that iron steadily with wood-fuel and gentle fire. // RCint_8.146 //
<s>Lauhapāka</s> (Cooking/Melting of Iron)

children.text: nikṣipya triphalājalam uditaṃ yattad ghṛtaṃ ca dugdhaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Adding the prescribed <s>triphalā</s> water, ghee, and milk,

children.text: saṃcālya lauhamayyā darvyā lagnaṃ samutpāṭya // RCint_8.147 //
children.translated_text: stirring with an iron ladle, scraping off what sticks — // RCint_8.147 //
<s>Pāka</s> (Cooking/Heating): Three Grades
Cooking is of three kinds here — soft, medium, and hard — which will be described:
for persons of <s>pitta</s>, <s>vāta</s>, and <s>kapha</s> constitutions [respectively]; the medium is balanced. // RCint_8.148 //
<s>Pāka</s>: Detecting the Intensity
Iron on a greased ladle that slides off easily or with difficulty — [that is] soft and medium;
that which leaves the ladle [completely] is called hard by some teachers. // RCint_8.149 //
Others say that when devoid of ladle-coating, resembling a mole-hill shape, [it is] soft;

children.text: mṛdu madhyam ardhacūrṇaṃ sikatāpuñjopamaṃ tu kharam // RCint_8.150 //
children.translated_text: medium is half-powder; and hard is like a heap of sand. // RCint_8.150 //

children.text: trividho'pi pāka īdṛk sarveṣāṃ guṇakṛdeva na tu viphalaḥ /
children.translated_text: All three types of cooking are indeed productive of good qualities, not fruitless;
in specific constitutions, the subtle merits and defects produced are but slight. // RCint_8.151 //
<s>Prakṣepa</s> (Addition of Ingredients)

children.text: vijñāya pākameva drāgavatārya kṣitau kṣaṇān kiyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having recognized the [degree of] cooking, quickly removing [from fire] and placing on the ground for some moments,

children.text: viśrāmya tatra lauhe triphalādeḥ prakṣipeccūrṇam // RCint_8.152 //
children.translated_text: resting there, one should add the powder of <s>triphalā</s> and other [ingredients] to that iron. // RCint_8.152 //
If camphor is obtainable, then when its heat has dissipated,

children.text: cūrṇīkṛtamanurūpaṃ kṣipenna vā na yadi tallābhaḥ // RCint_8.153 //
children.translated_text: the powdered [camphor] should be added in appropriate measure; or not, if it is unavailable. // RCint_8.153 //
Iron: Molten: Storage
The cooked steel, to prevent dryness from long storage without ghee,
should be stored in a milking-pail or similar vessel, in the absence of an iron vessel. // RCint_8.154 //

children.text: yadi tu pariplutihetor ghṛtam īkṣetādhikaṃ tato'nyasmin /
children.translated_text: But if one sees excess ghee due to overflow, then in another

children.text: bhāṇḍe nidhāya rakṣed bhāvyupayogo hyanena mahān // RCint_8.155 //
children.translated_text: vessel one should store and preserve it, for its future use is great. // RCint_8.155 //
Iron: <s>Snehana</s> (Oleation)
When the iron has become dry, oleation should be accomplished with <s>triphalā</s>-ghee;
this is superior in qualities to that, therefore it should be oleated with this. // RCint_8.156 //
Iron: <s>Sevana</s> (Administration)
For one of extremely <s>kapha</s>-dominant constitution, the consumption of iron is recommended with this alone;

children.text: kevalam apīdam aśitaṃ janatyayaso guṇān kiyataḥ // RCint_8.157 //
children.translated_text: even consumed alone, this generates some of iron's virtues. // RCint_8.157 //
Alternatively, taking black <s>abhra</s> (mica) powder processed by the prescribed method,
in a fraction of one-fourth, one-half, equal, double, triple, quadruple, or quintuple of the iron — // RCint_8.158 //
adding and cooking the iron as before with both, until it becomes powder,
the quantity of <s>triphalā</s> and other substances should be in proportion to that measure recalled. // RCint_8.159 //

children.text: idam āpyāyakam idam atipittanud idameva kāntibalajananam /
children.translated_text: This is nourishing, this is exceedingly bile-removing, this itself generates radiance and strength;

children.text: stabhnāti tṛṭkṣudhau param adhikādhikamātrayā kṣiptam // RCint_8.160 //
children.translated_text: it arrests thirst and hunger; added in progressively greater doses, [the effect is] greater. // RCint_8.160 //
<s>Abhra</s> (Mica): <s>Śodhana</s> (Purification): <s>Niścandrikā</s> (Without Lustre)
Making black <s>abhra</s> frog-shaped, called <s>vajra</s> (diamond), into single sheets,
one should powder it with a pestle in a wooden mortar. // RCint_8.161 //

children.text: bhūyo dṛṣadi ca piṣṭaṃ vāsaḥ sūkṣmāvakāśatalagalitam /
children.translated_text: Further ground on a stone, [passed through] cloth with fine openings,
it should be placed for three days in abundant juice of <s>maṇḍūkaparṇikā</s> (Centella asiatica). // RCint_8.162 //
Extracting it from that juice, one should then grind with winter-season rice-grain
in walnut-size [portions] with very sour, clear water, with effort. // RCint_8.163 //
Rubbing should be done with the same earlier juice of <s>maṇḍūkaparṇikā</s>;
pot-cooking and sealed heating also with the earlier [substances] like <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> and others. // RCint_8.164 //
Making a ball, placing it among leaves of <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) and others, in bellows-fire,
one should heat it until a blue flame is seen for a long time. // RCint_8.165 //

children.text: nirvāpayecca dugdhe dugdhaṃ prakṣālya vāriṇā tadanu /
children.translated_text: One should quench it in milk, wash the milk with water, then

children.text: piṣṭvā ghṛṣṭvā gālya vastre cūrṇaṃ niścandrakaṃ kuryāt // RCint_8.166 //
children.translated_text: grinding, rubbing, and filtering through cloth, one should make the powder free of lustre (<s>niścandrika</s>). // RCint_8.166 //
<s>Siddhalauhasevana</s> (Administration of Perfected Iron)
For the pacification of various diseases, for nourishment and radiance, having worshipped <s>Śiva</s>,
on a thoroughly pure and auspicious day, one should take that nectar called iron. // RCint_8.167 //
In the measure of ten <s>kṛṣṇala</s> (Abrus seeds), considering differences of strength and age,

children.text: idamadhikaṃ tad adhikataram iyadeva na mātṛmodakavat // RCint_8.168 //
children.translated_text: this much more, that still more — not like mother's sweets [of fixed size]. // RCint_8.168 //
In a smooth, clean iron vessel, one should rub it again with iron [pestle],

children.text: dattvā madhvanurūpaṃ tadanu ghṛtaṃ yojayed adhikam // RCint_8.169 //
children.translated_text: adding appropriate honey, then one should mix in abundant ghee. // RCint_8.169 //
So that it holds together as honey does, without separating, like mud — inseparable;

children.text: idamiha dṛṣṭopakaraṇametad adṛṣṭaṃ tu mantreṇa // RCint_8.170 //
children.translated_text: this is the visible preparation; the invisible [aspect] is through <s>mantra</s>. // RCint_8.170 //
With [a mantra ending in] <s>svāhā</s>, the rubbing is done; with [one ending in] <s>phaṭ</s>, the iron's strength is protected;
with <s>namasḥ</s>, the offering is made; the consumption of iron [is done] with [a mantra ending in] <s>hūṃ</s>. // RCint_8.171 //

children.text: oṃ amṛtodbhavāya svāhā oṃ amṛte hūṃ phaṭ /

children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ namaś caṇḍavajrapāṇaye mahāyakṣasenādhipataye suraguruvidyāmahābalāya svāhā</s>.
<s>Oṃ amṛte hūṃ</s>.
Having consumed that nectar-essence, one should drink water or milk as an after-drink;

children.text: kāntakrāmakamamalaṃ saṃcarvya rasaṃ pibed gilenna tu tat // RCint_8.172 //
children.translated_text: chewing <s>kānta</s> (magnetite) and <s>krāmaka</s> (betel), spotless, one should drink the juice but not swallow it. // RCint_8.172 //
<s>Oṃ amṛtodbhavāya svāhā</s>. <s>Oṃ amṛte hūṃ phaṭ</s>.

children.text: ācamya ca tāmbūlaṃ lābhe ghanasārasahitamupayojyam // RCint_8.173 //
children.translated_text: After rinsing the mouth, betel leaf, if available with camphor, should be used. // RCint_8.173 //
One should not sit excessively, nor talk excessively, nor stand excessively. // RCint_8.174 //
Excessive wind, cold, heat, travel, bathing, suppression of natural urges, and the like
should be abandoned, along with daytime sleep and eating at improper times. // RCint_8.175 //
<s>Vāta</s>-causing, <s>pitta</s>-causing — all pungent, sour, bitter, and astringent [foods],
those that instantly cause destruction — sexual intercourse, anger, and exertion — [should be kept] far away. // RCint_8.176 //

children.text: aśitaṃ tadayaḥ paścātpatatu na vā pāṭavaṃ chaḍu prathatām /
children.translated_text: After consuming that iron, whether it settles or not, whether vigor quickly spreads,
whether pain occurs in the new intestines, [when] the stomach rumbles — one must eat without hesitation. // RCint_8.177 //

children.text: prathamaṃ pītvā dugdhaṃ śālyannaṃ viśadasiddham aklinnam /
children.translated_text: First drinking milk, one should eat <s>śāli</s> rice food, clearly cooked, not sticky,
drenched with ghee, mostly with meats of birds. // RCint_8.178 //
Best is the meat of animals from arid lands, land-dwelling, and gallinaceous birds, also goat, deer (<s>aiṇa</s>), and such;
among other aquatic animals too, those with broad scales are superior. // RCint_8.179 //
In the absence of meat, fish — faultless, large, of good qualities — should be taken;
<s>madgura</s> (catfish), <s>rohita</s> (rohu), and <s>śakula</s> (a river fish), grilled, with dried meat, not much less. // RCint_8.180 //
<s>Śṛṅgāṭaka</s> (water chestnut) fruit, spine gourd, <s>śeruka</s>, banana fruit, palmyra, coconut, and others —

children.text: anyadapi yacca vṛṣyaṃ madhuraṃ panasādikaṃ jyāyaḥ // RCint_8.181 //
children.translated_text: and whatever else is aphrodisiac and sweet, such as jackfruit and the like, is superior. // RCint_8.181 //
<s>Kebuka</s> (Costus), palmyra, <s>karīra</s> (caper), combined with eggplant, <s>kupaṭola</s> (pointed gourd) fruit and leaves,
<s>mudga</s> (green gram), <s>masūra</s> (lentil), and sugarcane juices — these are recommended among non-meat [dishes]. // RCint_8.182 //

children.text: śākaṃ praheyamakhilaṃ stokaṃ rucaye tu vāstukaṃ dadyāt /
children.translated_text: All leafy vegetables should be avoided; only a small amount of <s>vāstuka</s> (bathua/Chenopodium) may be given for taste;
whatever is other than prescribed and prohibited should be known as belonging to the middle category. // RCint_8.183 //
Hot milk as an adjuvant generally loosens the bowels of one with constipation;
or else, water drunk from the tender fruit of the coconut [also helps]. // RCint_8.184 //

children.text: yasya na tathāpi sarati sayavakṣāraṃ jalaṃ pibetkoṣṇam /
children.translated_text: If even then it does not move, one should drink warm water mixed with <s>yavakṣāra</s> (barley alkali);
warm decoction of <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits) combined with alkali is even more effective. // RCint_8.185 //

children.text: trīṇi dināni samaṃ syādahni caturthe tu vardhayet kramaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: For three days the dose should be equal; on the fourth day, one should increase it gradually,
until it reaches eight <s>māṣas</s>; beyond that one should not increase further. // RCint_8.186 //
In the beginning, two <s>raktīs</s>; at the second increase, three <s>raktīs</s>;
five times five <s>raktīs</s>; beyond that one should increase in a regulated manner. // RCint_8.187 //
In the yearly regimen course, for as many days as the dose was first increased,
for that many [days] in the remainder of the year, one should decrease it inversely. // RCint_8.188 //
During those eight-<s>māṣa</s> [doses], in the morning one should eat three <s>māṣas</s>,

children.text: sāyaṃ ca tāvadahṇo madhye māṣadvayaṃ śeṣam // RCint_8.189 //
children.translated_text: and likewise in the evening; the remaining two <s>māṣas</s> during midday. // RCint_8.189 //
Thus, eating that ambrosia, one obtains radiance, a long-lasting body;
in merely three weeks, it destroys all diseases — what more need be said? // RCint_8.190 //

children.text: āryābhir iha navatyā saptavidhibhir yathāvad ākhyātam /
children.translated_text: With ninety <s>āryā</s> [verses] here, the seven methods have been properly described;
the practice has been elevated, free from misunderstanding, error, and doubt. // RCint_8.191 //
Having crossed the ocean of treatises composed by sages and extracting the essence therefrom,
a certain performer of the six rites composed [this] for the benefit of his kinsmen. // RCint_8.192 //
<s>Tāmrayoga</s> (Copper Preparation)

children.text: kanyātoye tāmrapatraṃ sutaptaṃ kṛtvā vārān viṃśatiṃ prakṣipettat /
children.translated_text: A well-heated copper plate in maiden's water — one should immerse it twenty times;

children.text: śuddhaṃ gandhaṃ taddvibhāgaṃ vimardya nimbūtoyaistāmrapatrāṇi liptvā // RCint_8.193 //
children.translated_text: grinding purified sulphur to half its amount, smearing the copper plates with lemon juice, // RCint_8.193 //

children.text: bhāṇḍe kṛtvā rodhayitvā tu bhāṇḍaṃ śālāgnau taṃ nikṣipet pañcarātram /
children.translated_text: placing them in a vessel and sealing the vessel, one should deposit it in a hearth fire for five nights;

children.text: śītaṃ jātaṃ bhāvayeduktatoyair yadvā nīrais traiphalair ekaghasram // RCint_8.194 //
children.translated_text: when cooled, one should saturate with the aforementioned waters, or with <s>triphalā</s> juice for one whole day. // RCint_8.194 //

children.text: madhvājyābhyāṃ peṣayitvā puṭet tacchuddhaṃ siddhaṃ jāyate dehasiddhyai /
children.translated_text: Grinding with honey and ghee, one should fire it — thus purified and perfected, it becomes effective for bodily perfection;

children.text: guñjāmātraṃ śālmalīnīrayuktaṃ madhvājyābhyāṃ sevayed vatsarārdham // RCint_8.195 //
children.translated_text: in a <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus seed) measure, combined with <s>śālmalī</s> (silk-cotton tree) juice, one should consume it with honey and ghee for half a year. // RCint_8.195 //

children.text: dugdhaṃ khaṇḍaṃ vānupānaṃ vidadhyāt sājyaṃ bhojyaṃ gauḍyam amlena yuktam /
children.translated_text: One should administer milk and sugar as adjuvant; food with ghee, jaggery combined with sour substance;

children.text: vīryaṃ puṣṭiṃ dīpanaṃ dehadārḍhyaṃ divyāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ dīrghamāyuḥ karoti // RCint_8.196 //
children.translated_text: it produces virility, nourishment, digestive fire, bodily firmness, divine sight, and long life. // RCint_8.196 //
<s>Tāmrayoga</s> (Copper Preparation, second)

children.text: rasatastāmraṃ dviguṇaṃ tāmrāt kṛṣṇābhrakaṃ tathā dviguṇam /
children.translated_text: Copper is double the mercury; from the copper, black <s>abhraka</s> (mica) is likewise double;
purification of each is separate; for copper, the purification is then twofold. // RCint_8.197 //
The killing [calcination] of the foil-form [copper] is either by sulphur method or by salts;
when smeared and blown copper is immersed in <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex) paste and sour gruel, // RCint_8.198 //
what becomes red-ochre colored — that, ground with half its weight of sulphur,

children.text: puṭapākena viśuddhaṃ śuddhaṃ syādabhrakaṃ tu punaḥ // RCint_8.199 //
children.translated_text: is purified by sealed heating; and the <s>abhraka</s> (mica) should again be purified. // RCint_8.199 //
Placed in a ball of <s>hilamoci</s> root, then in a smeared <s>mārda</s> (earthen) crucible,

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ dagdhaṃ piṣṭam amlāmbhasā sādhu candrikāvirahitam // RCint_8.200 //
children.translated_text: heated intensely, ground with sour water thoroughly, [until] free of lustrous particles. // RCint_8.200 //

children.text: recitatāmreṇa rasaḥ khalvaśilāyāṃ ghṛṣṭaḥ piṇḍikā kāryā /
children.translated_text: Mercury with the described copper, ground on a stone mortar, should be made into a pellet;
sweating it with household water, purified repeatedly in <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex) paste. // RCint_8.201 //
This perfected triad, each separately combined with half the powdered copper,
with <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper), <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia), and black pepper, finely ground — two to three <s>māṣas</s> should be consumed. // RCint_8.202 //
In <s>śūla</s> (colic), acid-bile disorders, swelling, <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption), consumption, and abdominal diseases,
this is a great <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative); the regimen here is without exception obligatory. // RCint_8.203 //
<s>Lakṣmīvilāsarasa</s> (Lakṣmī's Delight Mercury)
One <s>pala</s> of black <s>abhraka</s> (mica) powder, half of that [amount] of mercury and sulphur,

children.text: karpūrasya tadarddhaṃ tu jātīkoṣaphale tathā // RCint_8.204 //
children.translated_text: half of that of camphor, and <s>jātī</s> (nutmeg) and <s>koṣa</s> (mace) fruits likewise. // RCint_8.204 //
<s>Vṛddhadāraka</s> (Argyreia) seeds, and seeds of <s>unmattaka</s> (Datura),
<s>Trailokyavijayā</s> (Cannabis) seeds, and <s>vidārī</s> (Pueraria) tuber also; // RCint_8.205 //
<s>Nārāyaṇī</s>, and <s>Nāgabalā</s> (Grewia), and <s>Atibalā</s> (Abutilon) likewise,

children.text: bījaṃ gokṣurakasyāpi haijjalaṃ bījameva ca // RCint_8.206 //
children.translated_text: seeds of <s>gokṣura</s> (Tribulus) also, and <s>haijjala</s> seeds as well. // RCint_8.206 //

children.text: eteṣāṃ kārṣikaṃ cūrṇaṃ gṛhītvā vāriṇā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Taking one <s>karṣa</s> measure of powder of each of these, again with water,
grinding them, pills should be made in the measure of three <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus seed) fruits. // RCint_8.207 //
It destroys terrible and extremely fierce diseases arising from <s>sannipāta</s> (tri-doṣa derangement),

children.text: vātotthān paittikāṃścāpi nāstyatra niyamaḥ kvacit // RCint_8.208 //
children.translated_text: those arising from <s>vāta</s> and from <s>pitta</s> as well — there is no restriction whatsoever. // RCint_8.208 //
Eighteen types of <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), twenty types of <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorders),
<s>nāḍīvraṇa</s> (sinus ulcer), severe wounds, rectal diseases, and <s>bhagandara</s> (fistula), // RCint_8.209 //
<s>ślīpada</s> (elephantiasis) arising from <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, chronic and hereditary,
goiter, hernia, and extremely severe diarrhea, // RCint_8.210 //
cough, cold, consumption, hemorrhoids, obesity, and weakness,
<s>āmavāta</s> (rheumatism) of all types, tongue paralysis, and throat obstruction, // RCint_8.211 //
abdominal [diseases], deformities of the ears, nose, eyes, and face,
all colics, headache, and the destroyer of women's diseases — // RCint_8.212 //
one should eat one pill each morning regularly, according to one's strength;

children.text: anupānamidaṃ proktaṃ māṃsaṃ piṣṭaṃ payo dadhi // RCint_8.213 //
children.translated_text: the adjuvant prescribed for this is meat, flour, milk, and yogurt. // RCint_8.213 //
Through the use of water, buttermilk, liquor, and wine, one assumes any form at will;

children.text: vṛddho'pi taruṇaspardhī na ca śukrasya saṃkṣayaḥ // RCint_8.214 //
children.translated_text: even an old man rivals the young, and there is no depletion of semen. // RCint_8.214 //

children.text: na ca liṅgasya śaithilyaṃ na keśā yānti pakvatām /
children.translated_text: There is no laxity of the male organ, nor do the hairs turn grey;
one can approach a hundred women daily, with the vigor of a rutting elephant. // RCint_8.215 //
Vision extending two hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> is attained; it is supremely nourishing;
this king of preparations was proclaimed by the great-souled <s>Nārada</s>. // RCint_8.216 //
This mercury is called <s>Lakṣmīvilāsa</s> (Lakṣmī's Delight); <s>Vāsudeva</s> is the teacher of the world;
by practice of which, the Lord became the beloved of a hundred thousand women. // RCint_8.217 //
<s>Śilājatu</s> (Mineral Pitch) — Origin
Gold and other metallic ores, heated by the sun, exude from the mountains;
the impurity that is resin-like, soft, earthy, and clear — that is <s>śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch). // RCint_8.218 //
<s>Śilājatu</s> — Medicinal Properties
<s>Śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch) is non-sour, non-astringent, pungent in post-digestive effect;
neither very hot nor very cold; its origin is from four types of ores —
from gold, from silver, from copper, from tin, and from black iron. // RCint_8.219 //
That which is sweet, slightly bitter, resembling <s>japā</s> (hibiscus) flower [in color],

children.text: kaṭurvipāke śītaśca sa suvarṇasya nisravaḥ // RCint_8.220 //
children.translated_text: pungent in post-digestive effect and cooling — that is the exudate of gold. // RCint_8.220 //
<s>Śilājatu</s> from Gold — Medicinal and Physical Properties

children.text:
<śilājatu:: from silver:: medic./phys. properties>
rūpyasya kaṭukaḥ śvetaḥ śītaḥ svādurvipacyate /
