children.translated_text: <s>Śilājatu</s> from Silver — Medicinal and Physical Properties: that from silver is pungent, white, cooling, sweet in post-digestive effect;

children.text: tāmrasya barhikaṇṭhābhas tiktoṣṇaḥ pacyate kaṭuḥ // RCint_8.221 //
children.translated_text: that from copper is peacock-neck colored, bitter, hot, and pungent in post-digestive effect. // RCint_8.221 //
<s>Śilājatu</s> from Copper — Medicinal and Physical Properties
That which resembles <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium) in appearance, is bitter and salty,

children.text: kaṭurvipāke śītaśca sarvaśreṣṭhaḥ sa cāyasaḥ // RCint_8.222 //
children.translated_text: pungent in post-digestive effect and cooling — that from iron is the best of all. // RCint_8.222 //
<s>Śilājatu</s> from Iron — Medicinal and Physical Properties
All [types] have the smell of cow's urine and are useful in all procedures;
in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative) applications, the last one (iron-type) is especially distinguished. // RCint_8.223 //
In <s>vāta</s>-<s>pitta</s>, in <s>śleṣma</s> (kapha)-<s>pitta</s>, in <s>kapha</s>, and in all three [combined],
respectively, the impurities born from gold and other ores are especially recommended. // RCint_8.224 //
<s>Śilājatu</s> — Testing
It becomes like iron slag in fire, burns without smoke in water;

children.text: tṛṇātyagre kṛtaṃ śreṣṭhamadho galati tantuvat // RCint_8.225 //
children.translated_text: that which, placed at the tip of a grass blade, sinks down like a thread, is the best. // RCint_8.225 //
<s>Śilājatu</s> — Purification
Whatever is impure should be washed with plain water;

children.text: lauhapātreṣu vidhinā ūrdhvībhūtaṃ ca saṃharet // RCint_8.226 //
children.translated_text: in iron vessels, by proper method, the risen [upper portion] should be collected. // RCint_8.226 //
Well saturated with decoctions that alleviate <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>,

children.text: vīryotkarṣaṃ paraṃ yāti sarvair ekaikaśo'pi vā // RCint_8.227 //
children.translated_text: it attains supreme potency, [whether treated] with all [decoctions] or with each separately. // RCint_8.227 //
Having deposited and extracted the essence, one should again deposit it in the juice

children.text: koṣṇe saptāhametena vidhinā tasya bhāvanāṃ // RCint_8.228 //
children.translated_text: while lukewarm, for seven days — by this method its saturation [is accomplished]. // RCint_8.228 //
<s>Śilājatu</s> — Soaking

children.text: tulyaṃ girijena jale caturguṇe bhāvanauṣadhaṃ kvāthyam /
children.translated_text: With <s>girija</s> (mineral pitch) equal [in amount], the soaking herb should be boiled in four times water;

children.text: tataḥ kvāthe ca pādāṃśe pūtoṣṇe prakṣipedgirijam /
children.translated_text: then when the decoction is reduced to a quarter, while still pure and warm, one should add the mineral pitch;

children.text: tat samarasatāṃ yātaṃ saṃśuṣkaṃ prakṣipedrase bhūyaḥ // RCint_8.229 //
children.translated_text: when it has become homogeneous and dried, one should again deposit it in the juice. // RCint_8.229 //
<s>Śilājatu</s> — Medicinal Properties
By the aforementioned method, together with powdered iron preparations,

children.text: tatpītaṃ payasā dadyād dīrghamāyuḥ sukhānvitam // RCint_8.230 //
children.translated_text: that, drunk with milk, bestows long life endowed with happiness. // RCint_8.230 //
It pacifies old age and disease, produces supreme bodily firmness,
produces intellect and memory, and is auspicious — one should employ it while on a milk diet. // RCint_8.231 //
The course is seven times seven [weeks], three [courses] and one [additional] set of seven;

children.text: nirdiṣṭas trividhas tasya paro madhyo'varastathā // RCint_8.232 //
children.translated_text: the three types prescribed are superior, middling, and inferior respectively. // RCint_8.232 //

children.text: mātrā palaṃ tvarddhapalaṃ syātkarṣaṃ tu kanīyasī // RCint_8.233 //
children.translated_text: The dose is one <s>pala</s>, or half a <s>pala</s>, or one <s>karṣa</s> as the minimum. // RCint_8.233 //
<s>Śilājatu</s> — Dosage for Medicinal Use
During <s>śilājatu</s> treatments, substances that cause burning and are heavy

children.text: varjayet sarvakālaṃ ca kulatthān parivarjayet // RCint_8.234 //
children.translated_text: should be avoided at all times, and <s>kulattha</s> (horse gram) should be completely avoided. // RCint_8.234 //
<s>Śilājatu</s> — Regulations and Diet

children.text: payāṃsi śuktāni rasāḥ sayūṣās toyaṃ samūtraṃ vividhāḥ kaṣāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Milk, fermented preparations, juices, broths, water, [water] mixed with urine, and various decoctions —

children.text: āloḍanārthaṃ girijasya śastāste te prayojyāḥ prasamīkṣya kāryam // RCint_8.235 //
children.translated_text: these are recommended for dissolving <s>girija</s> (mineral pitch); they should be employed after considering the purpose. // RCint_8.235 //
<s>Kāmeśvaramodaka</s> (Lord of Love's Confection)

children.text: samyaṅmāritamabhrakaṃ kaṭuphalaṃ kuṣṭhāśvagandhāmṛtā methī mocaraso vidārimuśalī gokṣūrakaṃ cekṣuram /
children.translated_text: Properly calcined <s>abhraka</s> (mica), <s>kaṭuphala</s> (Strychnos), <s>kuṣṭha</s> (Saussurea), <s>aśvagandhā</s> (Withania), <s>amṛtā</s> (Tinospora), <s>methī</s> (fenugreek), <s>mocarasa</s> (Salmalia resin), <s>vidārī</s> (Pueraria), <s>muśalī</s> (Curculigo), <s>gokṣūraka</s> (Tribulus), and sugarcane;

children.text: rambhākandaśatāvarī hyajamodā māṣāstilā dhānyakaṃ yaṣṭī nāgabalā balā madhurikā jātīphalaṃ saindhavam // RCint_8.236 //
children.translated_text: banana stem, <s>śatāvarī</s> (Asparagus), <s>ajamodā</s> (celery seeds), <s>māṣa</s> (black gram), sesame, coriander, licorice, <s>nāgabalā</s> (Grewia), <s>balā</s> (Sida), fennel, nutmeg, and rock salt; // RCint_8.236 //

children.text: bhārṅgīkarkaṭaśṛṅgikā trikaṭukaṃ jīradvayaṃ citrakaṃ cāturjātapunarnave gajakaṇā drākṣā śaṭhī vāsakam /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhārṅgī</s> (Clerodendrum), <s>karkaṭaśṛṅgī</s> (Pistacia), the three pungents, two types of cumin, <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago), the four aromatics, the two <s>punarnava</s> (Boerhavia), <s>gajakaṇā</s>, grapes, <s>śaṭhī</s> (Hedychium), <s>vāsaka</s> (Adhatoda);

children.text: śālmalyaṅghriphalatrikaṃ kapibhavaṃ bījaṃ samaṃ cūrṇayet cūrṇāṃśā vijayā sitā dviguṇitā madhvājyamiśraṃ tu tat // RCint_8.237 //
children.translated_text: <s>śālmalī</s> (silk-cotton) root and the three fruits, <s>kapibhava</s> (monkey fruit) — all in equal parts should be powdered; the powder portions with <s>vijayā</s> (Cannabis), double the white sugar, mixed with honey and ghee. // RCint_8.237 //

children.text: karṣārddhā guḍikātha karṣamathavā sevyā satāṃ sarvadā peyā kṣīrasitānuvīryakaraṇe stambhe'pyayaṃ kāminām /
children.translated_text: A pill of half a <s>karṣa</s> or one <s>karṣa</s> should always be taken by the virtuous; to be drunk with milk and sugar as adjuvant; even in premature ejaculation of lovers,

children.text: vāmāvaśyakaraḥ sukhātisukhadaḥ prauḍhāṅganādrāvakaḥ kṣīṇe puṣṭikaraḥ kṣayakṣayakaro nānāmayadhvaṃsakaḥ // RCint_8.238 //
children.translated_text: it subjugates women, bestows supreme delight, melts even mature women, nourishes the emaciated, destroys consumption, and demolishes various diseases. // RCint_8.238 //

It alleviates cough, asthma, and severe diarrhea, kindles weak digestive fire, removes hemorrhoids, <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption), <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorders), and dispels <s>śleṣma</s> (kapha), blood, and <s>pitta</s>;

children.text: nityānandakaro viśeṣakavitāvācāṃ vilāsodbhavaṃ dhatte sarvaguṇaṃ mahāsthiravayo dhyānāvadhāne 'pyalam // RCint_8.239 //
children.translated_text: it produces constant bliss, gives rise to eloquence and poetic excellence, bestows all virtues, supreme longevity, and suffices even for meditation and concentration. // RCint_8.239 //

children.text: abhyāsena nihanti mṛtyupalitaṃ kāmeśvaro vatsarāt sarveṣāṃ hitakāriṇā nigaditaḥ śrīnityanāthena saḥ /
children.translated_text: By regular practice, <s>Kāmeśvara</s> (Lord of Love) [confection] destroys death and grey hair within a year; it was proclaimed by <s>Śrī Nityanātha</s>, the benefactor of all.

children.text: vṛddhānām api kāmavardhanakaraḥ prauḍhāṅganāsaṅgame siddho'yaṃ mama dṛṣṭipratyayakaro bhūpaiḥ sadā sevyatām // RCint_8.240 //
children.translated_text: It increases desire even in the aged, proven effective in union with mature women; this [preparation], producing conviction before my very eyes, should always be employed by kings. // RCint_8.240 //
<s>Cūrṇaratna</s> (Jewel Powder)

children.text: vṛṣyagaṇacūrṇatulyaṃ tat puṭapakvaṃ ghanaṃ sitā dviguṇam /
children.translated_text: Equal to the aphrodisiac group powder, that [mixture] baked in a sealed crucible, dense, with double the sugar;
more aphrodisiac than aphrodisiacs, a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative) — this is the <s>Cūrṇaratna</s> (Jewel Powder). // RCint_8.241 //
<s>Śṛṅgārābhrarasa</s> (Amorous Mica Mercury)
Purified black <s>abhra</s> (mica) powder, two <s>palas</s> in measure, one <s>śāṇa</s> measure of each of the following:

children.text: karpūraṃ jātikoṣaṃ sajalamibhakaṇā tejapatraṃ lavaṅgam // RCint_8.242 //
children.translated_text: <s>karpūra</s> (camphor), <s>jātikoṣa</s> (nutmeg mace), <s>ibhakaṇā</s> (Scindapsus) with water, <s>tejapatrā</s> (cinnamon leaf), <s>lavaṅga</s> (clove), // RCint_8.242 //

children.text: māṃsī tālīśacoce gajakusumagadaṃ dhātakī ceti tulyaṃ /
children.translated_text: <s>māṃsī</s> (spikenard), <s>tālīśa</s> (Abies) and <s>coca</s> (Piper cubeba), <s>gajakusuma</s> (Mesua), <s>gadā</s> (mace), <s>dhātakī</s> (Woodfordia) — all in equal measure;

children.text: pathyā dhātrī vibhītaṃ trikaṭuratha pṛthak tvarddhaśāṇaṃ dviśāṇam // RCint_8.243 //
children.translated_text: <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula), <s>dhātrī</s> (Emblica), <s>vibhīta</s> (Terminalia bellirica), <s>trikaṭu</s> (three pungents), and separately half a <s>śāṇa</s> each, two <s>śāṇas</s> [of the following]: // RCint_8.243 //

children.text: elājātīphalākhyaṃ kṣititalavidhinā śuddhagandhāśmakolaṃ kolārddhaṃ pāradasya pratipadavihitaṃ piṣṭamekatra miśram /
children.translated_text: <s>elā</s> (cardamom) and <s>jātīphala</s> (nutmeg), purified <s>gandhāśma</s> (sulphur) by the earth-method, half a <s>kola</s> of mercury, prepared at each step, ground and mixed together;

children.text: pānīyenaiva kāryāḥ pariṇatacaṇakasvinnatulyāśca vaṭyaḥ prātaḥ khādyāś catasras tadanu ca hi kiyacchṛṅgaveraṃ saparṇam // RCint_8.244 //
children.translated_text: pills equal to mature soaked chickpeas should be made with water alone; four should be eaten in the morning, and after that some fresh ginger with its leaf. // RCint_8.244 //

children.text: pānīyaṃ pītamante dhruvamapaharati kṣiprametān vikārān koṣṭhe duṣṭāgnijātān jvaramudararujo rājayakṣmaṃ kṣayaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Water drunk afterwards certainly removes quickly these disorders: those arising from corrupted digestive fire in the abdomen — fever, stomach ailments, <s>rājayakṣma</s> (consumption), and wasting;

children.text: kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ saśothaṃ nayanaparibhavaṃ mehamedovikārān chardiṃ śūlāmlapittaṃ tṛṣamapi mahatīṃ gulmajālaṃ viśālam // RCint_8.245 //
children.translated_text: cough, asthma with swelling, eye afflictions, urinary disorders and fat-related diseases, vomiting, <s>śūla</s> (colic), acid bile, great thirst, and the extensive network of abdominal tumors. // RCint_8.245 //

children.text: pāṇḍutvaṃ raktapittaṃ garalabhavagadān pīnasaṃ plīharogaṃ hanyād āmānilotthān kaphapavanakṛtān pittarogānaśeṣān /
children.translated_text: Anemia, <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders), diseases caused by poison, catarrh, splenic disease — it destroys diseases arising from <s>āma</s> (undigested matter) and wind, and all <s>pitta</s> diseases caused by <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>;

children.text: balyo vṛṣyaśca yogastaruṇatarakaraḥ sarvaroge praśastaḥ pathyaṃ māṃsaiśca yūṣair ghṛtaparilulitair gavyadugdhaiśca bhūyaḥ // RCint_8.246 //
children.translated_text: the formulation is strengthening and aphrodisiac, producing youthfulness, excellent in all diseases; the diet should be with meats and broths mixed with ghee, and further with cow's milk. // RCint_8.246 //

children.text: bhojyaṃ yojyaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ lalitalalanayā dīyamānaṃ mudā yacchṛṅgārābhreṇa kāmī yuvatijanaśatāṃ bhogayogādatuṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: Food may be taken as desired, given joyfully by a graceful woman; the lover, unsatisfied even by the sexual enjoyment of a hundred young women through <s>Śṛṅgārābhra</s>;

children.text: varjyaṃ śākāmlamādau dinakatipayacit svecchayā bhojyamanyad dīrghāyuḥ kāmamūrtir gatavalipalito mānavo'sya prasādāt // RCint_8.247 //
children.translated_text: vegetables and sour things should be avoided at first for some days, other food may be taken at will; by its grace, a man becomes long-lived, an embodiment of desire, free from wrinkles and grey hair. // RCint_8.247 //
<s>Jayāvaṭī</s> (Victory Pill)
<s>Viṣa</s> (aconite), <s>trikaṭuka</s> (three pungents), <s>musta</s> (Cyperus), <s>haridrā</s> (turmeric), <s>nimba</s> (neem) leaves,
<s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia) as the eighth — powdered with goat's urine, equal parts of each;

children.text: caṇakābhā vaṭī kāryā syājjayā yogavāhikā // RCint_8.248 //
children.translated_text: pills the size of chickpeas should be made; this is <s>Jayā</s> (Victory), the vehicle of formulations. // RCint_8.248 //
<s>Trinetrarasaḥ</s> (Three-Eyed [Śiva's] Mercury)
First, copper killed by sulphur, then equal snake-mercury (mercury);
<s>Trinetra</s> (Three-Eyed), ground with ghee, is cooling in potency, with half the sulphur. // RCint_8.249 //
If heating is desired, one should make a <s>parpaṭī</s> (flake preparation) by grinding with equal sulphur;
this indeed produces perfection of the body and cuts through all diseases. // RCint_8.250 //
<s>Siddhayogeśvararasa</s> (Accomplished Yoga-Lord Mercury)

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ dvidhā gandhaṃ khalve ghṛṣṭvā tu kajjalīm /
children.translated_text: Purified mercury, double the sulphur — grinding in a mortar, make a <s>kajjalī</s> (black paste);

children.text: tayoḥ samaṃ kāntalauhamabhāve tasya tīkṣṇakam // RCint_8.251 //
children.translated_text: to those [add] equal <s>kāntalauha</s> (magnetite iron), or in its absence, <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (steel). // RCint_8.251 //
Mixed, O Goddess of Gods, ground with <s>kanyā</s> (aloe vera) juices
for two <s>yāmas</s> (six hours), then afterwards that ball [placed] in a copper container, // RCint_8.252 //
covered with castor leaves, it should be deposited in a grain-heap;

children.text: tridinānte samuddhṛtya piṣṭaṃ vāritaraṃ bhavet // RCint_8.253 //
children.translated_text: after three days, having extracted it, [it should be] ground until it becomes fluid. // RCint_8.253 //
<s>Kumārī</s> (aloe), <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta), <s>koraṇṭa</s> (Barleria), <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade), <s>punarnavā</s> (Boerhavia),

children.text: nīlī muṇḍī ca nirguṇḍī sahadevī śatāvarī // RCint_8.254 //
children.translated_text: <s>nīlī</s> (indigo), <s>muṇḍī</s> (Sphaeranthus), <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex), <s>sahadevī</s> (Vernonia), <s>śatāvarī</s> (Asparagus), // RCint_8.254 //
<s>amlaparṇī</s> (Oxalis), <s>gokṣuraka</s> (Tribulus), <s>kacchūmūla</s> (Mucuna root), <s>vaṭāṅkurā</s> (banyan sprouts) —

children.text: eteṣāṃ bhāvayeddrāvaiḥ saptavārān pṛthak pṛthak // RCint_8.255 //
children.translated_text: with the juices of these, one should saturate [the preparation] seven times, each separately. // RCint_8.255 //
With the decoctions of <s>tryūṣaṇa</s> (three pungents), <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), and <s>somarājī</s> (Vernonia anthelmintica);
when dried, weighed powder in equal parts — called the eleven [ingredients]. // RCint_8.256 //
<s>Varā</s> (Terminalia), <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents), <s>agni</s> (Plumbago), <s>viśvailā</s> (greater cardamom), <s>jātīphala</s> (nutmeg), <s>lavaṅga</s> (clove) —
combining [these], stirring with honey, grinding this, one should take it regularly. // RCint_8.257 //

children.text: rātrau pibed gavāṃ kṣīraṃ kṛṣṇānāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: At night one should drink the milk of cows, especially of black cows;
within a year it wards off the host of diseases, old age, and death. // RCint_8.258 //
It is the best producer of increased virility, giving pleasure of a hundred women;

children.text: tāvanna cyavate vīryaṃ yāvadamlaṃ na sevate // RCint_8.259 //
children.translated_text: virility does not diminish so long as one does not consume sour things. // RCint_8.259 //
It always kindles digestion, bestows radiance, nourishment, and satisfaction on those who use it;
this well-concealed mercury is called <s>Siddhayogeśvara</s> (Accomplished Yoga-Lord). // RCint_8.260 //
<s>Palitaghnacūrṇa</s> (Grey-Hair-Destroying Powder)
<s>Triphalā</s> (three fruits), iron powder, the root of red <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago),
dried mango seed, <s>pālāśa</s> (Butea), and small <s>dugdhikā</s> (Euphorbia); // RCint_8.261 //
taking these eight, each measured at five <s>palas</s>,
mixing them, saturated with the juice of all parts of <s>palāśa</s> (Butea); // RCint_8.262 //
then one should take three parts of <s>mahākāla</s> (Nigella) seeds
and one part of black sesame, mix them, and press out [the oil]. // RCint_8.263 //
With that oil, the powder should be made into a mass by grinding;

children.text: snigdhe bhāṇḍe tadādhāya śarāveṇa nirodhayet // RCint_8.264 //
children.translated_text: placing it in a greased vessel, one should seal it with a saucer. // RCint_8.264 //

children.text: liptvā tadāśu dhānye ca palalaughe nidhāpayet /
children.translated_text: Smearing it quickly with grain and depositing it in a heap of straw,
[after] one month, having extracted it, worshipping <s>Śiva</s> the auspicious, // RCint_8.265 //
one <s>tola</s> should be eaten in the morning, one <s>tola</s> after meals;
thus by practice for three months, it destroys grey hair without doubt;

children.text: varṣaikena jarāṃ hatvā mṛtyuṃ jayati mānavaḥ // RCint_8.266 //
children.translated_text: within one year, having conquered old age, a man conquers death. // RCint_8.266 //
<s>Kāminīmadanidhūnanarasa</s> (Mercury that Shakes the Pride of Passionate Women)
The seed of <s>kajjalī</s>-made sulphur and mercury, in equal parts with gold,
should be ground mixed with gold oil; this is <s>Kāminīmadavidhūnana</s> (Shaker of Women's Pride). // RCint_8.267 //

children.text: asya vallayugalaṃ sasitaṃ cet sevitaṃ harati mehagaṇaugham /
children.translated_text: If two pills of this, with sugar, are consumed, it removes the host of urinary diseases;

children.text: vīryadārḍhyakaraṇaṃ kamanīyaṃ drāvaṇaṃ nidhuvane vanitānām // RCint_8.268 //
children.translated_text: it produces firmness of virility, is delightful, and causes melting [of resistance] of women in lovemaking. // RCint_8.268 //
<s>Caturmukharasa</s> (Four-Faced [Brahmā's] Mercury)
Mercury, sulphur, iron, and <s>abhra</s> (mica) in equal parts, with one-quarter mercury [measure of] gold,
all thrown into the mortar, ground with <s>kanyā</s> (aloe vera) juice; // RCint_8.269 //
then ground successively with juices of <s>triphalā</s>, <s>tulasī</s> (holy basil), and <s>brāhmī</s> (Bacopa);
wrapped in castor leaves, [placed] in a grain-heap for three days. // RCint_8.270 //
Having placed and then extracted it, combined with <s>triphalā</s> and honey —
this excellent <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative) should be employed in all diseases. // RCint_8.271 //
One should consume it according to the strength of one's digestive fire; it destroys wrinkles and grey hair,
is nourishing, strengthening, life-prolonging, and causes the birth of sons. // RCint_8.272 //
Eleven types of consumption, five types of cough,
eighteen types of skin disease (<s>kuṣṭha</s>), anemia, and urinary disorders, // RCint_8.273 //

children.text: śūlaṃ śvāsaṃ ca hikkāṃ ca mandāgniṃ cāmlapittakam /
children.translated_text: <s>śūla</s> (colic), asthma, hiccup, weak digestive fire, and acid bile,

children.text: vraṇān sarvānāmavātaṃ visarpaṃ vidradhiṃ tathā // RCint_8.274 //
children.translated_text: all wounds, <s>āmavāta</s> (rheumatism), <s>visarpa</s> (erysipelas), and abscesses, // RCint_8.274 //
epilepsy, great madness, all hemorrhoids, and skin diseases —
consumed gradually it destroys [them], as <s>Indra's</s> thunderbolt [destroys] a tree;
this was instructed by the four-faced god (<s>Brahmā</s>) to <s>Kṛṣṇātreya</s>. // RCint_8.275 //
<s>Gandhalauha</s> (Sulphur-Iron)

children.text: gandhaṃ lauhaṃ bhasma madhvājyayuktaṃ sevyaṃ varṣaṃ vāriṇā traiphalena /
children.translated_text: Sulphur and iron ash, combined with honey and ghee, should be taken for a year with <s>triphalā</s> water;

children.text: śukle keśe kālimā divyadṛṣṭiḥ puṣṭivīryaṃ jāyate dīrghamāyuḥ // RCint_8.276 //
children.translated_text: grey hair becomes black, divine vision [is gained], nourishment, virility, and long life are produced. // RCint_8.276 //
<s>Siddhalakṣmīśvararasa</s> (Accomplished Lakṣmīśvara Mercury)

children.text: aṣṭāṃśahemni haraje śikhimūṣikāyāṃ saṃjārya ṣaḍguṇabaliṃ kramaśo 'dhikaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: In a <s>śikhimūṣikā</s> (peacock crucible) with one-eighth gold added to mercury, revolving with six-fold and progressively increasing sacrificial offerings,

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ payo'gnim adhare vinidhāya dhīrāḥ siddhīḥ samagramatulāḥ svakare kurudhvam // RCint_8.277 //
children.translated_text: placing milk-fire below and above, the wise ones should produce incomparable complete <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments) in their own hands. // RCint_8.277 //
<s>Vahnisiddharasa</s> (Fire-Accomplished Mercury)

children.text: lauhaṃ gandhaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ bhrāmayitvā sārdhas tasmin sūtako'nyaśca gandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having revolved iron, sulphur, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), with one and a half of that, mercury and another sulphur;

children.text: kanyāmbhobhir marditaḥ kācakūpyāṃ kṣipto vahṇau siddhaye vahṇisiddhaḥ // RCint_8.278 //
children.translated_text: ground with <s>kanyā</s> (aloe vera) water, placed in a glass flask, put in fire — for accomplishment, [this is] <s>Vahnisiddha</s> (Fire-Accomplished). // RCint_8.278 //
